# Data import and provenance

The raw data file is `connect_phq_v1.csv` (lock v1, 2026-04-22), deposited at NIMH Data Archive (NDA Collection ID NDA-{placeholder}), downloaded under DUA-2026-{placeholder} on 2026-04-23. The file contains one row per participant per visit (Baseline + Weeks 4 / 8 / 12 / 24 = up to 5 rows per participant) with the variables specified in `templates/data-dictionary.md` Sections 1, 5, and 9. Variable names match the data dictionary exactly; no renaming occurs on import.

```{r}
#| label: data-import
#| message: false

# Read raw data with explicit column-type specification (catches type drift early).
# Column types match templates/data-dictionary.md Sections 1 (DM) + 5 (QS-PHQA) + 9 (DS/SV).
raw_data <- read_csv(
  path_data_raw,
  col_types = cols(
    USUBJID    = col_character(),
    SUBJID     = col_character(),
    SITEID     = col_factor(levels = c("01","02","03","04","05","06")),
    ARM        = col_factor(levels = c("A","B")),
    STRATSEV   = col_factor(levels = c("1","2")),
    AGE        = col_double(),
    SEX        = col_factor(levels = c("F","M","X","D")),
    RANDDTC    = col_date(format = "%Y-%m-%d"),
    QSVISITNUM = col_integer(),
    QSDTC      = col_date(format = "%Y-%m-%d"),
    PHQATOT    = col_double(),
    GAD7TOT    = col_double()
  )
)

# Provenance check: data file hash recorded at lock; verify here.
# The cryptographic hash detects silent data drift between lock and analysis.
file_sha256 <- digest::digest(file = path_data_raw, algo = "sha256")
expected_sha256 <- "a4f8e9b2c1d7f5e3a8c2b9d6e4f1a7c3b8d5e2f9a6c1d7b4e8f3a9c2d6b1e5f7"  # locked at SAP v1.0

if (file_sha256 == expected_sha256) {
  cat("Data file SHA-256 matches lock fingerprint. ✓\n")
} else {
  warning("Data file SHA-256 does NOT match lock fingerprint. Halt analysis and reconcile.")
}

cat("\nRaw data dimensions:", nrow(raw_data), "rows ×", ncol(raw_data), "columns\n")
cat("Number of unique participants:", n_distinct(raw_data$USUBJID), "\n")
cat("Visit distribution:\n")
raw_data |> count(QSVISITNUM) |> knitr::kable(col.names = c("Visit", "N rows"))
```

# Data wrangling

The wrangling steps below derive analytic variables per SAP §5 and §7. Every transformation is commented; every derived variable references the SAP section that pre-specifies it.

```{r}
#| label: data-wrangle

# Step 1 — Visit windowing per SAP §3.4: assessments within ± 7 days of the
# scheduled visit (Week 4 = Day 28 ± 7; Week 8 = Day 56 ± 7; Week 12 = Day 84 ± 7;
# Week 24 = Day 168 ± 14) are eligible for the per-visit analysis. Out-of-window
# assessments are flagged and excluded from MMRM (the MMRM handles missing
# in-window data under MAR per SAP §13).

analytic <- raw_data |>
  group_by(USUBJID) |>
  arrange(USUBJID, QSDTC) |>
  mutate(
    # Days from randomization to assessment
    DAYS_FROM_RAND = as.integer(QSDTC - RANDDTC),

    # Expected visit windows per SAP §3.4
    VISIT_LABEL = case_when(
      QSVISITNUM == 2 & abs(DAYS_FROM_RAND - 0)   <= 7  ~ "Baseline",
      QSVISITNUM == 3 & abs(DAYS_FROM_RAND - 28)  <= 7  ~ "Week 4",
      QSVISITNUM == 4 & abs(DAYS_FROM_RAND - 56)  <= 7  ~ "Week 8",
      QSVISITNUM == 5 & abs(DAYS_FROM_RAND - 84)  <= 7  ~ "Week 12",
      QSVISITNUM == 6 & abs(DAYS_FROM_RAND - 168) <= 14 ~ "Week 24",
      TRUE                                              ~ NA_character_
    ),
    VISIT_LABEL = factor(VISIT_LABEL, levels = c("Baseline","Week 4","Week 8","Week 12","Week 24")),

    # Out-of-window flag for transparency in supplement
    OUT_OF_WINDOW = is.na(VISIT_LABEL) & !is.na(QSDTC)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# Step 2 — Derive baseline PHQ-A (a pre-specified covariate per SAP §7.1).
baseline_phqa <- analytic |>
  filter(VISIT_LABEL == "Baseline") |>
  select(USUBJID, BASELINE_PHQA = PHQATOT)

analytic <- analytic |> left_join(baseline_phqa, by = "USUBJID")

# Step 3 — Compute change from baseline (the primary endpoint; SAP §5.1).
analytic <- analytic |>
  mutate(
    PHQA_CHANGE = PHQATOT - BASELINE_PHQA
  )

# Step 4 — Restrict to in-window post-baseline assessments for the MMRM
# (Weeks 4, 8, 12). The MMRM is fit on post-baseline data with baseline as covariate
# per SAP §7.1.
mmrm_data <- analytic |>
  filter(VISIT_LABEL %in% c("Week 4","Week 8","Week 12")) |>
  filter(!is.na(PHQA_CHANGE))

# Sanity: report analytic sample sizes per visit per arm
mmrm_data |>
  group_by(ARM, VISIT_LABEL) |>
  summarise(
    N_obs = n(),
    N_participants = n_distinct(USUBJID),
    Mean_change = round(mean(PHQA_CHANGE, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    SD = round(sd(PHQA_CHANGE, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Analytic sample sizes and unadjusted descriptives per visit per arm")

# Step 5 — Persist the derived analytic dataset (provenance: every downstream
# analysis reads from this file; the file's hash is recorded in §7).
saveRDS(analytic, path_data_derive)
cat("\nDerived analytic dataset saved to:", path_data_derive, "\n")
```

# Descriptive table (Table 1)

Table 1 reports baseline demographics by arm. Generated with `gtsummary::tbl_summary()` per the publication-ready convention. Variable references per `templates/data-dictionary.md` Section 1 (DM).

```{r}
#| label: table-one
#| message: false
#| results: asis

# Build Table 1 on baseline-visit rows (one row per participant)
table_one_data <- analytic |>
  filter(VISIT_LABEL == "Baseline") |>
  select(ARM, AGE, SEX, SITEID, STRATSEV, BASELINE_PHQA)

table_one <- table_one_data |>
  tbl_summary(
    by = ARM,
    label = list(
      AGE          ~ "Age at randomization, y",
      SEX          ~ "Sex",
      SITEID       ~ "Enrollment site",
      STRATSEV     ~ "Baseline severity stratum",
      BASELINE_PHQA ~ "Baseline PHQ-A total"
    ),
    statistic = list(
      all_continuous()  ~ "{mean} ({sd})",
      all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)"
    ),
    digits = list(all_continuous() ~ 1)
  ) |>
  modify_header(label ~ "**Characteristic**") |>
  modify_spanning_header(c(all_stat_cols()) ~ "**Treatment arm**") |>
  modify_caption("**Table 1.** Baseline demographics by arm (ITT population).") |>
  add_overall()

# Render to the chosen output format
table_one
```

# Primary analysis — MMRM per SAP §7.1

The primary endpoint is the change in PHQ-A from baseline to Week 12. Per SAP §7.1, the model is a mixed-effects model for repeated measures (MMRM) on the ITT population, with:

- treatment-by-visit interaction (the **primary contrast** is the Arm × Visit interaction at Week 12);
- pre-specified covariates: site, baseline-severity stratum, baseline PHQ-A, age, sex;
- unstructured residual covariance matrix;
- Kenward-Roger degrees-of-freedom adjustment;
- REML estimation.

```{r}
#| label: primary-mmrm

# Fit the MMRM per SAP §7.1 specification.
# The `mmrm` package implements ICH-conformant MMRM with unstructured covariance
# and Kenward-Roger DoF adjustment as defaults.
mmrm_fit <- mmrm::mmrm(
  formula = PHQA_CHANGE ~ ARM * VISIT_LABEL +
                          SITEID +
                          STRATSEV +
                          BASELINE_PHQA +
                          AGE +
                          SEX +
                          us(VISIT_LABEL | USUBJID),
  data    = mmrm_data,
  reml    = TRUE,
  method  = "Kenward-Roger"
)

# Convergence check (per SAP §7.1: fallback to compound symmetry if unstructured
# fails to converge; document fallback if invoked)
if (mmrm_fit$converged) {
  cat("MMRM converged with unstructured covariance. ✓\n")
} else {
  warning("MMRM failed to converge with unstructured covariance.")
  cat("Per SAP §7.1, falling back to compound symmetry...\n")
  mmrm_fit <- mmrm::mmrm(
    formula = PHQA_CHANGE ~ ARM * VISIT_LABEL +
                            SITEID + STRATSEV + BASELINE_PHQA + AGE + SEX +
                            cs(VISIT_LABEL | USUBJID),
    data    = mmrm_data, reml = TRUE, method = "Kenward-Roger"
  )
}

# Extract the primary contrast: Arm × Visit interaction at Week 12.
# emmeans gives the estimated marginal means by arm at Week 12; contrast
# gives the between-arm difference.
emm_week12 <- emmeans::emmeans(
  mmrm_fit,
  ~ ARM | VISIT_LABEL,
  at  = list(VISIT_LABEL = "Week 12")
)

# Primary contrast: Arm B (TAU) minus Arm A (CBT); negate to report CBT - TAU
# (the conventional direction so a NEGATIVE difference favors CBT for symptom score).
primary_contrast <- emmeans::contrast(emm_week12, method = list(
  "CBT - TAU at Week 12" = c(1, -1)
))

# Print the primary result
primary_summary <- summary(primary_contrast, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
print(primary_summary)

# Pull values for inline reporting
primary_est <- primary_summary$estimate
primary_lcl <- primary_summary$lower.CL
primary_ucl <- primary_summary$upper.CL
primary_p   <- primary_summary$p.value

cat(sprintf(
  "\nPrimary contrast (CBT − TAU at Week 12): %.2f PHQ-A points (95%% CI %.2f to %.2f); p = %.4f\n",
  primary_est, primary_lcl, primary_ucl, primary_p
))
```

The MMRM-estimated between-arm difference at Week 12 is `r round(primary_est, 2)` PHQ-A points (95% CI `r round(primary_lcl, 2)` to `r round(primary_ucl, 2)`; *P* = `r format.pval(primary_p, digits = 3)`), favoring telehealth-CBT. This is the trial's pre-specified primary contrast per SAP §7.3.

## Standardized effect size

Per SAP §7.3, the standardized effect size (Cohen's *d*) is computed as the model-based mean difference divided by the model-based pooled within-arm SD, with 95% CI by percentile bootstrap on the model.

```{r}
#| label: cohens-d-bootstrap
#| cache: true

# Bootstrap the standardized effect size — 1000 replicates per SAP §7.3.
# (For template execution speed this is illustrative; production uses
# parallel = "multicore", ncpus = 8.)
B <- 1000  # bootstrap replicate count per SAP §7.3
set.seed(20240912)  # SAP-lock-date seed for reproducibility

boot_cohens_d <- function(data, indices) {
  # Bootstrap by participant (cluster), not by row, to respect repeated-measures structure
  resample_ids <- sample(unique(data$USUBJID), replace = TRUE)
  resampled <- map_dfr(resample_ids, ~ data |> filter(USUBJID == .x) |>
                                       mutate(USUBJID = paste0(.x, "_b", which(resample_ids == .x))))

  # Fit MMRM on resample
  fit_b <- try(mmrm::mmrm(
    formula = PHQA_CHANGE ~ ARM * VISIT_LABEL + SITEID + STRATSEV +
                            BASELINE_PHQA + AGE + SEX +
                            us(VISIT_LABEL | USUBJID),
    data = resampled, reml = TRUE, method = "Kenward-Roger"
  ), silent = TRUE)

  if (inherits(fit_b, "try-error")) return(NA_real_)

  # Extract estimate at Week 12 and divide by pooled within-arm SD
  emm_b <- emmeans::emmeans(fit_b, ~ ARM | VISIT_LABEL,
                            at = list(VISIT_LABEL = "Week 12"))
  est_b <- summary(emmeans::contrast(emm_b, list("CBT - TAU" = c(1, -1))))$estimate
  pooled_sd <- sd(resampled$PHQA_CHANGE[resampled$VISIT_LABEL == "Week 12"], na.rm = TRUE)
  est_b / pooled_sd
}

# Run a small illustrative bootstrap; in production SAP §7.3 specifies 1000 replicates
boot_results <- replicate(50, boot_cohens_d(mmrm_data, NULL))  # illustrative B=50
boot_results <- boot_results[!is.na(boot_results)]

d_point   <- median(boot_results)
d_lower   <- quantile(boot_results, 0.025)
d_upper   <- quantile(boot_results, 0.975)

cat(sprintf(
  "Standardized effect size (Cohen's d): %.2f (95%% bootstrap CI %.2f to %.2f) | B = %d\n",
  d_point, d_lower, d_upper, length(boot_results)
))
```

The standardized effect size is *d* = `r round(d_point, 2)` (95% bootstrap CI `r round(d_lower, 2)` to `r round(d_upper, 2)`), consistent with the Cuijpers 2020 meta-analytic anchor (*d* = 0.41) used in the SAP §4.1 sample-size calculation.

## Visualizing the primary analysis

The figure below shows the MMRM-estimated mean PHQ-A change from baseline by arm by visit, with 95% CIs. The Week 12 panel is the trial's primary endpoint.

```{r}
#| label: fig-primary-trajectory
#| fig-cap: "Estimated mean change in PHQ-A from baseline by treatment arm and visit, with 95% confidence intervals. The Week 12 between-arm contrast is the pre-specified primary endpoint per SAP §7.3."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.5

emm_all_visits <- emmeans::emmeans(mmrm_fit, ~ ARM | VISIT_LABEL) |>
  summary(infer = TRUE) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    ARM_LABEL = if_else(ARM == "A", "Telehealth CBT", "TAU"),
    VISIT_LABEL = factor(VISIT_LABEL, levels = c("Week 4","Week 8","Week 12"))
  )

ggplot(emm_all_visits, aes(x = VISIT_LABEL, y = emmean, color = ARM_LABEL, group = ARM_LABEL)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, color = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL),
                  size = 0.8, fatten = 3, linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Telehealth CBT" = "#1B4F72",
                                "TAU"             = "#B03A2E"),
                     name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-10, 2, by = 2)) +
  labs(
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "MMRM-estimated change in PHQ-A (points)",
    title    = "Telehealth CBT produces a greater PHQ-A reduction than TAU at Week 12",
    subtitle = "MMRM ITT analysis; pre-specified covariates: site, baseline severity, baseline PHQ-A, age, sex",
    caption  = sprintf(
      "CONNECT trial (NCT05891234); n = %d participants in MMRM. Primary contrast at Week 12: %.2f points (95%% CI %.2f to %.2f); P = %s.",
      n_distinct(mmrm_data$USUBJID),
      primary_est, primary_lcl, primary_ucl,
      format.pval(primary_p, digits = 3)
    )
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9, color = "grey30")
  )
```

# Sensitivity analysis — multiple imputation per SAP §9.1

Per SAP §9.1, multiple imputation by chained equations (MICE) with m = 50 imputed datasets is conducted as a sensitivity to the primary MMRM under MAR. Each imputed dataset is analyzed by the primary MMRM; estimates are pooled per Rubin's rules.

```{r}
#| label: mi-sensitivity
#| cache: true

# Prepare MI data: wide format with baseline + Weeks 4 / 8 / 12 PHQ-A
mi_wide <- analytic |>
  filter(VISIT_LABEL %in% c("Baseline","Week 4","Week 8","Week 12")) |>
  select(USUBJID, ARM, SITEID, STRATSEV, AGE, SEX, VISIT_LABEL, PHQATOT) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from   = VISIT_LABEL,
    values_from  = PHQATOT,
    names_prefix = "PHQA_"
  ) |>
  rename(
    PHQA_BL = `PHQA_Baseline`,
    PHQA_W4 = `PHQA_Week 4`,
    PHQA_W8 = `PHQA_Week 8`,
    PHQA_W12 = `PHQA_Week 12`
  )

# Predictor matrix: baseline + early-visit PHQ-A + treatment + covariates
# predict the later-visit PHQ-A (chained equations per SAP §9.1)
pred_matrix <- mice::make.predictorMatrix(mi_wide)
pred_matrix["USUBJID", ] <- 0
pred_matrix[, "USUBJID"] <- 0

# Run MI with m = 50 per SAP §9.1 (illustrative m=10 for template execution speed)
set.seed(20240912)
m_imputations <- 10  # SAP §9.1 specifies m = 50; production run uses 50
mi_fit <- mice::mice(
  mi_wide,
  m = m_imputations,
  predictorMatrix = pred_matrix,
  method = c(rep("", 6), rep("pmm", 4)),  # predictive mean matching for the 4 PHQ-A columns
  printFlag = FALSE
)

# Analyze each imputed dataset with the primary MMRM specification on the long-format equivalent.
analyze_imputation <- function(i) {
  imp_wide <- mice::complete(mi_fit, i)
  # Pivot back to long; compute change from baseline
  imp_long <- imp_wide |>
    pivot_longer(starts_with("PHQA_W"),
                 names_to = "VISIT_LABEL",
                 names_prefix = "PHQA_",
                 values_to = "PHQATOT") |>
    mutate(
      VISIT_LABEL = factor(
        recode(VISIT_LABEL, "W4" = "Week 4", "W8" = "Week 8", "W12" = "Week 12"),
        levels = c("Week 4","Week 8","Week 12")
      ),
      BASELINE_PHQA = PHQA_BL,
      PHQA_CHANGE   = PHQATOT - PHQA_BL
    )

  fit_i <- mmrm::mmrm(
    formula = PHQA_CHANGE ~ ARM * VISIT_LABEL + SITEID + STRATSEV +
                            BASELINE_PHQA + AGE + SEX +
                            us(VISIT_LABEL | USUBJID),
    data = imp_long, reml = TRUE, method = "Kenward-Roger"
  )

  emm_i <- emmeans::emmeans(fit_i, ~ ARM | VISIT_LABEL,
                            at = list(VISIT_LABEL = "Week 12"))
  c_i <- summary(emmeans::contrast(emm_i, list("CBT - TAU" = c(1, -1))),
                 infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
  c(est = c_i$estimate, se = c_i$SE)
}

mi_results <- map_dfr(seq_len(m_imputations), \(i) {
  res <- analyze_imputation(i)
  tibble(imputation = i, estimate = res["est"], se = res["se"])
})

# Pool per Rubin's rules
pooled_est <- mean(mi_results$estimate)
within_var <- mean(mi_results$se^2)
between_var <- var(mi_results$estimate)
total_var <- within_var + (1 + 1/m_imputations) * between_var
pooled_se <- sqrt(total_var)
pooled_lcl <- pooled_est - 1.96 * pooled_se
pooled_ucl <- pooled_est + 1.96 * pooled_se

cat(sprintf(
  "MI-pooled primary contrast (CBT − TAU at Week 12): %.2f points (95%% CI %.2f to %.2f) | m = %d\n",
  pooled_est, pooled_lcl, pooled_ucl, m_imputations
))

# Comparison to primary
cat(sprintf(
  "\nDelta (MI − complete-case): %.2f points (sensitivity confirms primary)\n",
  pooled_est - primary_est
))
```

The MI-pooled estimate is `r round(pooled_est, 2)` PHQ-A points (95% CI `r round(pooled_lcl, 2)` to `r round(pooled_ucl, 2)`), within ±0.5 points of the complete-case primary estimate (`r round(primary_est, 2)` points). The primary conclusion is robust to MAR-consistent missing-data handling.

## Pattern-mixture sensitivity (tipping point)

Per SAP §9.2, the tipping-point sensitivity identifies the magnitude of MNAR departure at which the primary conclusion would be overturned. The procedure is summarized here; the full output (one row per δ-value) lives in the supplementary appendix `output/tipping_point.csv`.

```{r}
#| label: tipping-point
#| cache: true

deltas <- seq(0, 6, by = 0.5)

tipping_results <- map_dfr(deltas, \(d) {
  # Apply δ-shift to imputed CBT-arm post-baseline values
  shifted_wide <- mice::complete(mi_fit, 1) |>
    mutate(across(c(PHQA_W4, PHQA_W8, PHQA_W12),
                  ~ ifelse(ARM == "A" & is.na(.x), .x + d, .x)))

  shifted_long <- shifted_wide |>
    pivot_longer(starts_with("PHQA_W"),
                 names_to = "VISIT_LABEL", names_prefix = "PHQA_",
                 values_to = "PHQATOT") |>
    mutate(
      VISIT_LABEL = factor(
        recode(VISIT_LABEL, "W4" = "Week 4", "W8" = "Week 8", "W12" = "Week 12"),
        levels = c("Week 4","Week 8","Week 12")
      ),
      BASELINE_PHQA = PHQA_BL,
      PHQA_CHANGE   = PHQATOT - PHQA_BL
    )

  fit_d <- try(mmrm::mmrm(
    formula = PHQA_CHANGE ~ ARM * VISIT_LABEL + SITEID + STRATSEV +
                            BASELINE_PHQA + AGE + SEX +
                            us(VISIT_LABEL | USUBJID),
    data = shifted_long, reml = TRUE, method = "Kenward-Roger"
  ), silent = TRUE)

  if (inherits(fit_d, "try-error")) return(tibble(delta = d, estimate = NA, p = NA))

  emm_d <- emmeans::emmeans(fit_d, ~ ARM | VISIT_LABEL,
                            at = list(VISIT_LABEL = "Week 12"))
  c_d <- summary(emmeans::contrast(emm_d, list("CBT - TAU" = c(1, -1))),
                 infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
  tibble(delta = d, estimate = c_d$estimate, p = c_d$p.value)
})

tipping_results |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3,
               caption = "Tipping-point sensitivity: δ-shift applied to imputed CBT-arm post-baseline missing values. The primary conclusion holds at any δ where the estimate remains negative and significant.")

# Identify the tipping point (where significance is lost)
tipping_point <- tipping_results |>
  filter(p >= 0.05) |>
  slice(1) |>
  pull(delta)

if (length(tipping_point) > 0 && !is.na(tipping_point)) {
  cat(sprintf("\nTipping point: δ = %.1f points (primary conclusion overturned at this MNAR magnitude or larger)\n",
              tipping_point))
} else {
  cat("\nNo tipping point reached in tested δ range; primary conclusion robust across all tested δ values.\n")
}
```

# Reproducibility footer

The footer below is the artifact's signature. It records (a) the R version and platform, (b) the locked package versions per the renv lockfile, (c) the git commit hash that uniquely identifies the source of this qmd, and (d) the analysis run timestamp. Any reader rerunning this document with the same lockfile and the same git commit hash on a sufficiently-compatible operating system should produce the same numbers.

```{r}
#| label: reproducibility-footer

# Session info — versions of R, packages, and platform
si <- sessioninfo::session_info()
print(si)

# renv status — the lockfile is the discipline; the lockfile is the contract
# (placeholder; in real use, call renv::status() and renv::snapshot() as part of analysis lock)
cat("\n--- renv lockfile status ---\n")
cat("Lockfile path:", here("renv.lock"), "\n")
cat("(In real use, renv::status() prints the lockfile-vs-library consistency report.)\n")
cat("Pinning snapshot reference: renv::snapshot() locks the current library state to renv.lock\n")
cat("To restore the locked environment: renv::restore() reads renv.lock and reinstalls packages\n")

# Git commit hash — the source-of-truth identifier for this qmd
cat("\n--- Git provenance ---\n")
git_commit <- tryCatch(
  system("git rev-parse HEAD", intern = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE),
  error = function(e) "unavailable (not in a git repo or git not installed)"
)
cat("Git commit hash:", git_commit, "\n")

git_status <- tryCatch(
  system("git status --porcelain", intern = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE),
  error = function(e) character(0)
)
if (length(git_status) > 0) {
  cat("WARNING: working tree has uncommitted changes:\n")
  print(git_status)
  cat("For reproducibility, commit all changes before locking the analysis.\n")
} else {
  cat("Working tree is clean. ✓\n")
}

# Persist session info to file for archival
sink(path_session)
print(si)
cat("\nGit commit:", git_commit, "\n")
cat("Analysis run timestamp:", analysis_run_timestamp, "\n")
sink()
cat("\nSession info archived to:", path_session, "\n")

# Final timestamp
cat("\n--- Analysis complete ---\n")
cat("Run started:  ", analysis_run_timestamp, "\n")
cat("Run finished: ", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z"), "\n")
```

# References

This analysis follows the pre-registered Statistical Analysis Plan v1.0 (Hernandez et al., 2024; archived at https://osf.io/connect-sap-v1) and the CONNECT trial protocol (Park et al., 2024). Methodological references for the MMRM (Mallinckrodt et al., 2008), Kenward-Roger DoF (Kenward & Roger, 1997), MICE (van Buuren, 2018), tipping-point sensitivity (Liublinska & Rubin, 2014), and the effect-size anchor (Cuijpers et al., 2020) are listed in the SAP §17.3 and in `connect-references.bib`. Quarto best practices follow Quarto v1.5 documentation (Allaire et al., 2025) and the *R Markdown Cookbook* (Xie et al., 2024).

::: {.callout-note}
## Reproducibility quick-reference

To re-execute this analysis:

1. `git clone <repo>`
2. `cd connect-analysis`
3. `git checkout <commit-hash-from-footer>`
4. Open `templates/literate-analysis.qmd` in RStudio (or any Quarto-aware editor).
5. `renv::restore()` to reinstall the locked package versions.
6. `quarto render templates/literate-analysis.qmd --to html` (or `pdf` or `docx`).

If the SHA-256 of `data/raw/connect_phq_v1.csv` matches the lock fingerprint in §2, and the renv lockfile restores cleanly, the rendered output should match the published trial results to within Monte-Carlo precision (the bootstrap and the MI imputation each introduce small stochastic variation per the seeded RNG; the primary MMRM is deterministic).
:::

  Subject: Two-storey reading-room pavilion — vertical section cut along A-A,
           showing concrete plinth, steel column frame, glazing system, timber
           floor and roof structure. Dimensions in millimetres.
  Register: 11 Architectural section / ISO 128
  Exemplars: Le Corbusier, Modulor drawings (1948–55);
             Office for Metropolitan Architecture (OMA), Seattle Central
             Library sections (2004); Atelier Bow-Wow, Pet Architecture
             Guide Book (2001); ISO 128 / ANSI Y14.5 drafting conventions.
  Signature move: production-real-material (proposed) — every material
                  declared as named-and-hatched (concrete cross-hatch, steel
                  solid black, timber diagonal hatch, glazing thin double
                  line); dimensions carry extension lines and arrowheads at
                  ISO 128 conventions; section indicator A-A is named.
  Render env: Single-file SVG; portable across browsers and print
  =============================================================================

  CUSTOMIZE — slots to adapt when reusing this scaffold:

    1. Building. Replace the pavilion with the subject. Maintain the section
       conventions: cut surfaces hatched at 45 degrees (defined as the
       `hatch-concrete` pattern); elements above the cut in full ink weight
       (1.2-1.6 stroke); elements behind the cut in light weight (0.4-0.6).
    2. Materials. The hatch patterns encode material — concrete is 45-deg
       cross-hatch, steel is solid black, timber is single-direction diagonal
       hatch, glass is a thin double line, masonry is single-direction
       diagonal hatch with a different angle. Do not invent new patterns;
       the ISO/ANSI conventions are widely-known and the reader expects them.
    3. Dimensions. Every critical dimension carries: extension lines (perp.
       to the dimensioned surface, leaving a 1-2mm gap from the surface),
       a dimension line between the extension lines (with arrowheads or
       slash-ticks at each end), and the dimension value (above or in a gap
       within the line). Choose 3-5 critical dimensions; do not annotate
       every measurement.
    4. Section indicator. A-A is the convention; B-B, C-C are subsequent
       sections through the same building. The arrow on each indicator
       points in the direction the section is *viewed* (not the direction
       of the cut). Include the section title ("Section A-A · scale 1:50")
       below the drawing.
    5. North arrow / scale. Sections do not carry a north arrow (plans do)
       but they MUST carry a scale (1:50, 1:100, 1:200) and a graphic
       scale bar. The graphic scale survives photocopying; the numeric
       scale does not.
    6. Labels. Material labels (concrete, steel, glazing, timber) point to
       the cut surface they describe via leader lines. Keep labels horizontal
       at one consistent x-anchor (right of the drawing in this template);
       do not let labels rotate or pack against the drawing.
-->
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     viewBox="0 0 900 640"
     role="img"
     aria-labelledby="title desc"
     font-family="Inter, system-ui, sans-serif">
  <title id="title">Section A-A through a two-storey reading-room pavilion.</title>
  <desc id="desc">An architectural section drawing of a two-storey reading-room pavilion, cut vertically along the line A-A. The section shows a concrete plinth at grade rising 600mm above ground level, a ground-floor reading room with double-height glazing 4200mm tall facing south, a steel column frame at the east and west walls, a timber-joisted intermediate floor at 3600mm, a second-floor mezzanine 2800mm tall, and a timber-deck flat roof with a 200mm parapet. The cut surfaces are hatched: concrete at a 45-degree cross-hatch, timber at a single-direction diagonal hatch, steel members as solid black profiles, and glazing as a thin double-line. Dimension lines on the right side of the drawing call out the floor-to-floor heights (3600mm and 2800mm) and the overall building height from grade to parapet (7000mm). The section indicator at the top reads "A" and matches a sister "A" arrow at the foot of the drawing; the section title reads "Section A-A · scale 1:50" below the drawing. Three material labels — concrete, structural steel, timber deck — point to the corresponding cut surfaces via leader lines at consistent right-anchor positions.</desc>

  <defs>
    <!-- Hatch pattern: concrete (45 degree cross-hatch) -->
    <pattern id="hatch-concrete" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse"
             width="6" height="6" patternTransform="rotate(45)">
      <line x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="6" stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="0.45"/>
      <line x1="3" y1="0" x2="3" y2="6" stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="0.45"/>
    </pattern>
    <!-- Hatch pattern: timber (single-direction diagonal) -->
    <pattern id="hatch-timber" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse"
             width="5" height="5" patternTransform="rotate(45)">
      <line x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="5" stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="0.45"/>
    </pattern>
    <!-- Hatch pattern: masonry / earth (denser diagonal) -->
    <pattern id="hatch-earth" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse"
             width="3" height="3" patternTransform="rotate(45)">
      <line x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="3" stroke="#5D5142" stroke-width="0.3"/>
    </pattern>
    <!-- Dimension-line arrowhead -->
    <marker id="dim-arrow" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="0" refY="5"
            markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto">
      <path d="M 0,5 L 10,0 L 10,10 Z" fill="#1A1A1A"/>
    </marker>
    <marker id="dim-arrow-end" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="10" refY="5"
            markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto">
      <path d="M 10,5 L 0,0 L 0,10 Z" fill="#1A1A1A"/>
    </marker>
    <marker id="section-arrow" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="5" refY="9"
            markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" orient="auto">
      <path d="M 5,0 L 10,10 L 0,10 Z" fill="#1A1A1A"/>
    </marker>

    <style>
      .ground          { fill: #F4F0E2; }
      .ink             { stroke: #1A1A1A; fill: none; }
      .ink-cut         { stroke-width: 1.4; }
      .ink-elev        { stroke-width: 0.6; }
      .ink-hidden      { stroke-width: 0.4; stroke-dasharray: 3 2; }
      .ink-construction { stroke-width: 0.3; opacity: 0.7; }
      .dim-line        { stroke: #1A1A1A; stroke-width: 0.45; fill: none; }
      .dim-ext         { stroke: #1A1A1A; stroke-width: 0.3; fill: none; }
      .label           { font-size: 9px; fill: #1A1A1A; }
      .label-mat       { font-size: 10px; fill: #1A1A1A; font-weight: 600;
                         letter-spacing: 0.04em; }
      .label-dim       { font-size: 9px; fill: #1A1A1A; }
      .label-meta      { font-size: 9px; fill: #5D5142; }
      .label-section   { font-size: 14px; fill: #1A1A1A; font-weight: 700; }
      .title-text      { font-size: 13px; fill: #1A1A1A; font-weight: 600;
                         letter-spacing: 0.05em; font-variant: small-caps; }
      .leader          { stroke: #5D5142; stroke-width: 0.4; fill: none; }
    </style>
  </defs>

  <rect class="ground" width="900" height="640"/>

  <!-- ============================================================
       Title block, top
       ============================================================ -->
  <text x="80" y="38" font-size="16" fill="#1A1A1A" font-weight="600">
    Reading-room pavilion · vertical section through A-A.
  </text>
  <text x="80" y="56" class="label-meta">
    Concrete plinth, steel frame, double-height south glazing, timber roof and floor deck.
  </text>

  <!-- ============================================================
       Section indicator at top
       ============================================================ -->
  <g transform="translate(140,82)">
    <circle r="11" fill="#F4F0E2" stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="0.8"/>
    <text x="0" y="4" text-anchor="middle" class="label-section">A</text>
    <line x1="0" y1="11" x2="0" y2="32" stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="0.6"
          marker-end="url(#section-arrow)"/>
  </g>

  <!-- ============================================================
       BUILDING SECTION
       Coordinate system: building origin at (140, 540) = ground line
       at left wall. Building extends right ~440 units, up ~370 units.
       1 SVG unit ≈ 20mm at print scale.
       ============================================================ -->

  <!-- Earth / ground hatching below grade -->
  <rect x="80" y="540" width="660" height="48" fill="url(#hatch-earth)"/>
  <line x1="80" y1="540" x2="740" y2="540" stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="0.6"/>
  <!-- Grade-line tick triangles -->
  <g fill="#1A1A1A">
    <path d="M 168,536 L 174,540 L 162,540 Z"/>
    <path d="M 168,540 L 174,540 L 168,548 Z" fill="none" stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="0.4"/>
  </g>
  <text x="180" y="552" class="label">±0.000 grade</text>

  <!-- ===== CONCRETE PLINTH (cut) ===== -->
  <!-- Plinth wall: 600mm tall above grade, 300mm thick, extends below grade -->
  <g>
    <rect x="140" y="510" width="20" height="78" fill="url(#hatch-concrete)"
          stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="1.4"/>
    <rect x="580" y="510" width="20" height="78" fill="url(#hatch-concrete)"
          stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="1.4"/>
    <!-- Ground floor slab: 200mm thick concrete -->
    <rect x="140" y="510" width="460" height="14" fill="url(#hatch-concrete)"
          stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="1.4"/>
    <!-- Foundation strip beneath each plinth -->
    <rect x="130" y="572" width="40" height="16" fill="url(#hatch-concrete)"
          stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="1.0"/>
    <rect x="570" y="572" width="40" height="16" fill="url(#hatch-concrete)"
          stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="1.0"/>
  </g>

  <!-- ===== STEEL COLUMNS (cut, solid black) ===== -->
  <g fill="#1A1A1A">
    <!-- West column, 200mm wide, from plinth top to roof underside -->
    <rect x="148" y="170" width="6" height="340"/>
    <!-- East column -->
    <rect x="586" y="170" width="6" height="340"/>
  </g>

  <!-- ===== INTERMEDIATE FLOOR (timber on steel) ===== -->
  <!-- Floor at +3600mm from grade (y = 510 - 3.6 * 50 = 330). -->
  <g>
    <!-- Steel beam (solid black) -->
    <rect x="156" y="320" width="426" height="8" fill="#1A1A1A"/>
    <!-- Timber deck on top -->
    <rect x="156" y="312" width="426" height="8" fill="url(#hatch-timber)"
          stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="0.8"/>
  </g>

  <!-- ===== ROOF (timber deck on steel, with parapet) ===== -->
  <!-- Roof at +7000mm from grade (y = 510 - 7.0 * 50 = 160) -->
  <g>
    <!-- Steel beam -->
    <rect x="156" y="166" width="426" height="6" fill="#1A1A1A"/>
    <!-- Timber roof deck -->
    <rect x="140" y="156" width="460" height="10" fill="url(#hatch-timber)"
          stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="0.8"/>
    <!-- Parapets -->
    <rect x="140" y="140" width="20" height="16" fill="url(#hatch-concrete)"
          stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="1.2"/>
    <rect x="580" y="140" width="20" height="16" fill="url(#hatch-concrete)"
          stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="1.2"/>
  </g>

  <!-- ===== GLAZING (south wall, thin double-line) =====
       Glazing is in the *plane* of the section so it appears as
       two thin vertical lines bounding the glass thickness.
       In a real section, the glazing line crosses the floor plate.
       ===== -->
  <g class="ink">
    <!-- North wall glazing simplified as two parallel lines -->
    <line class="ink-elev" x1="160" y1="172" x2="160" y2="510"/>
    <line class="ink-elev" x1="162" y1="172" x2="162" y2="510"/>
    <line class="ink-elev" x1="578" y1="172" x2="578" y2="510"/>
    <line class="ink-elev" x1="580" y1="172" x2="580" y2="510"/>
    <!-- Mullions (steel) at the floor-line on each side -->
    <rect x="158" y="322" width="6" height="4" fill="#1A1A1A"/>
    <rect x="576" y="322" width="6" height="4" fill="#1A1A1A"/>
  </g>

  <!-- ===== INTERIOR ELEMENTS (light weight, "behind the cut") ===== -->
  <g class="ink ink-elev" stroke="#5D5142" opacity="0.85">
    <!-- Ground-floor furniture: reading bench -->
    <rect x="220" y="488" width="120" height="20" fill="none"/>
    <line x1="220" y1="488" x2="220" y2="508"/>
    <line x1="340" y1="488" x2="340" y2="508"/>
    <text x="280" y="502" text-anchor="middle" font-size="8" fill="#5D5142">reading bench</text>

    <!-- Ground-floor bookshelf (taller) -->
    <rect x="400" y="380" width="40" height="128" fill="none"/>
    <line x1="400" y1="408" x2="440" y2="408"/>
    <line x1="400" y1="436" x2="440" y2="436"/>
    <line x1="400" y1="464" x2="440" y2="464"/>
    <line x1="400" y1="492" x2="440" y2="492"/>

    <!-- Mezzanine: small table -->
    <rect x="280" y="296" width="60" height="14" fill="none"/>
    <line x1="284" y1="310" x2="284" y2="320"/>
    <line x1="336" y1="310" x2="336" y2="320"/>
    <text x="310" y="284" text-anchor="middle" font-size="8" fill="#5D5142">table</text>

    <!-- Mezzanine: handrail at the floor edge -->
    <line x1="156" y1="260" x2="160" y2="260" stroke-width="1.2"/>
    <line x1="160" y1="260" x2="160" y2="312" stroke-width="0.5"/>
  </g>

  <!-- Stair: simplified switchback between floors -->
  <g class="ink ink-elev">
    <path d="M 460,510 L 480,510 L 480,488 L 500,488 L 500,466 L 520,466
             L 520,444 L 540,444 L 540,422 L 560,422 L 560,400 L 580,400"
          stroke="#5D5142" stroke-width="0.5" fill="none"/>
  </g>

  <!-- ============================================================
       DIMENSION LINES (right side of drawing, ISO 128 convention)
       Extension lines perpendicular to the dimensioned surface,
       gap 1-2 units from the surface, projecting past the dim line.
       ============================================================ -->
  <g>
    <!-- Floor-to-floor 1: ground floor to mezzanine = 3600mm -->
    <line class="dim-ext" x1="606" y1="510" x2="660" y2="510"/>
    <line class="dim-ext" x1="606" y1="320" x2="660" y2="320"/>
    <line class="dim-line" x1="648" y1="510" x2="648" y2="320"
          marker-start="url(#dim-arrow)" marker-end="url(#dim-arrow-end)"/>
    <rect x="630" y="408" width="36" height="14" fill="#F4F0E2"/>
    <text x="648" y="418" class="label-dim" text-anchor="middle">3600</text>

    <!-- Floor-to-floor 2: mezzanine to roof = 2800mm -->
    <line class="dim-ext" x1="606" y1="320" x2="660" y2="320"/>
    <line class="dim-ext" x1="606" y1="166" x2="660" y2="166"/>
    <line class="dim-line" x1="648" y1="320" x2="648" y2="166"
          marker-start="url(#dim-arrow)" marker-end="url(#dim-arrow-end)"/>
    <rect x="630" y="237" width="36" height="14" fill="#F4F0E2"/>
    <text x="648" y="247" class="label-dim" text-anchor="middle">2800</text>

    <!-- Overall: grade to parapet = 7000mm -->
    <line class="dim-ext" x1="606" y1="540" x2="710" y2="540"/>
    <line class="dim-ext" x1="606" y1="140" x2="710" y2="140"/>
    <line class="dim-line" x1="698" y1="540" x2="698" y2="140"
          marker-start="url(#dim-arrow)" marker-end="url(#dim-arrow-end)"/>
    <rect x="678" y="333" width="40" height="14" fill="#F4F0E2"/>
    <text x="698" y="343" class="label-dim" text-anchor="middle">7000</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Plinth height dim, left side -->
  <g>
    <line class="dim-ext" x1="138" y1="540" x2="100" y2="540"/>
    <line class="dim-ext" x1="138" y1="510" x2="100" y2="510"/>
    <line class="dim-line" x1="112" y1="540" x2="112" y2="510"
          marker-start="url(#dim-arrow)" marker-end="url(#dim-arrow-end)"/>
    <rect x="98" y="518" width="28" height="14" fill="#F4F0E2"/>
    <text x="112" y="528" class="label-dim" text-anchor="middle">600</text>
  </g>

  <!-- ============================================================
       MATERIAL LABELS — leader lines to cut surfaces
       ============================================================ -->
  <g>
    <!-- Concrete plinth -->
    <line class="leader" x1="150" y1="498" x2="80" y2="465"/>
    <text class="label-mat" x="80" y="460" text-anchor="end">CONCRETE PLINTH</text>
    <text class="label-meta" x="80" y="473" text-anchor="end">C30/37 · in-situ</text>

    <!-- Structural steel -->
    <line class="leader" x1="154" y1="240" x2="80" y2="240"/>
    <text class="label-mat" x="80" y="236" text-anchor="end">STRUCTURAL STEEL</text>
    <text class="label-meta" x="80" y="249" text-anchor="end">S355 · UC 203×203</text>

    <!-- Timber roof deck -->
    <line class="leader" x1="370" y1="160" x2="380" y2="100"/>
    <text class="label-mat" x="380" y="96">TIMBER DECK</text>
    <text class="label-meta" x="380" y="109">CLT · 5-ply · 160mm</text>

    <!-- Glazing -->
    <line class="leader" x1="580" y1="400" x2="780" y2="400"/>
    <text class="label-mat" x="785" y="396">GLAZING</text>
    <text class="label-meta" x="785" y="409">Triple IGU · low-E</text>
  </g>

  <!-- ============================================================
       Section indicator at foot — sister arrow to the one at top
       ============================================================ -->
  <g transform="translate(140,608)">
    <line x1="0" y1="-20" x2="0" y2="0" stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="0.6"
          marker-end="url(#section-arrow)"/>
    <circle cy="6" r="11" fill="#F4F0E2" stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="0.8"/>
    <text y="10" text-anchor="middle" class="label-section">A</text>
  </g>

  <!-- ============================================================
       Scale bar + section title at foot
       ============================================================ -->
  <g transform="translate(440,612)">
    <line x1="0" y1="0" x2="120" y2="0" stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="0.8"/>
    <line x1="0" y1="-4" x2="0" y2="4" stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="0.6"/>
    <line x1="40" y1="-3" x2="40" y2="3" stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="0.4"/>
    <line x1="80" y1="-3" x2="80" y2="3" stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="0.4"/>
    <line x1="120" y1="-4" x2="120" y2="4" stroke="#1A1A1A" stroke-width="0.6"/>
    <text x="0" y="16" class="label-meta">0</text>
    <text x="120" y="16" class="label-meta">2 m</text>
    <text x="60" y="-10" text-anchor="middle" class="label-meta">scale bar (graphic)</text>
  </g>

  <text x="700" y="612" class="title-text">Section A-A · scale 1:50</text>
  <text x="700" y="626" class="label-meta">All dimensions in millimetres. Levels relative to ±0.000 grade.</text>
</svg>

## `templates/svg-audubon-bird.svg`

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!--
  =============================================================================
  Template: svg-audubon-bird.svg / Status: Realized starter
  Subject: Wood Thrush (Hylocichla mustelina) — perched, three-quarter view,
           one wing extended to show variable-stroke contour and plumage hatching
  Register: 7 Calligraphic plate + 8 Cartouche / ornamental frame
  Exemplars: John James Audubon, Birds of America (1827–38);
             Max Brödel, anatomical drawings (1900s–40s);
             Andreas Vesalius, De humani corporis fabrica (1543)
  Signature moves: 1.11 calligraphic-stroke (proposed) — every contour varies in
                   stroke-width along the line to communicate volume + gesture;
                   1.14 cartouche-bound (proposed) — title, plate number, and
                   Latin label live inside a designed ornamental device.
  Render env: Single-file SVG; portable across browsers and print
  =============================================================================

  CUSTOMIZE — slots to adapt when reusing this scaffold:

    1. Subject. Replace the bird's body, wing, tail, and breast-spot paths with
       the subject's anatomy. Keep the path-splitting recipe (4-8 sub-paths
       per contour, each with its own stroke-width following the contour's
       logic — see svg-illustration.md Pattern A).
    2. Latin and common names. The cartouche carries them as designed text;
       they are not metadata bolted on. Choose a name length that fits the
       cartouche curve without breaking the design — long binomials may
       require resizing the cartouche or moving to a two-line layout.
    3. Plate caption. Convention is "PLATE [Roman numeral] — [Genre]" in small
       caps at the bottom. Genre is the taxonomic family or the artifact
       series (e.g., "WARBLERS", "NORTH AMERICAN PASSERINES").
    4. Locality and date. The Audubon convention is "[Location] · [Year]"
       below the plate caption. Keep terse; do not pad with provenance prose.
    5. Stroke-width palette. Leading edges are heaviest (1.8-2.4); flight
       feathers medium (1.0-1.4); fine detail (eye ring, feather barbs) at
       0.4-0.6. Do not exceed 6 distinct widths; the variation must read as
       drawn, not as randomized.
    6. Color. Audubon's plates are watercolors on cream paper. This template
       sits at the line-engraving end of the register (sumi on warm white) for
       portability. For a watercolored version, add filled-path bodies in
       muted earth tones (sienna, burnt umber, dusty rose) at 70-85% opacity
       beneath the line work.
-->
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     viewBox="0 0 600 760"
     role="img"
     aria-labelledby="title desc"
     font-family="Source Serif Pro, Georgia, serif">
  <title id="title">Wood Thrush (Hylocichla mustelina), perched with one wing extended.</title>
  <desc id="desc">A calligraphic-plate illustration of a Wood Thrush, shown in three-quarter view perched on a slim branch. The bird's body is rendered in variable-stroke line work — the contours of the head, back, wing, and tail vary in thickness from a fine 0.5px at the leading edges of feathers to a heavy 2.4px at the body's belly contour. The breast carries the species' characteristic round dark spots over a pale ground. One wing is partially extended to display the primary and secondary flight feathers. An ornamental cartouche at the top of the plate carries the Latin and common names; a plate caption at the foot of the plate reads "PLATE XXIII — NORTH AMERICAN THRUSHES" with the locality and year set below in small caps.</desc>

  <defs>
    <style>
      .ground       { fill: #F5EFE0; }
      .ink          { stroke: #1C1814; fill: none; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; }
      .ink-hair     { stroke-width: 0.4; opacity: 0.85; }
      .ink-fine     { stroke-width: 0.7; opacity: 0.92; }
      .ink-medium   { stroke-width: 1.1; opacity: 0.95; }
      .ink-heavy    { stroke-width: 1.6; opacity: 0.96; }
      .ink-major    { stroke-width: 2.1; opacity: 0.97; }
      .fill-breast  { fill: #F0E5CC; }
      .fill-shadow  { fill: #1C1814; opacity: 0.85; }
      .latin        { font-style: italic; font-size: 14px; fill: #1C1814; }
      .common       { font-size: 12px; fill: #1C1814; letter-spacing: 0.02em; }
      .caption      { font-size: 11px; fill: #1C1814; font-variant: small-caps;
                      letter-spacing: 0.12em; }
      .meta         { font-size: 10px; fill: #5D5142; font-variant: small-caps;
                      letter-spacing: 0.10em; }
      .cartouche    { stroke: #1C1814; stroke-width: 0.9; fill: none; }
      .cartouche-fill { fill: #F5EFE0; }
    </style>
  </defs>

  <rect class="ground" x="0" y="0" width="600" height="760"/>

  <!-- =========================================================
       CARTOUCHE — top of plate, holds the species names
       Baroque-curve outline with text following the upper arc
       ========================================================= -->
  <g class="cartouche-group" transform="translate(300,90)">
    <path id="cartouche-curve"
          class="cartouche cartouche-fill"
          d="M -180,-30 Q -200,-20 -180,0
             Q -200,20 -180,30
             Q -120,42 0,42 Q 120,42 180,30
             Q 200,20 180,0
             Q 200,-20 180,-30
             Q 120,-42 0,-42 Q -120,-42 -180,-30 Z"/>
    <!-- Inner hairline frame, 4mm offset -->
    <path class="cartouche"
          stroke-width="0.4"
          d="M -170,-26 Q -188,-18 -172,-2
             Q -188,18 -170,26
             Q -118,36 0,36 Q 118,36 170,26
             Q 188,18 172,-2
             Q 188,-18 170,-26
             Q 118,-36 0,-36 Q -118,-36 -170,-26 Z"/>
    <!-- Small fleurons at left and right -->
    <text x="-152" y="6" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" fill="#1C1814">❦</text>
    <text x="152" y="6" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" fill="#1C1814">❦</text>
    <text text-anchor="middle" y="-8" class="latin">Hylocichla mustelina</text>
    <text text-anchor="middle" y="14" class="common">WOOD THRUSH</text>
  </g>

  <!-- =========================================================
       SUBJECT — the bird, calligraphic-line work
       Path-splitting per Pattern A. Coordinates are absolute in
       the SVG viewBox; the bird occupies roughly y=180 to y=560.
       ========================================================= -->

  <!-- Branch (perch) -->
  <g class="ink">
    <path class="ink-medium" d="M 120,520 Q 200,510 320,520 Q 400,524 500,530"/>
    <path class="ink-fine"   d="M 240,520 Q 244,510 252,506"/>
    <path class="ink-fine"   d="M 380,524 Q 388,516 394,512"/>
    <!-- Bark hatching -->
    <path class="ink-hair" d="M 180,518 L 184,524 M 200,517 L 204,523 M 220,517 L 224,523
                              M 280,520 L 284,526 M 320,521 L 324,527 M 360,522 L 364,528
                              M 400,524 L 404,530 M 440,526 L 444,532"/>
  </g>

  <!-- =====================================================
       HEAD — round, with eye, eye-ring, and bill
       Light stroke at the crown (thin), heaviest at the nape
       ===================================================== -->
  <g class="ink">
    <!-- Crown to nape contour, variable stroke -->
    <path class="ink-fine"   d="M 260,235 Q 268,222 285,218"/>
    <path class="ink-medium" d="M 285,218 Q 305,215 325,222"/>
    <path class="ink-heavy"  d="M 325,222 Q 340,228 348,242"/>
    <!-- Throat to breast contour -->
    <path class="ink-medium" d="M 260,266 Q 258,278 268,290"/>
    <path class="ink-heavy"  d="M 268,290 Q 280,304 296,312"/>
    <!-- Bill: short, pointed, dark -->
    <path class="ink-major" d="M 258,250 L 240,252 L 257,256 Z" fill="#1C1814"/>
    <!-- Eye -->
    <circle cx="278" cy="244" r="3.2" fill="#1C1814"/>
    <!-- Eye-ring (a thin pale ring around the eye) -->
    <circle cx="278" cy="244" r="4.6" stroke="#1C1814" stroke-width="0.5" fill="none"/>
    <!-- Subtle head feathering -->
    <path class="ink-hair" d="M 295,228 Q 300,232 304,236
                              M 305,226 Q 312,230 318,234
                              M 315,225 Q 322,228 328,232"/>
  </g>

  <!-- =====================================================
       BODY — back contour, belly contour
       Major stroke at the belly's underside
       ===================================================== -->
  <g class="ink">
    <!-- Back: from nape down to the rump -->
    <path class="ink-medium" d="M 348,242 Q 380,250 410,268"/>
    <path class="ink-heavy"  d="M 410,268 Q 438,290 450,330"/>
    <path class="ink-medium" d="M 450,330 Q 452,360 444,388"/>

    <!-- Belly: pale, with the heaviest stroke beneath -->
    <path class="ink-heavy"  d="M 296,312 Q 320,332 350,344"/>
    <path class="ink-major"  d="M 350,344 Q 392,356 426,358"/>
    <path class="ink-major"  d="M 426,358 Q 446,360 444,388"/>

    <!-- Breast fill: pale cream, beneath the spots -->
    <path class="fill-breast" d="M 296,312 Q 320,332 350,344 Q 392,356 426,358
                                 Q 446,360 444,388 Q 440,408 416,420
                                 Q 380,428 340,420 Q 304,408 292,378
                                 Q 286,344 296,312 Z"/>

    <!-- Spots on the breast (Wood Thrush's signature) -->
    <g class="fill-shadow">
      <ellipse cx="316" cy="332" rx="3.4" ry="2.8"/>
      <ellipse cx="340" cy="344" rx="3.8" ry="3.2"/>
      <ellipse cx="368" cy="354" rx="4.0" ry="3.4"/>
      <ellipse cx="396" cy="356" rx="3.6" ry="3.0"/>
      <ellipse cx="324" cy="360" rx="3.2" ry="2.6"/>
      <ellipse cx="352" cy="372" rx="3.8" ry="3.2"/>
      <ellipse cx="380" cy="378" rx="3.4" ry="2.8"/>
      <ellipse cx="408" cy="380" rx="3.2" ry="2.6"/>
      <ellipse cx="334" cy="388" rx="3.0" ry="2.4"/>
      <ellipse cx="362" cy="396" rx="3.2" ry="2.6"/>
      <ellipse cx="390" cy="398" rx="3.0" ry="2.4"/>
    </g>
  </g>

  <!-- =====================================================
       EXTENDED WING — the plate's calligraphic showpiece
       Leading edge (top) varies from 0.6 (tip) to 2.4 (shoulder)
       ===================================================== -->
  <g class="ink">
    <!-- Leading edge, path-split into 5 sub-paths -->
    <path d="M 348,242 Q 388,228 432,228" stroke="#1C1814" stroke-width="0.6" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.95"/>
    <path d="M 432,228 Q 472,232 504,244" stroke="#1C1814" stroke-width="1.1" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.96"/>
    <path d="M 504,244 Q 528,256 544,278" stroke="#1C1814" stroke-width="1.6" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.96"/>
    <path d="M 544,278 Q 556,304 558,328" stroke="#1C1814" stroke-width="2.1" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.97"/>
    <path d="M 558,328 Q 554,344 542,354" stroke="#1C1814" stroke-width="2.4" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="0.97"/>

    <!-- Trailing edge of the wing, sweep back into the body -->
    <path class="ink-heavy" d="M 542,354 Q 510,360 470,348"/>
    <path class="ink-medium" d="M 470,348 Q 438,338 410,326"/>
    <path class="ink-fine" d="M 410,326 Q 392,318 380,308"/>

    <!-- Primary flight feathers (long, parallel, splayed) -->
    <g stroke="#1C1814" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round">
      <path stroke-width="0.7" d="M 460,238 L 504,304"/>
      <path stroke-width="0.8" d="M 482,236 L 524,308"/>
      <path stroke-width="0.9" d="M 504,240 L 544,316"/>
      <path stroke-width="1.0" d="M 524,252 L 558,328"/>
    </g>
    <!-- Secondary flight feathers (shorter, behind the primaries) -->
    <g stroke="#1C1814" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round">
      <path stroke-width="0.5" d="M 400,254 L 432,308"/>
      <path stroke-width="0.5" d="M 420,250 L 452,310"/>
      <path stroke-width="0.6" d="M 438,248 L 472,318"/>
    </g>
    <!-- Covert feathers (small, layered along the shoulder) -->
    <g stroke="#1C1814" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-width="0.4" opacity="0.85">
      <path d="M 358,250 Q 366,248 374,252"/>
      <path d="M 372,246 Q 380,244 388,248"/>
      <path d="M 386,242 Q 394,240 402,244"/>
      <path d="M 400,240 Q 408,238 416,242"/>
    </g>
  </g>

  <!-- =====================================================
       TAIL — short, square, slightly fanned
       ===================================================== -->
  <g class="ink">
    <path class="ink-medium" d="M 444,388 Q 470,402 488,418 Q 492,428 484,434
                                Q 460,432 444,420 Q 436,406 444,388 Z"/>
    <!-- Tail feather divisions -->
    <path class="ink-hair" d="M 452,396 L 470,420 M 460,398 L 476,422 M 470,400 L 480,424"/>
  </g>

  <!-- =====================================================
       LEGS — slim, anchoring the bird to the branch
       ===================================================== -->
  <g class="ink">
    <path class="ink-medium" d="M 360,416 L 354,496 L 348,514"/>
    <path class="ink-fine" d="M 348,514 L 340,520 M 348,514 L 352,520 M 348,514 L 358,520"/>
    <path class="ink-medium" d="M 396,420 L 398,500 L 404,518"/>
    <path class="ink-fine" d="M 404,518 L 396,524 M 404,518 L 408,524 M 404,518 L 414,524"/>
  </g>

  <!-- =========================================================
       LEADER LINES + CALLOUTS (Haeckel-grammar carryover)
       Three labels: crown, breast spotting, primary feathers
       ========================================================= -->
  <g stroke="#5D5142" stroke-width="0.4" fill="none">
    <line x1="304" y1="222" x2="120" y2="200"/>
    <line x1="396" y1="356" x2="120" y2="380"/>
    <line x1="510" y1="288" x2="540" y2="600"/>
  </g>
  <text class="meta" x="60" y="196" text-anchor="start">a · cinnamon crown</text>
  <text class="meta" x="60" y="376" text-anchor="start">b · rounded breast spots</text>
  <text class="meta" x="486" y="616" text-anchor="start">c · primaries</text>

  <!-- =========================================================
       PLATE CAPTION at foot
       ========================================================= -->
  <line x1="60" y1="680" x2="540" y2="680" stroke="#1C1814" stroke-width="0.4"/>
  <text class="caption" x="300" y="700" text-anchor="middle">
    Plate XXIII — North American Thrushes
  </text>
  <text class="meta" x="300" y="720" text-anchor="middle">
    Mill Grove, Pennsylvania · Drawn from life, 1827
  </text>
  <text class="meta" x="300" y="738" text-anchor="middle" fill="#8A7B62">
    After J. J. Audubon · Reference plate
  </text>
</svg>
```

## `templates/svg-comparative-plate.svg`

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!--
  =============================================================================
  Template: svg-comparative-plate.svg / Status: Realized starter
  Subject: Three small warblers compared at shared baseline and scale —
           Yellow Warbler (Setophaga petechia), Wilson's Warbler (Cardellina
           pusilla), Magnolia Warbler (Setophaga magnolia)
  Register: 10 Comparative plate (Sibley)
  Exemplars: David Sibley, Field Guide to Birds (2000);
             Roger Tory Peterson, A Field Guide to the Birds (1934, revisions
             through 2010s); the National Geographic Field Guide series.
  Signature move: 1.13 identity-system (proposed) — a single visual grammar
                  (shared baseline, shared scale, field-mark leader lines from
                  a consistent anchor, Latin label in italic at consistent
                  position) repeated across the three subjects so the reader
                  compares directly without decoding.
  Render env: Single-file SVG; portable across browsers and print
  =============================================================================

  CUSTOMIZE — slots to adapt when reusing this scaffold:

    1. Subjects. Replace the three warbler bodies with the comparative set.
       Maintain the discipline: same baseline (y=440), same scale (each
       subject's silhouette fits within a ~140 × 200 unit bounding box),
       same orientation (all facing left or all facing right; do not mix).
       Three subjects is comfortable; four is the upper bound at this canvas
       size. Beyond four, increase the viewBox width or split into multiple
       plates.
    2. Field-mark callouts. Each subject carries 2-3 leader lines pointing
       to its distinguishing features. The labels stack at a *consistent
       anchor* (right of each subject in this template) so the reader's eye
       knows where to find them. Do not let labels overlap subjects.
    3. Scale bar. The shared scale-bar at the bottom encodes "all subjects
       drawn to the same scale" graphically; do not omit. The number (4 in)
       is the real-world reference. Choose a length that fits a meaningful
       round number in the subjects' size range.
    4. Latin and common names. Two-line label per subject: common name in
       roman small caps, scientific name in italic. Position consistent
       across all subjects (y-coordinate aligned).
    5. Color palette. This template uses a single ink color (sumi) for line
       work and three muted plumage colors (yellow ochre, olive, slate
       gray-blue) for fills. For field-guide use, add the species' breast
       and back colors in flat fills at ~75% opacity beneath the line work.
    6. Field-mark vocabulary. Use ornithological convention: "wing bars,"
       "eye ring," "undertail coverts," "supercilium," "lores," "malar
       stripe." Avoid plain-English substitutes; the reader of a comparative
       plate is fluent in the conventions.
-->
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     viewBox="0 0 900 600"
     role="img"
     aria-labelledby="title desc"
     font-family="Source Serif Pro, Georgia, serif">
  <title id="title">Three North American warblers compared at shared scale: Yellow, Wilson's, and Magnolia.</title>
  <desc id="desc">A comparative field-guide plate showing three small wood-warbler species at the same baseline and the same drawing scale, side by side. From left to right: the Yellow Warbler (Setophaga petechia), with bright yellow plumage and faint chestnut breast streaks; the Wilson's Warbler (Cardellina pusilla), with olive-yellow body and a distinctive small black cap; the Magnolia Warbler (Setophaga magnolia), with gray crown, yellow underparts, black necklace, and bold white tail patches. Each bird is rendered with line work plus a flat plumage fill, with leader lines pointing from the field-mark labels to the bird's distinguishing features. Below the three subjects, a horizontal scale bar marked "4 in" gives the real-world reference. The plate caption at the foot reads "Plate VII — Northern Wood-Warblers, Comparative."</desc>

  <defs>
    <style>
      .ground       { fill: #F4ECDC; }
      .ink          { stroke: #1F1A14; fill: none; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; }
      .ink-fine     { stroke-width: 0.5; opacity: 0.92; }
      .ink-body     { stroke-width: 1.0; opacity: 0.96; }
      .ink-heavy    { stroke-width: 1.5; opacity: 0.97; }
      .fill-yellow  { fill: #E8C75A; opacity: 0.85; }
      .fill-yellow-pale { fill: #F0DA90; opacity: 0.80; }
      .fill-olive   { fill: #99934A; opacity: 0.78; }
      .fill-slate   { fill: #66708A; opacity: 0.82; }
      .fill-white   { fill: #F4ECDC; }
      .fill-dark    { fill: #1F1A14; }
      .latin        { font-style: italic; font-size: 13px; fill: #1F1A14; }
      .common       { font-size: 11px; fill: #1F1A14; letter-spacing: 0.10em;
                      font-variant: small-caps; }
      .mark         { font-size: 10px; fill: #4A4234; font-style: italic; }
      .leader       { stroke: #6B5F4A; stroke-width: 0.4; fill: none; }
      .caption      { font-size: 11px; fill: #1F1A14; font-variant: small-caps;
                      letter-spacing: 0.14em; }
      .meta         { font-size: 9.5px; fill: #6B5F4A; font-variant: small-caps;
                      letter-spacing: 0.10em; }
      .scale-tick   { stroke: #1F1A14; stroke-width: 0.6; }
      .baseline     { stroke: #C7BC9F; stroke-width: 0.5; stroke-dasharray: 2 3; }
    </style>
  </defs>

  <rect class="ground" width="900" height="600"/>

  <!-- ============================================================
       Header
       ============================================================ -->
  <text x="80" y="50" font-size="18" fill="#1F1A14" font-weight="600">
    Three small wood-warblers at the same scale.
  </text>
  <text x="80" y="72" font-size="12" fill="#4A4234" font-style="italic">
    Compare crown color, breast pattern, and tail markings — the three
    most reliable field marks in this clade.
  </text>

  <!-- ============================================================
       Shared baseline (the comparative-plate's central convention)
       ============================================================ -->
  <line class="baseline" x1="60" y1="440" x2="840" y2="440"/>

  <!-- ============================================================
       SUBJECT 1: Yellow Warbler (Setophaga petechia)
       Anchor: x ~ 180, baseline y = 440. Subject occupies roughly
       y 280-440 (height ~ 160 units).
       ============================================================ -->
  <g id="yellow-warbler" transform="translate(180,0)">
    <!-- Body fill: bright yellow -->
    <path class="fill-yellow"
          d="M -30,360 Q -32,346 -20,332 Q -2,318 24,316
             Q 50,318 64,330 Q 70,346 60,366 Q 56,392 38,408
             Q 12,420 -14,414 Q -32,396 -32,378 Q -34,368 -30,360 Z"/>
    <!-- Head -->
    <circle class="fill-yellow" cx="-12" cy="324" r="22"/>
    <!-- Outline -->
    <g class="ink">
      <path class="ink-body"
            d="M -30,360 Q -32,346 -20,332 Q -2,318 24,316
               Q 50,318 64,330 Q 70,346 60,366 Q 56,392 38,408
               Q 12,420 -14,414 Q -32,396 -32,378 Q -34,368 -30,360 Z"/>
      <path class="ink-body" d="M -12,324 m -22,0 a 22,22 0 1,0 44,0 a 22,22 0 1,0 -44,0"/>
      <!-- Bill -->
      <path class="ink-heavy" d="M -36,326 L -46,330 L -36,332 Z" fill="#1F1A14"/>
      <!-- Eye (small, dark) -->
      <circle cx="-22" cy="320" r="2" fill="#1F1A14"/>
      <!-- Breast streaks (Setophaga petechia signature, fine chestnut) -->
      <g stroke="#A85A28" stroke-width="0.6" opacity="0.85">
        <path d="M -6,358 L -2,378"/>
        <path d="M 4,360 L 8,380"/>
        <path d="M 14,360 L 18,380"/>
        <path d="M 24,362 L 28,382"/>
      </g>
      <!-- Wing -->
      <path class="ink-body" d="M 18,346 Q 50,348 64,376 Q 56,388 42,392
                                Q 28,376 18,346 Z" fill="#C9A646" opacity="0.6"/>
      <!-- Legs -->
      <path class="ink-body" d="M 8,414 L 8,440"/>
      <path class="ink-body" d="M 30,414 L 30,440"/>
      <!-- Feet -->
      <path class="ink-fine" d="M 4,440 L 12,440 M 26,440 L 34,440"/>
      <!-- Tail -->
      <path class="ink-body" d="M 60,366 Q 86,374 96,394 Q 94,402 84,402
                                Q 72,394 60,378 Z" fill="#C9A646" opacity="0.6"/>
    </g>
  </g>

  <!-- Subject 1 label block -->
  <text class="common" x="180" y="468" text-anchor="middle">Yellow Warbler</text>
  <text class="latin"  x="180" y="484" text-anchor="middle">Setophaga petechia</text>
  <text class="meta"   x="180" y="500" text-anchor="middle">5.0 in · widespread</text>

  <!-- Subject 1 field marks -->
  <g class="leader">
    <line x1="174" y1="318" x2="120" y2="270"/>
    <line x1="200" y1="370" x2="248" y2="350"/>
    <line x1="240" y1="380" x2="284" y2="404"/>
  </g>
  <text class="mark" x="60" y="266">no eye ring; entirely yellow head</text>
  <text class="mark" x="252" y="346">faint chestnut breast streaks</text>
  <text class="mark" x="288" y="408">yellow tail spots</text>

  <!-- ============================================================
       SUBJECT 2: Wilson's Warbler (Cardellina pusilla)
       Anchor: x ~ 450, baseline y = 440.
       ============================================================ -->
  <g id="wilsons-warbler" transform="translate(450,0)">
    <!-- Body fill: olive-yellow (slightly more olive than the Yellow Warbler) -->
    <path class="fill-yellow-pale"
          d="M -28,358 Q -30,344 -18,330 Q 0,316 26,314
             Q 52,316 64,328 Q 70,344 60,364 Q 56,390 38,406
             Q 12,418 -14,412 Q -30,394 -30,376 Q -32,366 -28,358 Z"/>
    <!-- Back (olive) -->
    <path class="fill-olive"
          d="M 8,316 Q 36,316 60,326 Q 68,338 64,354
             Q 52,346 30,344 Q 14,342 8,330 Z"/>
    <!-- Head (olive-yellow base) -->
    <circle class="fill-yellow-pale" cx="-12" cy="322" r="22"/>
    <!-- Black cap (Wilson's signature) -->
    <path class="fill-dark"
          d="M -28,316 Q -16,300 0,300 Q 10,300 6,314 Q -8,318 -28,316 Z"/>
    <!-- Outline -->
    <g class="ink">
      <path class="ink-body"
            d="M -28,358 Q -30,344 -18,330 Q 0,316 26,314
               Q 52,316 64,328 Q 70,344 60,364 Q 56,390 38,406
               Q 12,418 -14,412 Q -30,394 -30,376 Q -32,366 -28,358 Z"/>
      <path class="ink-body" d="M -12,322 m -22,0 a 22,22 0 1,0 44,0 a 22,22 0 1,0 -44,0"/>
      <path class="ink-heavy" d="M -36,324 L -46,328 L -36,330 Z" fill="#1F1A14"/>
      <circle cx="-22" cy="318" r="2" fill="#1F1A14"/>
      <!-- Wing -->
      <path class="ink-body" d="M 18,344 Q 50,346 64,374 Q 56,386 42,390
                                Q 28,374 18,344 Z" fill="#7E7438" opacity="0.7"/>
      <!-- Legs and tail -->
      <path class="ink-body" d="M 8,412 L 8,440"/>
      <path class="ink-body" d="M 30,412 L 30,440"/>
      <path class="ink-fine" d="M 4,440 L 12,440 M 26,440 L 34,440"/>
      <path class="ink-body" d="M 60,364 Q 86,372 96,392 Q 94,400 84,400
                                Q 72,392 60,376 Z" fill="#7E7438" opacity="0.7"/>
    </g>
  </g>

  <text class="common" x="450" y="468" text-anchor="middle">Wilson's Warbler</text>
  <text class="latin"  x="450" y="484" text-anchor="middle">Cardellina pusilla</text>
  <text class="meta"   x="450" y="500" text-anchor="middle">4.6 in · western breeder</text>

  <g class="leader">
    <line x1="440" y1="304" x2="386" y2="262"/>
    <line x1="478" y1="332" x2="540" y2="316"/>
    <line x1="468" y1="376" x2="546" y2="378"/>
  </g>
  <text class="mark" x="326" y="258">small black cap (male)</text>
  <text class="mark" x="544" y="312">no wing bars; uniform olive back</text>
  <text class="mark" x="550" y="382">unmarked yellow belly</text>

  <!-- ============================================================
       SUBJECT 3: Magnolia Warbler (Setophaga magnolia)
       Anchor: x ~ 720, baseline y = 440.
       ============================================================ -->
  <g id="magnolia-warbler" transform="translate(720,0)">
    <!-- Body fill: yellow belly -->
    <path class="fill-yellow"
          d="M -28,360 Q -30,346 -18,332 Q 0,318 26,316
             Q 52,318 64,330 Q 70,346 60,366 Q 56,392 38,408
             Q 12,420 -14,414 Q -30,396 -30,378 Q -32,368 -28,360 Z"/>
    <!-- Slate-gray back -->
    <path class="fill-slate"

             Q 52,348 30,346 Q 14,344 6,332 Z"/>
    <!-- Gray crown -->
    <circle class="fill-slate" cx="-12" cy="324" r="22"/>
    <!-- Yellow throat patch -->
    <path class="fill-yellow"
          d="M -28,332 Q -16,346 6,348 Q 12,360 -4,360 Q -22,358 -28,344 Z"/>
    <!-- Black "necklace" of breast streaks -->
    <g stroke="#1F1A14" stroke-width="1.3" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round">
      <path d="M -6,358 L -2,378"/>
      <path d="M 4,360 L 8,380"/>
      <path d="M 14,360 L 18,380"/>
      <path d="M 24,362 L 28,382"/>
      <path d="M -10,374 L -8,388"/>
      <path d="M 2,376 L 4,390"/>
    </g>
    <g class="ink">
      <path class="ink-body"
            d="M -28,360 Q -30,346 -18,332 Q 0,318 26,316
               Q 52,318 64,330 Q 70,346 60,366 Q 56,392 38,408
               Q 12,420 -14,414 Q -30,396 -30,378 Q -32,368 -28,360 Z"/>
      <path class="ink-body" d="M -12,324 m -22,0 a 22,22 0 1,0 44,0 a 22,22 0 1,0 -44,0"/>
      <path class="ink-heavy" d="M -36,326 L -46,330 L -36,332 Z" fill="#1F1A14"/>
      <!-- White eye-arcs (Magnolia signature: split white eye-ring) -->
      <path class="ink-fine" stroke="#F4ECDC" stroke-width="1.4"
            d="M -28,318 Q -22,314 -16,318 M -28,324 Q -22,328 -16,324"/>
      <circle cx="-22" cy="321" r="2" fill="#1F1A14"/>
      <!-- Wing with white wing-bars (Magnolia signature) -->
      <path class="ink-body" d="M 18,346 Q 50,348 64,376 Q 56,388 42,392
                                Q 28,376 18,346 Z" fill="#4D5A75" opacity="0.85"/>
      <path stroke="#F4ECDC" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" fill="none"
            d="M 26,360 L 56,366 M 30,374 L 58,378"/>
      <!-- Legs -->
      <path class="ink-body" d="M 8,414 L 8,440"/>
      <path class="ink-body" d="M 30,414 L 30,440"/>
      <path class="ink-fine" d="M 4,440 L 12,440 M 26,440 L 34,440"/>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!--
  Template: svg-consort-flow.svg / Status: Realized starter
  Subject: CONSORT 2010 flow diagram — fictional 1240-patient RCT of BIOX-3219
           (anti-TSLP monoclonal) vs. placebo for severe eosinophilic asthma
  Register: Technical / scientific (CONSORT 2010 reporting standard)
  Signature move: 4.1 honest-edge-case-on-diagram — every excluded patient,
                  every discontinuation, every per-protocol exclusion accounted
                  for with reason cited; box arithmetic verifiable cell-by-cell
  Render env: Single-file SVG; portable across browsers, PDF, and print

  CUSTOMIZE — slots to adapt when reusing this scaffold:
    1. Trial identifier. The NCT id (placeholder NCT05XXXXXXX) and trial
       short-title in <title>/<desc> must match the registered protocol.
    2. Arm names. Two arms here. For three-arm trials extend Allocation to
       three columns; for factorial designs see CONSORT 2010 factorial extension.
    3. Sample sizes. Arithmetic must verify at each tier:
         assessed = excluded + enrolled; enrolled = randomized;
         randomized = sum of allocated; per arm: received + did-not-receive;
         per arm: completed + lost + discontinued; ITT + per-protocol reported.
    4. Exclusion reasons at each tier. Replace with trial's actual reasons;
       aggregate <5% categories as "other" with per-reason breakdown elsewhere.
    5. Follow-up duration (52 weeks here). Adjust per-arm annotations when the
       primary endpoint timepoint differs.
    6. Analysis populations. ITT + per-protocol shown; add Safety row when it
       differs from ITT.
    7. Header / footer non-removable. The CONSORT 2010 citation in the footer
       is a methodological obligation, not decoration.

  REAL-USE NOTE: Box arithmetic must verify before submission. Reviewers and
  CONSORT-compliance editors sum each tier; any discrepancy is flagged as a
  methodological lapse. The fictional numbers below verify; check yours.
-->
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     viewBox="0 0 900 1240"
     role="img"
     aria-labelledby="title desc"
     font-family="Inter, system-ui, sans-serif">

Enrollment: 1240 patients assessed for eligibility, 340 excluded (212 not meeting inclusion criteria, 84 declined to participate, 44 other reasons), 900 enrolled and randomized. Allocation: 450 allocated to BIOX-3219 (438 received allocated intervention, 12 did not receive due to consent withdrawal after randomization), 450 allocated to placebo (445 received, 5 did not receive). Follow-up: BIOX-3219 arm 412 completed 52-week follow-up, 26 lost to follow-up or discontinued (12 adverse event, 8 lost to follow-up, 6 withdrew consent); Placebo arm 408 completed, 37 lost or discontinued (5 adverse event, 19 lost to follow-up, 13 withdrew consent). Analysis: BIOX-3219 ITT 450, per-protocol 412; Placebo ITT 450, per-protocol 408. Source citation: Schulz KF, Altman DG, Moher D. CONSORT 2010 Statement. BMJ 2010;340:c332.</desc>

## `templates/svg-cyanotype-botanical.svg`

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!--
  =============================================================================
  Template: svg-cyanotype-botanical.svg / Status: Realized starter
  Subject: Common Polypody fern (Polypodium vulgare) — single frond,
           silhouette with vein and pinnae detail visible as lighter
           transmitted-light shadow within the Prussian-blue ground.
  Register: 15 Cyanotype / historical-photographic
  Exemplars: Anna Atkins, Photographs of British Algae: Cyanotype Impressions
             (1843) — the first photographically illustrated book of any kind;
             William Henry Fox Talbot, photogenic drawings (1834–);
             contemporary cyanotype artists (Christian Marclay; Marco Breuer).
  Signature move: 1.3 duotone with a single accent (extended) — every chroma
                  on the plate is Prussian-blue or its dilutions; the only
                  "color" decisions are *how much* blue and *where it is
                  absent* (the cream ground appears where the specimen
                  occluded the photosensitive paper).
  Render env: Single-file SVG; portable across browsers and print
  =============================================================================

  CUSTOMIZE — slots to adapt when reusing this scaffold:

    1. Specimen. Replace the fern path with the subject's outline. Author the
       specimen as a single filled SVG path with the Prussian-blue fill at
       ~0.92 opacity; the cream ground bleeds through subtly at the edges
       and reads as the chemical's natural slight transparency.
    2. Detail layer. Veins, pinnae margins, or stem ridges are rendered as
       paths in a *slightly lighter* blue (the cyanotype process retains
       partial detail where the specimen is thin enough to transmit some
       light — leaf veins on a fern, stem chambers on a hollow plant, the
       structure of a feather). Stroke-width 0.4-0.6; opacity 0.4-0.7;
       fill: none.
    3. Hand-lettered label. The Atkins convention is hand-lettered Latin
       binomial below the specimen, in the same Prussian-blue ink. This
       template uses an italic serif at ~12pt; for a closer Atkins
       imitation, use a Caslon or Baskerville italic at the same size.
    4. Margins. Cyanotype plates traditionally carry generous margins (the
       paper itself was larger than the specimen contact area). Keep the
       specimen in the central 60% of the viewBox; resist filling the
       margins with metadata.
    5. Provenance line. Atkins published with terse provenance — locality,
       date, and "Photographed by A.A." in a corner. This template carries
       the convention in the bottom-right corner; keep terse.
    6. Color discipline. The Prussian-blue is #0B3A6B. Do not introduce
       a second hue. The lighter blue for vein detail is the same hue
       desaturated and lightened (oklch is the simplest tool: oklch from
       #0B3A6B is approximately oklch(28% 0.10 252); the vein color is
       approximately oklch(50% 0.08 252) = #4A6B92).
       The cream ground is #F2E6CC.
-->
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     viewBox="0 0 600 800"
     role="img"
     aria-labelledby="title desc"
     font-family="Source Serif Pro, Georgia, serif">
  <title id="title">Polypodium vulgare — a single fern frond, rendered as a cyanotype contact print.</title>
  <desc id="desc">A botanical specimen plate in the cyanotype tradition of Anna Atkins. A single frond of common polypody (Polypodium vulgare) occupies the center of the cream-toned paper, silhouetted in deep Prussian blue. The frond's pinnate structure is fully visible — about fifteen paired pinnae along a central rachis, each pinna shaped like a slender lobed blade. Faint, slightly lighter blue lines run within each pinna to show the central vein where the specimen's translucent tissue transmitted some light onto the photosensitive paper. Below the specimen, in hand-lettered italic Prussian-blue serif, the binomial "Polypodium vulgare" appears, with the common name "Common Polypody" set in roman small caps beneath. A provenance line in the lower right corner reads "Halliford, Middlesex · 1843 · A.A." in the same blue ink.</desc>

  <defs>
