      .prussian-soft { fill: #0B3A6B; opacity: 0.92; }
      .vein         { stroke: #4A6B92; stroke-width: 0.5; fill: none; opacity: 0.6;
                      stroke-linecap: round; }
      .vein-bold    { stroke: #4A6B92; stroke-width: 0.8; fill: none; opacity: 0.75;
                      stroke-linecap: round; }
      .label-latin  { font-style: italic; font-size: 18px; fill: #0B3A6B; }
      .label-common { font-size: 12px; fill: #0B3A6B; letter-spacing: 0.14em;
                      font-variant: small-caps; }
      .label-meta   { font-size: 10px; fill: #0B3A6B; letter-spacing: 0.06em;
                      font-style: italic; opacity: 0.85; }
      .border       { stroke: #0B3A6B; stroke-width: 0.4; fill: none; opacity: 0.6; }
      /* Subtle paper texture: pale blue blotches where the chemical wash pooled */
      .wash         { fill: #0B3A6B; opacity: 0.04; }
    </style>

    <!-- Soft edge for the specimen: the cyanotype's slight bleed at contours -->
    <filter id="soft-edge" x="-2%" y="-2%" width="104%" height="104%">
      <feGaussianBlur stdDeviation="0.4"/>
    </filter>

    <!-- One pinna (leaflet) used 30 times along the rachis -->
    <symbol id="pinna" viewBox="-60 -16 120 32">
      <path d="M -58,0 C -50,-12 -36,-15 -20,-14
               C -4,-13  12,-12  28,-10
               C 40,-7   50,-3   58,0
               C 50,3    40,7    28,10
               C 12,12   -4,13   -20,14
               C -36,15  -50,12  -58,0 Z"/>
    </symbol>
  </defs>

  <!-- ============================================================
       PAPER GROUND
       ============================================================ -->
  <rect class="ground" width="600" height="800"/>

  <!-- Subtle wash pools (slight chemical unevenness) -->
  <g>
    <circle class="wash" cx="120" cy="180" r="120"/>
    <circle class="wash" cx="480" cy="240" r="100"/>
    <circle class="wash" cx="540" cy="640" r="140"/>
    <circle class="wash" cx="80"  cy="700" r="100"/>

  <!-- Faint border (paper's natural plate-mark from the contact frame) -->
  <rect class="border" x="48" y="48" width="504" height="704"/>

## `templates/svg-illustration.svg`

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!--
  =============================================================================
  Template: svg-illustration.svg / Status: Realized starter
  Subject: HTTP request lifecycle — four-stage server-side pipeline
  Register: Schematic; left-to-right flow with one short-circuit branch
  Signature move: 4.1 honest-edge-case-on-diagram (the 401 short-circuit)
  Render env: Single-file SVG; portable across browsers and print
  =============================================================================

  CUSTOMIZE — slots to adapt when reusing this scaffold:

    1. Subject + claim. <title> and <desc> below — these are the accessible
       label and long description; they must reflect the actual diagram.
       The visible title text is the figure's thesis in one line.
    2. Stage labels. Receive / Authenticate / Route / Serialize. Four stages
       is the comfortable maximum for left-to-right flow at this canvas size;
       beyond four, switch to a vertical layout or split into two figures.
    3. Decision gate. The dashed "valid token?" branch out of Authenticate
       to the terminal 401 node is the diagram's argument — without it, this
       reduces to a linear pipeline anyone could have drawn from memory.
    4. Annotation. The italic caption below the branch names what the
       diagram shows; do not duplicate the labels above.
    5. Footer caption. Source + last updated. Keep it terse; figures earn
       their authority through the drawing, not the credits.
    6. Palette. Two grays + one accent (steel blue) + one warm (red for the
       error terminal). Do not add fourth or fifth colors; the diagram's
       legibility depends on the restraint.
-->
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     viewBox="0 0 800 460"
     role="img"
     aria-labelledby="title desc"
     font-family="Inter, system-ui, sans-serif">
  <title id="title">HTTP request lifecycle — four stages from inbound packet to response.</title>
  <desc id="desc">A left-to-right pipeline of four stages: Receive, Authenticate, Route to handler, and Serialize response. A branch from Authenticate represents the case where a token is invalid: the request short-circuits to a 401 Unauthorized terminal node, skipping Route and Serialize entirely. Arrows show the happy path through all four stages and the dashed error path to the 401 terminal.</desc>

  <defs>
    <marker id="arrow" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5"
            markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto-start-reverse">
      <path d="M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z" fill="#5B6879"/>
    </marker>
    <marker id="arrow-accent" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5"
            markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto-start-reverse">
      <path d="M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z" fill="#3663B7"/>
    </marker>
    <marker id="arrow-warm" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5"
            markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto-start-reverse">
      <path d="M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z" fill="#B73838"/>
    </marker>

    <style>
      .bg { fill: #F7F8FA; }
      .node { fill: #EDF0F5; stroke: #B5BECD; stroke-width: 1.5; }
      .node-accent { fill: oklch(94% 0.03 250); stroke: #3663B7; stroke-width: 1.5; }
      .node-terminal { fill: #2C3644; stroke: #1D252F; stroke-width: 2; }
      .node-error { fill: oklch(95% 0.03 25); stroke: #B73838; stroke-width: 1.5; }
      .edge { stroke: #5B6879; stroke-width: 1.5; fill: none;
              stroke-linejoin: round; stroke-linecap: round; }
      .edge-accent { stroke: #3663B7; stroke-width: 2; fill: none;
                     stroke-linejoin: round; stroke-linecap: round; }
      .edge-error { stroke: #B73838; stroke-width: 1.5; fill: none;
                    stroke-linejoin: round; stroke-linecap: round;
                    stroke-dasharray: 6 4; }
      .label { font-size: 14px; fill: #1D252F; font-weight: 600; }
      .label-accent { fill: #3663B7; }
      .label-error { fill: #B73838; }
      .label-meta { font-size: 11px; fill: #5B6879; }
      .label-on-dark { fill: #F7F8FA; font-weight: 600; }
      .label-meta-on-dark { font-size: 11px; fill: #B5BECD; }
      .title-text { font-size: 17px; font-weight: 650; fill: #1D252F; }
      .annotation { font-size: 12px; fill: #5B6879; font-style: italic; }
      .step-num {
        font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; fill: #8490A5;
        letter-spacing: 0.08em;
      }
      .gate { font-size: 11px; fill: #3663B7; font-style: italic; }
      .gate-error { font-size: 11px; fill: #B73838; font-style: italic; font-weight: 600; }

      @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
        .bg { fill: #10161D; }
        .node { fill: #1D252F; stroke: #3F4B5C; }
        .node-accent { fill: oklch(24% 0.06 250); stroke: oklch(75% 0.15 250); }
        .node-terminal { fill: #B5BECD; stroke: #EDF0F5; }
        .node-error { fill: oklch(24% 0.06 25); stroke: oklch(75% 0.15 25); }
        .edge { stroke: #8490A5; }
        .edge-accent { stroke: oklch(75% 0.15 250); }
        .edge-error { stroke: oklch(75% 0.15 25); }
        .label { fill: #EDF0F5; }
        .label-accent { fill: oklch(80% 0.12 250); }
        .label-error { fill: oklch(80% 0.14 25); }
        .label-meta { fill: #8490A5; }
        .label-on-dark { fill: #10161D; }
        .label-meta-on-dark { fill: #3F4B5C; }
        .title-text { fill: #EDF0F5; }
        .annotation { fill: #8490A5; }
        .gate { fill: oklch(80% 0.12 250); }
        .gate-error { fill: oklch(80% 0.14 25); }
      }
    </style>
  </defs>

  <rect class="bg" x="0" y="0" width="800" height="460"/>

  <text class="title-text" x="40" y="40">
    HTTP request lifecycle — four stages from inbound packet to response.
  </text>
  <text class="label-meta" x="40" y="60">
    Authentication gates the next two stages; an invalid token short-circuits to 401.
  </text>

  <!-- Inbound -->
  <g id="inbound">
    <circle cx="50" cy="200" r="14" fill="#5B6879"/>
    <text class="label-meta" x="50" y="234" text-anchor="middle">inbound</text>
    <text class="label-meta" x="50" y="248" text-anchor="middle">packet</text>
  </g>
  <path class="edge" d="M 66 200 L 109 200" marker-end="url(#arrow)"/>

  <!-- Stage 1: Receive -->
  <g>
    <rect class="node" x="110" y="160" width="140" height="80" rx="8"/>
    <text class="step-num" x="180" y="180" text-anchor="middle">STAGE 01</text>
    <text class="label" x="180" y="204" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle">
      Receive
    </text>
    <text class="label-meta" x="180" y="226" text-anchor="middle">parse headers, body</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Stage 1 -> 2 -->
  <path class="edge" d="M 250 200 L 309 200" marker-end="url(#arrow)"/>

  <!-- Stage 2: Authenticate (decision point, accented) -->
  <g>
    <rect class="node-accent" x="310" y="160" width="160" height="80" rx="8"/>
    <text class="step-num" x="390" y="180" text-anchor="middle" style="fill: #3663B7;">STAGE 02 · GATE</text>
    <text class="label label-accent" x="390" y="204" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle">
      Authenticate
    </text>
    <text class="label-meta" x="390" y="226" text-anchor="middle">verify token signature</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Gate label on the happy path -->
  <text class="gate" x="500" y="194" text-anchor="middle">valid token</text>

  <!-- Stage 2 -> 3 (happy path) -->
  <path class="edge-accent" d="M 470 200 L 529 200" marker-end="url(#arrow-accent)"/>

  <!-- Stage 3: Route -->
  <g>
    <rect class="node" x="530" y="160" width="140" height="80" rx="8"/>
    <text class="step-num" x="600" y="180" text-anchor="middle">STAGE 03</text>
    <text class="label" x="600" y="204" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle">
      Route to handler
    </text>
    <text class="label-meta" x="600" y="226" text-anchor="middle">match path, dispatch</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Stage 4: Serialize -->
  <g>
    <rect class="node" x="600" y="290" width="140" height="80" rx="8"/>
    <text class="step-num" x="670" y="310" text-anchor="middle">STAGE 04</text>
    <text class="label" x="670" y="334" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle">
      Serialize response
    </text>
    <text class="label-meta" x="670" y="356" text-anchor="middle">encode body, headers</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Stage 3 -> Stage 4 (vertical drop) -->
  <path class="edge" d="M 670 240 L 670 285" marker-end="url(#arrow)"/>

  <!-- Outbound from Serialize -->
  <g>
    <circle cx="780" cy="330" r="14" fill="#3663B7"/>
    <text class="label-meta" x="780" y="364" text-anchor="middle">200 OK</text>
    <text class="label-meta" x="780" y="378" text-anchor="middle">to client</text>
  </g>
  <path class="edge-accent" d="M 740 330 L 765 330" marker-end="url(#arrow-accent)"/>

  <!-- Short-circuit: 401 branch out of Authenticate -->
  <text class="gate-error" x="390" y="276" text-anchor="middle">invalid token · short-circuit</text>
  <path class="edge-error"
        d="M 390 240 L 390 330 L 519 330"
        marker-end="url(#arrow-warm)"/>

  <!-- 401 terminal -->
  <g>
    <rect class="node-error" x="520" y="300" width="80" height="60" rx="8"/>
    <text class="label label-error" x="560" y="324" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle">
      401
    </text>
    <text class="label-meta" x="560" y="346" text-anchor="middle" style="fill: #B73838;">unauthorized</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Caption / annotation -->
  <text class="annotation" x="40" y="420">
    If authentication fails, the request short-circuits to a 401 — Route and Serialize do not run.
  </text>
  <text class="label-meta" x="40" y="440">
    Source: server-side HTTP pipeline as commonly implemented in Express, Rails, FastAPI, and equivalents. Updated 2026-05-24.
  </text>
</svg>
```

## `templates/svg-lachman-test.svg`

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!--
  =============================================================================
  Template: svg-lachman-test.svg / Status: Realized starter
  Subject: Lachman test for ACL integrity — three-panel triptych showing
           positioning, maneuver, and interpretation. Knee at 20-30° flexion;
           examiner stabilizes distal femur and translates proximal tibia
           anteriorly; soft endpoint or excess translation = positive.
  Register: 17 Physical-exam maneuver plate
  Exemplars: Stanley Hoppenfeld, Physical Examination of the Spine and
             Extremities (1976), Hugh Thomas line-drawing conventions;
             David Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (7th ed., 2021),
             evidence-paired maneuvers; Frank Netter, Atlas of Human Anatomy
             and Netter's Orthopaedic Clinical Examination (Cleland).
             Sensitivity / specificity values from Benjaminse et al. 2006
             systematic review (Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical
             Therapy).
  Signature move: triptych-of-maneuver (Register 17 convention) — positioning
                  frame + maneuver frame + interpretation frame composed as
                  one plate; force-vector arrows carry magnitude annotation;
                  interpretation panel pairs the maneuver to published
                  diagnostic accuracy values.
  Render env: Single-file SVG; portable across browsers and print
  Pairs with: references/medium-playbooks/svg-illustration.md (Register 17);
              references/medium-playbooks/clinical-case.md (case
              integration); templates/clinical-pearl-card.md (pearl-card
              register).
  =============================================================================

  CUSTOMIZE — slots to adapt when reusing this scaffold:

    1. Maneuver. Replace the Lachman geometry with the target test:
         - Hawkins-Kennedy (shoulder impingement): shoulder at 90° forward
           flexion, internal rotation force at the wrist.
         - Spurling (cervical radiculopathy): axial-compression vector on
           an extended-rotated neck.
         - FABER (sacroiliac / hip): flexion-abduction-external-rotation
           position with downward pressure at the medial knee.
         - McMurray (meniscus): tibial rotation + valgus/varus stress at
           varying flexion angles.
       Each follows the same triptych: position → maneuver → interpretation.
    2. Anatomy. The knee is stylized lateral view, ~25° flexion. For other
       joints, redraw the relevant anatomy at the relevant test position.
       Maintain the convention: the anatomy is *drawn* (vector), not
       photographed; the body is schematic but anatomically literate.
    3. Color vocabulary (medical convention — carries over from Register 16):
         - Nerve:           #FFD700  (gold / yellow)
         - Artery:          #C8102E  (red — also used here for force vectors)
         - Vein:            #0066CC  (blue)
         - Ligament/tendon: #2E8B57  (forest green — for intact reference)
         - Fracture line:   #FFFFFF  with stroke-dasharray="5 3"
         - Tumor/lesion:    #C71585  (magenta)
         - Implant:         #00CED1  (cyan)
       Force vectors use a heavier red stroke (3-4px) with arrowhead;
       magnitude annotation sits at the arrow's origin or above the shaft.
    4. Examiner-hand glyphs. Conventionally drawn as a stylized C-shape
       or grasping outline showing palm + fingers; placement indicates
       grip (stabilizing vs. translating). Keep schematic; the hand's
       function is signaled by position, not by anatomical detail.
    5. Interpretation panel. Always includes:
         - Sensitivity (Sn), Specificity (Sp)
         - Positive likelihood ratio (LR+), Negative likelihood ratio (LR−)
         - Positive-test criteria (what counts as a positive result)
         - Cite the source of the diagnostic-accuracy values (e.g.,
           Benjaminse 2006 meta-analysis for Lachman).
         - Composite-test note: which other tests pair with this one.
    6. Endpoint vocabulary. "Soft endpoint" / "firm endpoint" is ligament-
       specific examiner-fluency language; for other tests substitute the
       appropriate vocabulary ("apprehension" for instability, "reproduces
       pain" for impingement, etc.).
-->
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     viewBox="0 0 1080 680"
     role="img"
     aria-labelledby="title desc"
     font-family="Source Serif Pro, Georgia, serif">
  <title id="title">The Lachman test for ACL integrity — positioning, maneuver, and interpretation triptych.</title>
  <desc id="desc">A three-panel physical-exam reference plate for the Lachman test, used to assess anterior cruciate ligament integrity. Panel one, on the left, shows positioning: the patient supine with the knee passively flexed to twenty to thirty degrees, the examiner standing at the lateral side, one hand stabilizing the distal femur from above and the other hand cupping the proximal tibia from below. Panel two, in the center, shows the maneuver: a gentle anteriorly directed force applied to the proximal posterior tibia while the femur is held stable, producing anterior tibial translation. A ghosted secondary outline shows the tibia's translated position; the translation distance is measured with a yellow caliper. The intact anterior cruciate ligament is traced in green for reference; a torn ligament would offer no resistance to the translation force. Panel three, on the right, is the interpretation panel: sensitivity 85 percent, specificity 94 percent, positive likelihood ratio 14.2, negative likelihood ratio 0.16 from the Benjaminse 2006 meta-analysis. Positive-test criteria are excess anterior translation compared with the contralateral knee, or a soft mushy endpoint. A composite-testing note recommends pairing with the pivot-shift and anterior drawer for ACL evaluation.</desc>

  <defs>
    <style>
      .ground          { fill: #F4ECDC; }
      .panel-bg        { fill: #FAF5E7; }
      .panel-rule      { stroke: #C7BC9F; stroke-width: 0.6; fill: none; }
      .ink             { stroke: #1F1A14; fill: none; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; }
      .ink-body        { stroke-width: 1.4; }
      .ink-fine        { stroke-width: 0.7; }
      .ink-hair        { stroke-width: 0.4; opacity: 0.85; }
      .skin            { fill: #E8D2B0; }
      .skin-shadow     { fill: #C8AB80; opacity: 0.65; }
      .bone            { fill: #F0E5CC; }
      .bone-stroke     { stroke: #1F1A14; stroke-width: 1.2; fill: #F0E5CC; }
      .bone-cancel     { fill: #D8C9A6; opacity: 0.85; }
      .bone-ghost      { fill: none; stroke: #1F1A14; stroke-width: 0.8; stroke-dasharray: 3 2; opacity: 0.55; }
      .ligament        { stroke: #2E8B57; stroke-width: 2.5; fill: none; stroke-linecap: round; }
      .ligament-fine   { stroke: #2E8B57; stroke-width: 1.5; fill: none; stroke-linecap: round; opacity: 0.85; }
      .force-vec       { stroke: #C8102E; stroke-width: 3.5; fill: none; stroke-linecap: round; }
      .stabilize       { stroke: #1F1A14; stroke-width: 1.8; fill: none; stroke-linecap: round; opacity: 0.9; }
      .caliper         { stroke: #FFD700; stroke-width: 1.2; fill: none; }

      .panel-label     { font-size: 10px; fill: #6B5F4A; font-variant: small-caps;
                         letter-spacing: 0.16em; font-weight: 600; }
      .panel-title     { font-size: 14px; fill: #1F1A14; font-weight: 600;
                         letter-spacing: 0.04em; }
      .anatomy         { font-size: 10px; fill: #4A4234; font-style: italic; }
      .force-label     { font-size: 11px; fill: #C8102E; font-weight: 600; }
      .meas-label      { font-size: 11px; fill: #B89000; font-weight: 600; }
      .endpoint-label  { font-size: 10.5px; fill: #1F1A14; }
      .endpoint-pos    { fill: #C8102E; font-weight: 600; }
      .endpoint-neg    { fill: #2E8B57; font-weight: 600; }
      .leader          { stroke: #6B5F4A; stroke-width: 0.4; fill: none; opacity: 0.85; }

      .stat-value      { font-size: 22px; fill: #1F1A14; font-weight: 700;
                         font-family: Inter, sans-serif; }
      .stat-key        { font-size: 10px; fill: #6B5F4A; font-variant: small-caps;
                         letter-spacing: 0.12em; font-family: Inter, sans-serif; }
      .stat-context    { font-size: 10px; fill: #4A4234; font-style: italic; }

      .interpret-h     { font-size: 11px; fill: #1F1A14; font-weight: 600;
                         font-variant: small-caps; letter-spacing: 0.08em; }

      .interpret-meta  { font-size: 9.5px; fill: #6B5F4A; font-style: italic; }

      .caption         { font-size: 11px; fill: #1F1A14; font-variant: small-caps;
                         letter-spacing: 0.14em; }
      .meta            { font-size: 9.5px; fill: #6B5F4A; font-variant: small-caps;
                         letter-spacing: 0.10em; }
    </style>

    <marker id="force-arrow" viewBox="0 0 12 12" refX="10" refY="6"
            markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" orient="auto">
      <path d="M 0,0 L 12,6 L 0,12 L 3,6 Z" fill="#C8102E"/>
    </marker>
    <marker id="caliper-tick" viewBox="0 0 6 6" refX="3" refY="3"
            markerWidth="5" markerHeight="5" orient="auto">
      <line x1="3" y1="0" x2="3" y2="6" stroke="#B89000" stroke-width="0.9"/>
    </marker>
    <marker id="ghost-arrow" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5"
            markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto">
      <path d="M 0,0 L 10,5 L 0,10 Z" fill="#1F1A14" opacity="0.55"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>

  <rect class="ground" width="1080" height="680"/>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       HEADER
       =================================================================== -->
  <text x="60" y="50" font-size="20" fill="#1F1A14" font-weight="600">
    The Lachman test for anterior cruciate ligament integrity.
  </text>
  <text x="60" y="72" font-size="12" fill="#4A4234" font-style="italic">
    Position the knee at 20–30° flexion, apply gentle anterior translation to the proximal tibia,
    read endpoint quality and translation magnitude against the contralateral knee.
  </text>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       PANEL 1 — POSITIONING
       Knee at 20-30° flexion; examiner stabilizes femur and cups tibia.
       =================================================================== -->
  <rect class="panel-bg" x="40" y="100" width="320" height="440" rx="3"/>
  <rect class="panel-rule" x="40" y="100" width="320" height="440" rx="3"/>

  <text x="56" y="124" class="panel-label">PANEL 1 · POSITIONING</text>
  <text x="56" y="148" class="panel-title">Patient supine; knee passively flexed 20–30°.</text>

  <g id="panel-1-anatomy" transform="translate(56, 200)">
    <!-- Thigh (femoral segment) -->
    <path class="skin"
          d="M 0,30 Q 0,10 30,8 L 168,8 Q 196,16 200,40 Q 196,68 168,72 L 30,72 Q 0,70 0,50 Z"/>
    <path class="skin-shadow"
          d="M 8,52 Q 30,66 80,68 L 152,66 Q 186,62 196,52 L 196,68 Q 168,72 30,72 Q 8,68 8,52 Z"/>
    <!-- Femur silhouette inside the thigh -->
    <rect class="bone-stroke" x="20" y="30" width="160" height="20" rx="4"/>
    <ellipse class="bone-stroke" cx="180" cy="40" rx="22" ry="22"/>

    <!-- Knee joint (transition + tibial segment) -->
    <!-- The knee joint at the proximal tibia, ~25° flexion -->
    <g transform="translate(200, 16) rotate(25)">
      <!-- Tibial-segment skin -->
      <path class="skin"
            d="M 0,30 Q 0,10 28,8 L 162,8 Q 188,16 192,38 Q 188,62 162,66 L 28,66 Q 0,64 0,46 Z"/>
      <path class="skin-shadow"
            d="M 6,48 Q 28,60 80,62 L 148,60 Q 180,56 188,48 L 188,62 Q 162,66 28,66 Q 6,62 6,48 Z"/>
      <!-- Tibial plateau + shaft -->
      <ellipse class="bone-stroke" cx="14" cy="38" rx="20" ry="20"/>
      <rect class="bone-stroke" x="30" y="26" width="152" height="20" rx="4"/>
    </g>

    <!-- Foot stylized -->
    <g transform="translate(376, 152)">
      <path class="skin" d="M 0,0 Q 4,-12 24,-14 L 56,-14 Q 70,-10 70,8 Q 60,18 32,16 L 8,14 Q 0,12 0,0 Z"/>
    </g>

    <!-- Examiner's stabilizing hand on distal femur (above) -->
    <g transform="translate(146, -28)">
      <!-- Stylized palm + fingers (C-shape grasping) -->
      <path class="stabilize"
            d="M 0,0 Q 4,-22 28,-26 L 58,-26 Q 84,-22 86,-2 Q 80,18 56,22 Q 28,20 0,16 Z"/>
      <!-- Finger creases -->
      <path class="ink-hair" d="M 18,-12 Q 22,-6 26,-2 M 36,-18 Q 40,-12 44,-8 M 54,-20 Q 58,-14 62,-10"/>
      <text x="44" y="-36" class="anatomy" text-anchor="middle">stabilizing hand</text>
      <text x="44" y="-48" class="anatomy" fill="#6B5F4A" text-anchor="middle">distal femur</text>
    </g>

    <!-- Examiner's translating hand cupping proximal tibia (below) -->
    <g transform="translate(206, 124) rotate(20)">
      <path class="stabilize"
            d="M 0,0 Q 4,22 28,26 L 58,26 Q 84,22 86,2 Q 80,-18 56,-22 Q 28,-20 0,-16 Z"/>
      <path class="ink-hair" d="M 18,12 Q 22,6 26,2 M 36,18 Q 40,12 44,8 M 54,20 Q 58,14 62,10"/>
    </g>
    <text x="280" y="186" class="anatomy">cupping hand · proximal tibia</text>

    <!-- Flexion-angle annotation -->
    <g transform="translate(196, 32)">
      <path class="leader" d="M 0,0 L 30,12" stroke-dasharray="2 2"/>
      <path class="leader" d="M 0,0 L 34,-2" stroke-dasharray="2 2"/>
      <path d="M 16,-2 A 18 18 0 0 1 18,8" stroke="#1F1A14" stroke-width="0.6" fill="none"/>
      <text x="32" y="6" class="anatomy">≈ 25°</text>
    </g>
  </g>

  <!-- Panel 1 caption -->
  <text x="56" y="466" class="endpoint-label">
    The examiner stands to the lateral side, knee at the level of their own hip.
  </text>
  <text x="56" y="484" class="interpret-meta">
    Smaller hands: rest patient's thigh on the examiner's thigh to free both hands. Large patients:
  </text>
  <text x="56" y="498" class="interpret-meta">
    rotate to the prone Lachman or use the modified-Lachman variant.
  </text>
  <text x="56" y="522" class="meta">Position · Stabilize · Translate</text>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       PANEL 2 — MANEUVER
       Anterior-translation force on proximal tibia; ghost shows result.
       =================================================================== -->
  <rect class="panel-bg" x="380" y="100" width="320" height="440" rx="3"/>
  <rect class="panel-rule" x="380" y="100" width="320" height="440" rx="3"/>

  <text x="396" y="124" class="panel-label">PANEL 2 · MANEUVER</text>
  <text x="396" y="148" class="panel-title">Anterior translation; read endpoint and excursion.</text>

  <g id="panel-2-mechanics" transform="translate(396, 220)">
    <!-- Femur (stable, fixed reference) -->
    <rect class="bone-stroke" x="0" y="0" width="160" height="20" rx="4"/>
    <ellipse class="bone-stroke" cx="160" cy="10" rx="22" ry="22"/>

    <!-- ACL (intact reference, green) — anatomically anchored from
         lateral femoral condyle to anterior tibial spine. With intact ACL,
         translation is limited (firm endpoint). -->
    <path class="ligament" d="M 168,18 Q 178,42 192,66"/>

    <!-- PCL (drawn fine, for completeness) -->
    <path class="ligament-fine" d="M 152,18 Q 168,42 188,66"/>

    <!-- Tibia (current resting position, solid) -->
    <g id="tibia-rest">
      <ellipse class="bone-stroke" cx="192" cy="76" rx="20" ry="20"/>
      <rect class="bone-stroke" x="208" y="64" width="150" height="20" rx="4"/>
    </g>

    <!-- Ghosted "after translation" position, offset anteriorly (left) -->
    <g id="tibia-ghost">
      <ellipse class="bone-ghost" cx="180" cy="76" rx="20" ry="20"/>
      <rect class="bone-ghost" x="196" y="64" width="150" height="20" rx="4"/>
      <!-- Motion-arrow connecting rest -> ghost -->
      <path d="M 198,76 L 188,76" stroke="#1F1A14" stroke-width="0.8" stroke-dasharray="2 2"
            fill="none" marker-end="url(#ghost-arrow)" opacity="0.7"/>
    </g>

    <!-- Force vector: anterior, gentle. Applied to the posterior aspect of
         the proximal tibia, directed anteriorly. -->
    <path class="force-vec" d="M 248,108 L 192,90" marker-end="url(#force-arrow)"/>
    <text x="252" y="124" class="force-label">anterior force</text>
    <text x="252" y="138" class="force-label" fill="#A0152A">gentle, sustained</text>

    <!-- Caliper measuring translation -->
    <line class="caliper" x1="180" y1="40" x2="192" y2="40"
          marker-start="url(#caliper-tick)" marker-end="url(#caliper-tick)"/>
    <text x="186" y="32" class="meas-label" text-anchor="middle">Δ translation</text>
    <text x="186" y="22" class="meas-label" text-anchor="middle" fill="#B89000">vs. contralateral</text>

    <!-- Labels -->
    <text x="-8" y="-12" class="anatomy" text-anchor="end" fill="#2E8B57">ACL · intact</text>
    <line class="leader" x1="-6" y1="-10" x2="172" y2="20"/>

    <text x="364" y="58" class="anatomy" fill="#1F1A14">tibia (resting)</text>
    <text x="364" y="100" class="anatomy" fill="#6B5F4A" opacity="0.85">tibia (translated · ghosted)</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Endpoint reading legend (within Panel 2) -->
  <g transform="translate(396, 410)">
    <text x="0" y="0" class="interpret-h">Endpoint quality</text>
    <line x1="0" y1="8" x2="288" y2="8" stroke="#C7BC9F" stroke-width="0.4"/>
    <text x="0" y="28" class="endpoint-label">
      <tspan class="endpoint-neg">Firm endpoint</tspan> — translation halts crisply.
    </text>
    <text x="0" y="44" class="endpoint-label" fill="#4A4234">
      Intact or near-intact ACL. <tspan font-style="italic">Negative test.</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="0" y="64" class="endpoint-label">
      <tspan class="endpoint-pos">Soft / mushy endpoint</tspan> — translation continues, no firm stop.
    </text>
    <text x="0" y="80" class="endpoint-label" fill="#4A4234">
      ACL disruption (partial or complete). <tspan font-style="italic">Positive test.</tspan>
    </text>
    <text x="0" y="104" class="endpoint-label">
      Excess translation alone (≥ 3 mm vs. contralateral) is also positive,
    </text>
    <text x="0" y="118" class="endpoint-label">
      even with apparently firm endpoint.
    </text>
  </g>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       PANEL 3 — INTERPRETATION
       Sn / Sp / LR+ / LR- + positive criteria + composite-test note.
       =================================================================== -->
  <rect class="panel-bg" x="720" y="100" width="320" height="440" rx="3"/>
  <rect class="panel-rule" x="720" y="100" width="320" height="440" rx="3"/>

  <text x="736" y="124" class="panel-label">PANEL 3 · INTERPRETATION</text>
  <text x="736" y="148" class="panel-title">Diagnostic accuracy and criteria.</text>

  <!-- Stat grid (2 x 2 of headline values) -->
  <g transform="translate(736, 190)">
    <!-- Sensitivity -->
    <g>
      <text x="0" y="0" class="stat-key">SENSITIVITY</text>
      <text x="0" y="34" class="stat-value">85%</text>
      <text x="0" y="50" class="stat-context">of true ACL tears called positive</text>
    </g>
    <!-- Specificity -->
    <g transform="translate(150, 0)">
      <text x="0" y="0" class="stat-key">SPECIFICITY</text>
      <text x="0" y="34" class="stat-value">94%</text>
      <text x="0" y="50" class="stat-context">of intact ACLs called negative</text>
    </g>
    <!-- LR+ -->
    <g transform="translate(0, 88)">
      <text x="0" y="0" class="stat-key">LR+</text>
      <text x="0" y="34" class="stat-value">14.2</text>
      <text x="0" y="50" class="stat-context">positive: large rule-in shift</text>
    </g>
    <!-- LR- -->
    <g transform="translate(150, 88)">
      <text x="0" y="0" class="stat-key">LR−</text>
      <text x="0" y="34" class="stat-value">0.16</text>
      <text x="0" y="50" class="stat-context">negative: moderate rule-out shift</text>
    </g>
  </g>

  <line x1="736" y1="362" x2="1024" y2="362" stroke="#C7BC9F" stroke-width="0.4"/>

  <text x="736" y="384" class="interpret-h">Positive criteria</text>
  <text x="736" y="404" class="interpret-body">
    <tspan font-weight="600">Either</tspan> soft / mushy endpoint
  </text>
  <text x="736" y="420" class="interpret-body">
    <tspan font-weight="600">or</tspan> excess anterior translation
  </text>
  <text x="736" y="436" class="interpret-body">
    (≥ 3 mm vs. contralateral knee).
  </text>

  <text x="736" y="464" class="interpret-h">Composite-test pairing</text>
  <text x="736" y="484" class="interpret-body">
    Pair with the <tspan font-style="italic">pivot-shift</tspan>
    (Sn 24% · Sp 98%)
  </text>
  <text x="736" y="500" class="interpret-body">
    and <tspan font-style="italic">anterior drawer</tspan>
    (Sn 55% · Sp 92%).
  </text>
  <text x="736" y="520" class="interpret-meta">
    Lachman is the most sensitive single test; pivot-shift is the most
  </text>
  <text x="736" y="534" class="interpret-meta">
    specific. Triad inference is more reliable than any one alone.
  </text>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       FOOTER — caption + evidence source + the cross-test recommendation
       =================================================================== -->
  <line x1="40" y1="568" x2="1040" y2="568" stroke="#C7BC9F" stroke-width="0.5"/>

  <text x="540" y="592" class="caption" text-anchor="middle">
    Plate III — Knee · Lachman Test
  </text>
  <text x="540" y="610" class="meta" text-anchor="middle">
    Sn / Sp / LR values: Benjaminse et al., JOSPT 2006 · meta-analysis of 17 studies, anesthetized + awake examination
  </text>
  <text x="540" y="626" class="meta" text-anchor="middle">
    Convention after Hoppenfeld (1976) · Magee (2021) · Netter's Orthopaedic Clinical Examination (Cleland)
  </text>
  <text x="540" y="650" class="meta" text-anchor="middle" fill="#8A7B62">
    Reference plate · Pair with imaging when the clinical picture is equivocal
  </text>
</svg>
```

## `templates/svg-mri-annotated.svg`

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!--
  =============================================================================
  Template: svg-mri-annotated.svg / Status: Realized starter
  Subject: Sagittal T2 knee MRI with partial-thickness mid-substance ACL tear,
           intact distal fibers; magenta lesion outline, green ligament
           reference, caliper measurement, sequence metadata, orientation.
  Register: 16 Medical-imaging overlay
  Exemplars: Stoller, Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Orthopaedics and Sports
             Medicine (3rd ed., 2007) — the ACL chapter as the convention
             atlas; Radsource MRI Web Clinic (radsource.us) — case-of-the-
             month annotation style; Bencardino et al., Skeletal Radiology
             ACL imaging review (2009).
  Signature move: medical-color-vocabulary (Register 16 convention) — green
                  for intact ligament reference, magenta for the lesion
                  outline, yellow for measurement caliper, white for sequence
                  / orientation metadata. The MRI's greyscale gradient is
                  the load-bearing image; vector overlay disambiguates the
                  finding without obscuring the underlying signal.
  Render env: Single-file SVG; portable across browsers and print
  Pairs with: references/medium-playbooks/svg-illustration.md (Register 16);
              references/libraries/medical-artifacts.md (MRI conventions);
              templates/svg-radiograph-overlay.svg (sibling Register-16
              example in a different modality).
  =============================================================================

  CUSTOMIZE — slots to adapt when reusing this scaffold:

    1. Imaging modality. This template uses a stylized greyscale sagittal-knee
       MRI built from vector gradients (T2-weighted: high-signal fluid in
       white, cortical bone in black, marrow fat in mid-gray, fibrocartilage
       in dark gray). In production, replace the <g id="pseudo-mri"> block
       with an <image href="sag-t2-knee.png" opacity="0.92"/> element
       pointing to a real DICOM-derived PNG. Re-anchor the ACL overlay to
       the actual ACL on your image.
    2. Anatomy + finding. The finding shown is a partial-thickness mid-
       substance ACL tear with intact distal fibers — a common reading.
       To adapt to other findings:
         - Meniscus tear: replace ACL overlay with meniscal triangle in
           the slice; use magenta for the tear cleft.
         - Bone marrow edema: replace lesion outline with magenta diffuse
           shading over the affected marrow.
         - Cartilage defect: use cyan to outline the chondral lesion.
       The color discipline holds across findings.
    3. Color vocabulary (medical convention — do not invent):
         - Nerve:           #FFD700  (gold / yellow)
         - Artery:          #C8102E  (red)
         - Vein:            #0066CC  (blue)
         - Ligament/tendon: #2E8B57  (forest green — intact reference)
         - Fracture line:   #FFFFFF  with stroke-dasharray="5 3"
         - Tumor/lesion:    #C71585  (magenta — for tear, lesion, edema)
         - Implant:         #00CED1  (cyan)
       Use green for the *intact* anatomy you are referencing; magenta
       for the *pathology* you are flagging.
    4. Measurement caliper. The yellow caliper convention is the same as
       radiograph templating — two tick caps with a connecting line, value
       label above or beside. For volumetric measurements (lesion volume,
       tumor diameter on three axes), draw three calipers in three planes.
    5. Sequence / protocol metadata. Top-right corner convention. Include:
       sequence (T1 / T2 / PD / STIR / DWI), plane (sagittal / coronal /
       axial), field strength (1.5T / 3T), and any contrast (post-Gd,
       fat-saturated, etc.). This is the radiologist's first-glance data.
    6. Orientation marker. Sagittal knee: A (anterior) and P (posterior)
       at the top corners; right or left knee in the corner. The reader
       must never have to guess orientation.
-->
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     viewBox="0 0 680 820"
     role="img"
     aria-labelledby="title desc"
     font-family="Inter, system-ui, sans-serif">
  <title id="title">Sagittal T2 knee MRI showing a partial-thickness mid-substance ACL tear, distal fibers intact.</title>
  <desc id="desc">A sagittal T2-weighted magnetic resonance image of the right knee, showing the femur, tibia, patella, quadriceps and patellar tendons, anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments, and the menisci in cross-section. The anterior cruciate ligament is traced in green along its normal Blumensaat-line course from the lateral femoral condyle to the anterior tibial spine. A focal region of abnormal high signal in the mid-substance is outlined in magenta — a partial-thickness tear approximately 9 millimeters in craniocaudal extent. The distal one-third of the ACL is intact and remains continuous with the tibial footprint. A yellow caliper at the lesion measures the tear extent. Sequence metadata in the upper right reads sagittal T2 fat-saturated at 3 Tesla. Orientation markers A and P appear at the upper corners along with the side marker R. A caption at the foot documents the finding, the differential consideration, and the recommended next imaging step.</desc>

  <defs>
    <!-- T2 greyscale gradients for the pseudo-MRI -->
    <radialGradient id="marrow" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="50%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#A8A39A"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#6E6A60"/>
    </radialGradient>
    <linearGradient id="cortex" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#0A0A0A"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A1A"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <radialGradient id="muscle" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="60%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#4A463E"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#36322C"/>
    </radialGradient>
    <radialGradient id="fluid" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="60%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#F8F4E8"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#D4CFC2"/>
    </radialGradient>
    <!-- The lesion's abnormal high signal (T2-bright fluid signal within the ACL) -->
    <radialGradient id="lesion-signal" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="50%">
      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#E8E2D0"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#857F70"/>
    </radialGradient>

    <style>
      .ground          { fill: #050505; }
      .label           { font-size: 10.5px; fill: #F0F0F0; font-weight: 500; }
      .label-orient    { font-size: 16px; fill: #FFFFFF; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.05em; }
      .label-side      { font-size: 11px; fill: #FFFFFF; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; }
      .label-seq       { font-size: 10px; fill: #DCDCDC; letter-spacing: 0.06em; font-weight: 500; }
      .label-anatomy   { font-size: 9.5px; fill: #C8C8C8; font-style: italic; }
      .label-finding   { font-size: 11px; fill: #FF7CD0; font-weight: 600; }
      .label-ref       { font-size: 10px; fill: #6FE0A0; font-weight: 500; }
      .label-meas      { font-size: 11px; fill: #FFD700; font-weight: 600; }
      .leader          { stroke: #C8C8C8; stroke-width: 0.5; fill: none; opacity: 0.85; }
      .ligament        { stroke: #2E8B57; stroke-width: 2.5; fill: none; stroke-linecap: round; }
      .ligament-ref    { stroke: #2E8B57; stroke-width: 1.5; fill: none; stroke-linecap: round;
                         stroke-dasharray: 3 2; opacity: 0.85; }
      .lesion          { stroke: #C71585; stroke-width: 1.8; fill: none; stroke-dasharray: 4 2; }
      .caliper         { stroke: #FFD700; stroke-width: 1.0; fill: none; }
      .caption-title   { font-size: 13px; fill: #F0F0F0; font-weight: 600; }
      .caption-finding { font-size: 11px; fill: #FF7CD0; font-weight: 600; }
      .caption-meta    { font-size: 10px; fill: #B0B0B0; }
    </style>

    <marker id="caliper-tick" viewBox="0 0 6 6" refX="3" refY="3"
            markerWidth="5" markerHeight="5" orient="auto">
      <line x1="3" y1="0" x2="3" y2="6" stroke="#FFD700" stroke-width="0.9"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>

  <rect class="ground" x="0" y="0" width="680" height="820"/>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       PSEUDO-MRI — vector substitute for the raster DICOM image
       IN PRODUCTION: replace this entire block with
         <image href="sag-t2-knee.png" x="80" y="80" width="520" height="600" opacity="0.92"/>
       =================================================================== -->
  <g id="pseudo-mri" transform="translate(80, 80)">
    <!-- Soft-tissue background (T2 muscle ~ mid-gray) -->
    <rect width="520" height="600" fill="url(#muscle)"/>

    <!-- ===== FEMUR — distal end, lateral condyle visible in sagittal ===== -->
    <!-- Cortex: black outline -->
    <path fill="#0A0A0A"
          d="M 60,40 L 380,40 L 380,180 Q 370,210 350,232 Q 320,260 280,272
             Q 240,278 200,272 Q 160,260 132,232 Q 110,200 110,160 L 60,160 Z"/>
    <!-- Marrow: gradient mid-gray with fatty high-signal regions -->
    <path fill="url(#marrow)"
          d="M 72,52 L 368,52 L 368,176 Q 358,204 342,222 Q 314,248 280,260
             Q 240,266 200,260 Q 164,248 140,224 Q 122,200 122,158 L 72,158 Z"/>
    <!-- Trochlear groove notch (where ACL attaches to lateral femoral condyle) -->
    <path fill="#0A0A0A" d="M 220,240 Q 240,260 270,260 Q 240,268 220,260 Z"/>

    <!-- ===== TIBIA — proximal end, plateau and shaft ===== -->
    <!-- Cortex -->
    <path fill="#0A0A0A"
          d="M 120,360 Q 160,348 220,348 L 360,348 Q 380,360 380,400 L 380,600 L 200,600 L 200,460
             Q 180,440 160,420 Q 130,400 120,380 Z"/>
    <!-- Marrow -->
    <path fill="url(#marrow)"
          d="M 132,372 Q 168,360 224,360 L 348,360 Q 368,372 368,400 L 368,588 L 212,588 L 212,460
             Q 194,442 174,422 Q 144,402 132,384 Z"/>
    <!-- Tibial plateau cartilage surface -->
    <path fill="#5C5650" d="M 132,348 Q 200,340 280,340 Q 340,340 360,348 L 360,360 L 132,360 Z"/>

    <!-- ===== PATELLA (anterior) ===== -->
    <ellipse cx="36" cy="240" rx="22" ry="40" fill="#0A0A0A"/>
    <ellipse cx="36" cy="240" rx="16" ry="34" fill="url(#marrow)"/>

    <!-- ===== PATELLAR TENDON ===== -->
    <path fill="#1F1B16" d="M 40,280 L 60,280 L 80,340 L 60,346 Z"/>
    <path fill="none" stroke="#0A0A0A" stroke-width="1" d="M 40,280 L 60,280 L 80,340 L 60,346 Z"/>

    <!-- ===== QUADRICEPS TENDON ===== -->
    <path fill="#1F1B16" d="M 32,200 L 56,200 L 56,90 L 36,90 Z"/>

    <!-- ===== MENISCI — anterior and posterior horns in cross-section ===== -->
    <!-- Anterior horn (lateral, hyperintense margin = degenerative signal) -->
    <path fill="#0A0A0A" d="M 168,344 L 200,344 L 192,358 L 176,358 Z"/>
    <!-- Posterior horn -->
    <path fill="#0A0A0A" d="M 300,344 L 340,344 L 332,358 L 312,358 Z"/>

    <!-- ===== POSTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT (PCL — intact reference) ===== -->
    <!-- The PCL appears as a low-signal dark band -->
    <path fill="#070707"
          d="M 290,260 Q 304,290 314,320 Q 320,340 326,348 L 310,348 Q 304,340 296,324 Q 282,294 274,266 Z"/>

    <!-- ===== ACL — drawn as the low-signal substrate -->
    <!-- The ACL's normal low-signal appearance — a dark band running from lateral
         femoral condyle to anterior tibial spine. In a partial tear, the
         mid-substance shows abnormal increased signal (fluid signal). -->
    <path fill="#0A0A0A"
          d="M 234,256 Q 222,288 210,316 Q 204,334 198,348 L 184,348 Q 188,334 196,316 Q 208,286 218,258 Z"/>
    <!-- Abnormal high-signal region within the ACL — the tear (T2-bright fluid signal) -->
    <ellipse cx="208" cy="300" rx="10" ry="14" fill="url(#lesion-signal)" opacity="0.95"/>

    <!-- ===== JOINT EFFUSION (small) — fluid in the suprapatellar pouch ===== -->
    <path fill="url(#fluid)" opacity="0.6"
          d="M 60,180 L 110,180 L 110,210 Q 90,220 60,210 Z"/>

    <!-- ===== ARTICULAR CARTILAGE — femoral surface ===== -->
    <path fill="#7A7468" opacity="0.5"
          d="M 132,232 Q 180,256 240,266 Q 300,260 342,232 Q 310,272 240,278 Q 168,272 132,232 Z"/>
  </g>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       ORIENTATION + SIDE markers — top corners
       Sagittal knee convention: A = anterior, P = posterior; side = R or L
       =================================================================== -->
  <text x="96" y="106" class="label-orient">A</text>
  <text x="586" y="106" class="label-orient">P</text>
  <text x="100" y="124" class="label-side">R knee</text>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       SEQUENCE METADATA — top-right corner convention
       =================================================================== -->
  <g transform="translate(584, 124)">
    <text x="0" y="0"  class="label-seq" text-anchor="end">SAG T2 FS · 3T</text>
    <text x="0" y="14" class="label-seq" text-anchor="end">TR 4200 · TE 80</text>
    <text x="0" y="28" class="label-seq" text-anchor="end">slice 3 mm · FOV 160 mm</text>
  </g>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       OVERLAY 1 — INTACT-LIGAMENT REFERENCE (green ACL course)
       The normal ACL runs along Blumensaat's line from lateral femoral
       condyle to anterior tibial spine. Drawn as a dashed green reference
       trace that the reader compares the actual ACL to.
       =================================================================== -->
  <g id="acl-reference">
    <path class="ligament-ref"
          d="M 314,336 Q 296,366 282,394 Q 274,412 268,428"/>
    <line class="leader" x1="270" y1="428" x2="338" y2="500"/>
    <text x="342" y="496" class="label-ref">ACL — expected course</text>
    <text x="342" y="510" class="label-anatomy" fill="#6FE0A0" opacity="0.85">Blumensaat line; LFC → ant. tibial spine</text>
  </g>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       OVERLAY 2 — INTACT DISTAL FIBERS (solid green, the preserved portion)
       The distal one-third of the ACL remains continuous with the tibial
       footprint; this is the key prognostic finding that distinguishes a
       partial tear from complete rupture.
       =================================================================== -->
  <g id="acl-intact-distal">
    <path class="ligament" d="M 282,394 Q 274,412 270,426"/>
    <line class="leader" x1="276" y1="420" x2="76" y2="490"/>
    <text x="76" y="486" class="label-ref">distal fibers intact</text>
    <text x="76" y="500" class="label-anatomy" fill="#6FE0A0" opacity="0.85">continuity at tibial footprint preserved</text>
  </g>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       OVERLAY 3 — TEAR LESION (magenta dashed outline)
       The focal region of abnormal high signal in the mid-substance.
       Magenta is the medical-overlay convention for tumor / lesion;
       it carries over to tear / focal abnormality in MRI annotation.
       =================================================================== -->
  <g id="tear-lesion">
    <ellipse cx="288" cy="380" rx="14" ry="22" class="lesion"/>
    <line class="leader" x1="304" y1="378" x2="416" y2="284"/>
    <text x="420" y="280" class="label-finding">partial-thickness tear</text>
    <text x="420" y="294" class="label-anatomy" fill="#FF7CD0" opacity="0.85">mid-substance · fluid signal on T2</text>
    <text x="420" y="308" class="label-anatomy" fill="#FF7CD0" opacity="0.75">no full-width discontinuity</text>
  </g>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       OVERLAY 4 — MEASUREMENT CALIPER (yellow)
       Craniocaudal extent of the tear region, the most reproducible
       measurement for partial ACL injury.
       =================================================================== -->
  <g id="caliper">
    <line class="caliper" x1="266" y1="358" x2="266" y2="402"
          marker-start="url(#caliper-tick)" marker-end="url(#caliper-tick)"/>
    <text x="260" y="384" class="label-meas" text-anchor="end">9 mm</text>
  </g>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       ANATOMIC LANDMARK LABELS — left margin
       =================================================================== -->
  <g id="landmarks">
    <!-- Femur -->
    <line class="leader" x1="220" y1="140" x2="76" y2="200"/>
    <text x="76" y="196" class="label">distal femur</text>
    <text x="76" y="210" class="label-anatomy">lateral condyle in plane</text>

    <!-- Tibia -->
    <line class="leader" x1="280" y1="500" x2="76" y2="592"/>
    <text x="76" y="588" class="label">proximal tibia</text>
    <text x="76" y="602" class="label-anatomy">plateau, anterior spine visible</text>

    <!-- Patella -->
    <line class="leader" x1="116" y1="320" x2="76" y2="320"/>
    <text x="76" y="316" class="label" text-anchor="end">patella</text>

    <!-- PCL reference (right margin) -->
    <line class="leader" x1="380" y1="496" x2="572" y2="540"/>
    <text x="576" y="536" class="label">PCL — intact</text>
    <text x="576" y="550" class="label-anatomy">low signal, continuous, no kink</text>

    <!-- Effusion -->
    <line class="leader" x1="156" y1="248" x2="76" y2="248"/>
    <text x="76" y="244" class="label" text-anchor="end">small effusion</text>
  </g>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       CAPTION PANEL at foot
       =================================================================== -->
  <line x1="60" y1="710" x2="620" y2="710" stroke="#3A3A3A" stroke-width="0.6"/>

  <text x="60" y="732" class="caption-title">
    Partial-thickness mid-substance ACL tear, 9 mm craniocaudal; intact distal fibers.
  </text>

  <text x="60" y="752" class="caption-finding">
    Focal T2-hyperintense signal · no full-width discontinuity · tibial footprint preserved
  </text>

  <text x="60" y="770" class="caption-meta">
    Differential: high-grade partial tear vs. interstitial sprain. Distinction matters: partial tears
    with greater than 50% fiber disruption and instability warrant surgical consideration.
  </text>

  <text x="60" y="786" class="caption-meta">
    Recommended next step: clinical correlation with Lachman and pivot-shift; consider MR arthrography
    if surgical decision is borderline. Compare contralateral knee on follow-up.
  </text>

  <text x="60" y="804" class="caption-meta" fill="#666666">
    Pseudo-MRI for template use. In production, replace with DICOM-derived sequence. Conventions per Stoller (2007) and Radsource MRI Web Clinic.
  </text>
</svg>
```

## `templates/svg-patient-pathway-map.svg`

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!--
  =============================================================================
  Template: svg-patient-pathway-map.svg / Status: Realized starter
  Subject: Sepsis patient pathway, ED arrival → ICU discharge.
           Multi-department whole-encounter map, BPMN 2.0 swim-lane notation,
           time-anchored across 7 lanes. Adapted from Surviving Sepsis
           Campaign 2021 (Evans L et al., Intensive Care Med 2021;47:1181) +
           generic institutional protocol; this is a teaching template, not
           an institutional pathway.
  Register: Patient-pathway swim-lane map (medical-artifacts.md §22 — the
            BPMN-derived analytical artifact whose gaps and lane-crossings
            are where waste, delay, and error live; NHS Improvement
            Pathway Mapping methodology lineage).
  Exemplars: Surviving Sepsis Campaign Hour-1 Bundle (the time-anchored
             intervention discipline); Mayo Clinic Diagnostic and Treatment
             Process Maps (the swim-lane visual lineage); NHS Improvement
             Improvement Leaders' Guide: Process Mapping (the methodology
             reference); BPMN 2.0 (the notational system).
  Signature move: handoff-as-first-class — lane crossings are rendered as
                  explicit baton glyphs (SBAR handoff convention) rather
                  than as edges-passing-through, because the lane crossing
                  is where the encounter's risk concentrates and the
                  pathway-mapping discipline demands the crossing be
                  visible as an event, not absorbed into a transition.
  Render env: Single-file SVG; portable across browsers and print
  =============================================================================

  CUSTOMIZE — slots to adapt when reusing this scaffold:

    1. Lanes (rows). Seven lanes here (ED Triage / ED Phys+RN / Lab+Micro /
       Imaging / Pharmacy / Hospitalist+ICU / Discharge+SW). Replace with
       your institution's actual departments. The discipline: one lane per
       department or named role; no shared lanes; no "other" lane. The
       lane-count drives the artifact height — keep to 6–8 for legibility.
    2. Time axis (columns). T-0 / T+1hr / T+6hr / T+24hr / Day 3 / Day 7
       / Discharge. The non-uniform time grid is intentional — early
       hours are time-critical (Hour-1 Bundle); later days compress.
       Replace with your pathway's clinical cadence. The discipline:
       every column header is a clock value, not a phase name.
    3. Events. Each event is a rectangle in its lane at its time column.
       Replace the sepsis events with your pathway's events. The
       discipline: every event names a verb + observable (Administer
       antibiotics, Obtain blood cultures, Print discharge instructions).
    4. Handoffs. Pentagonal home-plate glyphs at lane crossings carry
       SBAR baton convention (Situation / Background / Assessment /
       Recommendation). Update lane-pair pairing per your pathway.
    5. Time-critical badges. Clock glyphs (⏱) at events with explicit
       time budgets. Apply to any node where missing the budget
       constitutes a safety event (Hour-1 antibiotics, door-to-needle
       stroke, door-to-balloon STEMI).
    6. Decision diamonds. Diamond at lane-pair transitions where the
       decision selects which subsequent lane the patient enters
       (admit-vs-discharge; ward-vs-ICU). Yes/no/numeric labels on
       every outgoing edge; no unlabeled edges.
    7. Citation + last-reviewed. The footer carries the recommendation
       source. Update on every revision; never ship a clinical pathway
       artifact with no provenance and no last-reviewed date.
-->
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     viewBox="0 0 1200 720"
     role="img"
     aria-labelledby="title desc"
     font-family="Inter, system-ui, sans-serif">
  <title id="title">Sepsis patient pathway, ED arrival to ICU discharge — swim-lane map across seven departments and seven time anchors.</title>
  <desc id="desc">A BPMN swim-lane patient-pathway map showing the trajectory of a patient with suspected sepsis from emergency department arrival at time-zero through ICU discharge. Seven horizontal swim-lanes represent the departments and roles involved: (1) ED Triage, (2) ED Physician and Nursing, (3) Lab and Microbiology, (4) Imaging, (5) Pharmacy, (6) Hospitalist and ICU Team, (7) Discharge Planning and Social Work. Seven time anchors span the top: T-0 arrival, T+1 hour, T+6 hours, T+24 hours, Day 3, Day 7, and Discharge. The patient pathway threads through these lanes as a sequence of action rectangles, data-input parallelograms, decision diamonds, handoff baton glyphs at lane crossings, and clock-badge icons marking time-critical Surviving Sepsis Hour-1 Bundle interventions. The Hour-1 Bundle clock badge governs the leftmost cluster: lactate measurement at T+30 minutes (Lab lane), broad-spectrum antibiotic delivery within one hour of recognition (Pharmacy lane), thirty milliliters per kilogram crystalloid for hypotension or lactate four or greater (ED Physician lane), and vasopressor initiation if hypotension persists (Hospitalist lane). A decision diamond at T+4 hours selects ward versus ICU admission based on hemodynamic stability. Hospital course days 1 through 7 show empiric-to-targeted antibiotic de-escalation in the Pharmacy lane and discharge planning in the Discharge lane. The Discharge column terminus shows handoff to community primary-care provider with antibiotic completion plan and follow-up appointment. Citations to the Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 guideline and BPMN 2.0 notation appear in the footer beneath the diagram, alongside the last-reviewed date and the medical-mode YAML metadata block.</desc>

  <defs>
    <!-- Lane band fill (alternating subtle bands for row discrimination) -->
    <pattern id="band-soft" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse" width="6" height="6">
      <rect width="6" height="6" fill="#F8F7F2"/>
    </pattern>
    <!-- Arrow marker for sequence flow -->
    <marker id="seq-arrow" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5"
            markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" orient="auto">
      <path d="M 0,1 L 9,5 L 0,9 z" fill="#1A1A1A"/>
    </marker>
    <!-- Arrow marker for handoff (lighter weight) -->
    <marker id="handoff-arrow" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5"
            markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto">
      <path d="M 0,1 L 9,5 L 0,9 z" fill="#7A5C2E"/>
    </marker>
    <!-- Diamond marker (decision node visualized inline) -->
    <symbol id="time-budget-clock" viewBox="0 0 16 16">
      <circle cx="8" cy="8" r="6.5" fill="#FFF" stroke="#B91C1C" stroke-width="1.4"/>
      <line x1="8" y1="8" x2="8" y2="4.5" stroke="#B91C1C" stroke-width="1.2"/>
      <line x1="8" y1="8" x2="10.5" y2="9" stroke="#B91C1C" stroke-width="1.2"/>
    </symbol>
    <!-- SBAR baton glyph (handoff convention) -->
    <symbol id="sbar-baton" viewBox="0 0 22 12">
      <rect x="1" y="3" width="20" height="6" rx="3" fill="#FBEFD7" stroke="#7A5C2E" stroke-width="0.9"/>
      <text x="11" y="8.4" text-anchor="middle"
            font-size="5.5" font-weight="700" fill="#5C4318"
            font-family="Inter, system-ui, sans-serif"
            letter-spacing="0.08em">SBAR</text>
    </symbol>

    <style>
      .canvas       { fill: #FBFAF6; }
      .lane-band-a  { fill: #FFFFFF; }
      .lane-band-b  { fill: #F4F2EA; }
      .lane-rule    { stroke: #C7BFAA; stroke-width: 0.5; fill: none; }
      .lane-rule-heavy { stroke: #1A1A1A; stroke-width: 0.8; fill: none; }
      .time-rule    { stroke: #C7BFAA; stroke-width: 0.4; stroke-dasharray: 2 3; fill: none; }
      .time-rule-major { stroke: #8A7E5F; stroke-width: 0.6; fill: none; }
      .lane-label   { font-size: 10px; fill: #1A1A1A; font-weight: 600;
                      letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; }
      .lane-sublabel { font-size: 8.5px; fill: #5C4318; font-style: italic; }
      .time-label   { font-size: 10px; fill: #1A1A1A; font-weight: 600;
                      letter-spacing: 0.05em; }
      .time-sub     { font-size: 8.5px; fill: #5C4318; }
      .title-text   { font-size: 15px; fill: #1A1A1A; font-weight: 700;
                      letter-spacing: 0.03em; }
      .subtitle-text { font-size: 11px; fill: #5C4318; font-style: italic; }
      .event-action { font-size: 9.5px; fill: #0F172A; font-weight: 500; }
      .event-data   { font-size: 9px; fill: #1F2937; font-style: italic; }
      .event-decision { font-size: 9px; fill: #422006; font-weight: 600;
                       text-anchor: middle; }
      .event-terminus { font-size: 9.5px; fill: #064E3B; font-weight: 600; }
      .footer-text  { font-size: 9px; fill: #5C4318; }
      .footer-cite  { font-size: 8.5px; fill: #5C4318; font-style: italic; }
      .bundle-banner { font-size: 9px; fill: #7F1D1D; font-weight: 700;
                       letter-spacing: 0.07em; }
    </style>
  </defs>

  <rect class="canvas" width="1200" height="720"/>

  <!-- ============================================================
       Title block
       ============================================================ -->
  <text x="60" y="34" class="title-text">
    Sepsis patient pathway · ED arrival to ICU discharge.
  </text>
  <text x="60" y="51" class="subtitle-text">
    Seven swim-lanes across seven time anchors; baton glyphs mark every department handoff; clock badges mark Surviving Sepsis Hour-1 interventions.
  </text>

  <!-- ============================================================
       Coordinate system:
       Lanes occupy y ∈ [80, 580], split into 7 bands of 62.5 px each.
       (Lane heights: 75, 75, 60, 60, 60, 100, 70 — slightly variable
        to reflect event density per lane.)
       Time columns at x = 200, 350, 490, 640, 790, 940, 1090 (centers).
       Column ranges:  T-0:    150-300
                       T+1hr:  300-440
                       T+6hr:  440-570
                       T+24hr: 570-720
                       Day 3:  720-860
                       Day 7:  860-1010
                       Disch:  1010-1160
       Lane label gutter: x ∈ [50, 150].
       ============================================================ -->

  <!-- Lane bands (alternating soft fill for row discrimination) -->
  <rect class="lane-band-b" x="150" y="90"  width="1010" height="60"/>
  <rect class="lane-band-a" x="150" y="150" width="1010" height="65"/>
  <rect class="lane-band-b" x="150" y="215" width="1010" height="55"/>
  <rect class="lane-band-a" x="150" y="270" width="1010" height="55"/>
  <rect class="lane-band-b" x="150" y="325" width="1010" height="55"/>
  <rect class="lane-band-a" x="150" y="380" width="1010" height="100"/>
  <rect class="lane-band-b" x="150" y="480" width="1010" height="60"/>

  <!-- Lane separators (subtle horizontal rules) -->
  <line class="lane-rule" x1="150" y1="90"  x2="1160" y2="90"/>
  <line class="lane-rule" x1="150" y1="150" x2="1160" y2="150"/>
  <line class="lane-rule" x1="150" y1="215" x2="1160" y2="215"/>
  <line class="lane-rule" x1="150" y1="270" x2="1160" y2="270"/>
  <line class="lane-rule" x1="150" y1="325" x2="1160" y2="325"/>
  <line class="lane-rule" x1="150" y1="380" x2="1160" y2="380"/>
  <line class="lane-rule" x1="150" y1="480" x2="1160" y2="480"/>
  <line class="lane-rule-heavy" x1="150" y1="540" x2="1160" y2="540"/>
  <line class="lane-rule-heavy" x1="150" y1="80"  x2="1160" y2="80"/>
  <!-- Lane-gutter vertical rule -->
  <line class="lane-rule-heavy" x1="150" y1="80" x2="150" y2="540"/>
  <line class="lane-rule-heavy" x1="1160" y1="80" x2="1160" y2="540"/>

  <!-- ============================================================
       LANE LABELS (left gutter)
       ============================================================ -->
  <g>
    <text x="60" y="115" class="lane-label">ED Triage</text>
    <text x="60" y="127" class="lane-sublabel">Reception nurse</text>

    <text x="60" y="180" class="lane-label">ED Physician + RN</text>
    <text x="60" y="192" class="lane-sublabel">Treating clinicians</text>

    <text x="60" y="240" class="lane-label">Lab · Microbiology</text>
    <text x="60" y="252" class="lane-sublabel">Specimen + result</text>

    <text x="60" y="295" class="lane-label">Imaging</text>
    <text x="60" y="307" class="lane-sublabel">Radiology</text>

    <text x="60" y="350" class="lane-label">Pharmacy</text>
    <text x="60" y="362" class="lane-sublabel">Antimicrobial dispense</text>

    <text x="60" y="420" class="lane-label">Hospitalist · ICU</text>
    <text x="60" y="432" class="lane-sublabel">Admitting + critical-care</text>

    <text x="60" y="505" class="lane-label">Discharge · SW</text>
    <text x="60" y="517" class="lane-sublabel">Care coordination</text>
  </g>

  <!-- ============================================================
       TIME-AXIS HEADER (top)
       ============================================================ -->
  <g>
    <line class="time-rule-major" x1="300" y1="80" x2="300" y2="540"/>
    <line class="time-rule-major" x1="440" y1="80" x2="440" y2="540"/>
    <line class="time-rule-major" x1="570" y1="80" x2="570" y2="540"/>
    <line class="time-rule" x1="720" y1="80" x2="720" y2="540"/>

         parallelogram    → data input or output (result, order)

         baton glyph      → handoff between lanes (SBAR convention)

        units_explicit: true

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!--
  Template: svg-prisma-flow.svg / Status: Realized starter

                  identification through inclusion, with exclusion reasons
                  cited at every screening step; arithmetic verifiable per tier
  Render env: Single-file SVG; portable across browsers, PDF, and print

       short-title in <title>/<desc> must match the registered protocol.

       CINAHL, ClinicalTrials.gov) and "other sources" (hand-searching,
       citation chasing, expert contact, grey-literature) per actual searches.

         identified (db + other) = total identified
         total - duplicates = screened
         screened = excluded-title/abstract + sought-for-retrieval
         sought = not-retrieved + assessed-for-eligibility
         assessed = excluded-with-reasons + included
         included (qualitative) ⊇ included (quantitative meta-analysis subset)
    4. Exclusion reasons. PRISMA 2020 explicitly requires reasons for full-text
       exclusions. Group into 4–6 categories with counts.
    5. Synthesis populations. Qualitative (narrative) and quantitative

    6. Header / footer non-removable. The PRISMA 2020 citation in the footer
       is a methodological obligation, not decoration.

  compliance editors at Cochrane and major journals sum each tier; any

Eligibility: 164 excluded with reasons (no comparator 52, mixed population 38, abstract only 27, not protocolized CBT 23, measure not validated 14, outcome not extractable 10). ## `templates/svg-radiograph-overlay.svg`

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!--
  =============================================================================
  Template: svg-radiograph-overlay.svg / Status: Realized starter
  Subject: AP pelvis radiograph with right pertrochanteric femur fracture
           (AO/OTA 31-A2), neck-shaft angle measurement, femoral head
           circle-fit, structures at risk, calibration scale.
  Register: 16 Medical-imaging overlay
  Exemplars: Stoller, Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Orthopaedics and Sports
             Medicine (3rd ed., 2007); Radsource MRI Web Clinic; AIUM MSK
             Ultrasound Practice Parameter (2022); AO/OTA Fracture and
             Dislocation Classification Compendium (2018).
  Signature move: medical-color-vocabulary (Register 16 convention) — every
                  overlay element ink chosen from a disciplined clinical
                  palette: yellow nerve, red artery, blue vein, green
                  ligament, dashed white fracture line, magenta lesion,
                  cyan implant. The radiograph is the load-bearing image;
                  the vector overlay directs attention and measures.
  Render env: Single-file SVG; portable across browsers and print
  Pairs with: references/medium-playbooks/svg-illustration.md (Register 16);
              references/libraries/medical-artifacts.md (imaging conventions);
              references/medium-playbooks/clinical-case.md (figure conventions
              for teaching-case integration).
  =============================================================================

  CUSTOMIZE — slots to adapt when reusing this scaffold:

    1. Imaging modality. This template uses a stylized vector pseudo-
       radiograph (a grayscale pelvis silhouette built from <path> elements
       beneath the overlay). In production, replace the <g id="pseudo-
       radiograph"> block with an <image href="ap-pelvis.png"
       opacity="0.85"/> element pointing to a real DICOM-derived PNG or
       JPEG. The overlay coordinates assume the pelvis is roughly centered;
       re-anchor measurements to your image's actual landmarks.
    2. Anatomy + pathology. The fracture shown is an AO/OTA 31-A2.2
       pertrochanteric femur fracture (the most common geriatric hip
       fracture pattern). To adapt: change the fracture-line geometry in
       <g id="fracture-line"> and update the classification label in the
       caption. The neck-shaft angle measurement (128° normal, < 120° varus,
       > 135° valgus) and the circle-fit on the femoral head transfer to
       any femur radiograph.
    3. Color vocabulary (medical convention — do not invent):
         - Nerve:           #FFD700  (gold / yellow)
         - Artery:          #C8102E  (red)
         - Vein:            #0066CC  (blue)
         - Ligament/tendon: #2E8B57  (forest green)
         - Fracture line:   #FFFFFF  with stroke-dasharray="5 3"
         - Tumor/lesion:    #C71585  (magenta)
         - Implant:         #00CED1  (cyan)
       Use these consistently; clinicians read the colors as data.
    4. Measurement constructs. The template demonstrates three: angle
       (vertex + two rays), circle-fit (with center-crosshair), and linear
       caliper. For other constructs (parallel-distance with tick caps;
       Cobb angle in scoliosis; alpha angle at the femoral head-neck
       junction), see Stoller and Radsource for canonical examples.
    5. Calibration scale. The 25 mm reference ball is the orthopaedic
       templating standard; place it at constant pixel-to-mm ratio. For MRI,
       use the FOV scale; for ultrasound, the cm depth markers; for CT, the
       slice-thickness annotation.
    6. Plate caption. Convention: classification system + finding +
       measurement values + clinical implication. Keep terse; clinicians
       extract data, not prose.
-->
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     viewBox="0 0 760 880"
     role="img"
     aria-labelledby="title desc"
     font-family="Inter, system-ui, sans-serif">
  <title id="title">AP pelvis radiograph with right pertrochanteric femur fracture (AO/OTA 31-A2.2), annotated.</title>
  <desc id="desc">An anteroposterior pelvis radiograph showing a right pertrochanteric femur fracture classified AO/OTA 31-A2.2 (two-part intertrochanteric fracture with a separated lesser trochanter fragment). The right neck-shaft angle is measured at 122 degrees (compared with 130 degrees on the unaffected left side; normal range 125 to 140), indicating early varus collapse. A circle-fit is drawn on the right femoral head with a center crosshair to identify the head center for templating. Greater trochanter, lesser trochanter, and femoral head landmarks are labeled. The medial femoral circumflex artery — the dominant blood supply to the femoral head and the principal structure at risk during fixation — is traced in red along the medial neck. A 25 millimeter calibration sphere is shown at the lower left for radiographic templating. Orientation markers R and L appear at the upper corners. The caption documents classification, measurements, and the clinical recommendation.</desc>

## `templates/svg-taping-sequence.svg`
