```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!--
  =============================================================================
  Template: svg-taping-sequence.svg / Status: Realized starter
  Subject: Closed basket-weave ankle taping — the canonical prophylactic
           ankle-taping technique in athletic training and sports medicine.
           Six-panel sequence demonstrating (1) anchors, (2) stirrups,
           (3) horseshoes, (4) figure-of-eight, (5) heel locks, (6) closure.
  Audience: Athletic-training students learning the technique; certified ATs
            reviewing convention; sideline reference for the AT taping at
            speed before a game.
  Register: 16 Medical-imaging overlay (color vocabulary; anatomical
            landmark labeling) crossed with 10 Comparative plate (shared
            scale, shared baseline, sequence-as-grid). The six panels are
            comparative because they share orientation, scale, and label
            anchor; they form a sequence because the numbering carries
            instructional order.
  Exemplars: David Perrin, Athletic Taping, Bracing, and Casting (5th ed.,
             2018); the NATA's official taping reference; Mulligan / Maitland
             manual-therapy taping conventions; the Cramer / Mueller
             athletic-tape technical brochures (which themselves draw on a
             century of trainer-craft documentation from Cramer's 1923
             founding).
  Signature move: 7.5 minimum-difference example set — each panel varies
                  from the prior by exactly one tape application; the
                  reader's eye learns the technique by direct visual
                  comparison panel-to-panel rather than by reading
                  descriptive prose. The cumulative tape pattern grows
                  one feature per panel; the underlying foot anatomy
                  stays constant across all six panels. The teaching is
                  the visual delta. Secondary: 1.14 cartouche-bound
                  figure — the plate carries its provenance (tape brand
                  references, anatomical convention) in a footer cartouche
                  in the manner of a scientific plate.
  Render env: Single-file SVG; portable across browsers and print;
              ~24-inch wide at print quality. Targets ~30 KB on disk.
  Pairs with: references/medium-playbooks/svg-illustration.md (Register
              16 conventions); references/libraries/medical-artifacts.md
              §20 (sports-medicine genres); templates/svg-lachman-test.svg
              (Wave 10 sibling — physical-exam plate using the same color
              vocabulary); templates/sideline-eap.md (Wave 13 sibling —
              the AT who uses this taping technique is the same AT who
              executes the EAP).
  =============================================================================

  CUSTOMIZE — slots to adapt when reusing this scaffold:

    1. Taping technique. The closed basket-weave is the realized example.
       Substitutions: open basket-weave (omits closure strips for skin
       breathability; not for game use); Louisiana-style (adds extra
       lateral support, used in high-velocity rotational sports);
       elastic-tape augmentation (Kinesio / Mulligan registers, with
       elastic adhesive bandage layered over rigid tape; not the
       prophylactic register).
    2. Body region. The realized example is the ankle. The six-panel
       sequence convention transfers to: wrist (anchors + figure-8 +
       thumb-spica + closure); knee (Mc-Connell patellar taping with
       its own four-panel sequence); shoulder (Mulligan / Kinesio
       AC-joint with three-panel sequence).
    3. Tape gauge. The realized example uses standard 1.5-inch white
       athletic tape (Cramer / Mueller / Johnson & Johnson Coach
       reference). Substitutions: 1-inch tape for pediatric ankles or
       wrist; 2-inch elastic bandage (Elastikon) for figure-of-eight
       elements when greater flexibility needed; Hypafix for skin-
       protective base layer (the pre-wrap convention).
    4. Anatomical landmark labeling. The realized example labels the
       medial malleolus, lateral malleolus, navicular tuberosity, and
       fifth metatarsal base (the four bony prominences that drive
       tape placement and the structures-at-risk for skin breakdown
       under tape). Replace per anatomy if changing region.
    5. Pre-tape skin preparation. The plate assumes appropriate skin
       prep (clean and dry skin; tape adherent spray if athlete
       perspires heavily; heel-and-lace pads on dorsum to prevent
       blister); this is not depicted but is named in the footer.
    6. Color vocabulary (carries over from Register 16):
         - Skin tone neutral:   #E8D2B0
         - Skin shadow:         #C8AB80
         - Bone (visible deep): #F0E5CC with ink stroke
         - Tape (white):        #FAFAFA with thin gray stitching
         - Anatomical label:    italic serif, slate
         - Sequence numerals:   bold sans, small-caps eyebrow
         - Direction arrow:     thin black with arrowhead
       The tape's "stitching" hatching is the texture that distinguishes
       tape from skin in monochrome; do not omit.
-->
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     viewBox="0 0 1440 880"
     role="img"
     aria-labelledby="title desc"
     font-family="Source Serif Pro, Georgia, serif">
  <title id="title">Closed basket-weave ankle taping — six-panel instructional sequence from anchors through closure.</title>
  <desc id="desc">A six-panel instructional plate showing the closed basket-weave ankle taping technique used by athletic trainers for prophylactic ankle stabilization. The panels are arranged in a two-row, three-column grid. Each panel shows the right foot from a foreshortened lateral perspective with the medial malleolus, lateral malleolus, navicular tuberosity, and fifth metatarsal base labeled. Panel 1 shows three anchor strips: two proximal anchors around the distal leg and one distal anchor around the midfoot. Panel 2 adds three vertical stirrups running from the medial proximal anchor, under the heel, to the lateral proximal anchor, applied in medial-to-lateral order. Panel 3 adds three horizontal horseshoes running from anterior to posterior around the malleoli, applied distal to proximal. Panel 4 adds a figure-of-eight that wraps around the heel from the lateral anchor down across the dorsum and back. Panel 5 adds two heel locks, medial first then lateral. Panel 6 shows the completed wrap with closure strips covering all exposed tape edges. Each panel carries sequence numerals at the top left and a direction arrow on the just-applied tape strip. A scale bar at the foot of the plate gives a four-inch reference. The plate caption reads "Plate XII — Closed Basket-Weave Ankle Tape, Sequential Application." A footer cartouche names the technique convention (Perrin Athletic Taping, Bracing, and Casting 5th edition; Cramer and Mueller technical references; NATA convention).</desc>

  <defs>
    <style>
      .ground          { fill: #F4ECDC; }
      .panel-bg        { fill: #FAF5E7; }
      .panel-rule      { stroke: #C7BC9F; stroke-width: 0.6; fill: none; }

      .ink-body        { stroke-width: 1.2; }

      .ink-hair        { stroke-width: 0.4; opacity: 0.85; }

      .skin-stroke     { stroke: #8A6E48; stroke-width: 0.8; fill: none; opacity: 0.7; }
      .bone            { fill: #F0E5CC; }
      .bone-stroke     { stroke: #1F1A14; stroke-width: 0.6; fill: #F0E5CC; opacity: 0.55; }
      .tape            { fill: #FAFAFA; stroke: #1F1A14; stroke-width: 0.4; }
      .tape-stitch     { stroke: #A0A0A0; stroke-width: 0.25; fill: none; stroke-dasharray: 1.2 1.2; }
      .tape-active     { fill: #FAFAFA; stroke: #C8102E; stroke-width: 0.9; }
      .direction       { stroke: #C8102E; stroke-width: 1.4; fill: none; }
      .landmark-dot    { fill: #1F1A14; }
      .leader          { stroke: #6B5F4A; stroke-width: 0.4; fill: none; opacity: 0.75; }

      .panel-num       { font-size: 11px; fill: #6B5F4A; font-variant: small-caps;
                         letter-spacing: 0.16em; font-weight: 600; }
      .panel-step      { font-size: 22px; fill: #1F1A14; font-weight: 700;
                         font-family: Inter, sans-serif; }
      .panel-title     { font-size: 14px; fill: #1F1A14; font-weight: 600;
                         letter-spacing: 0.04em; }
      .anatomy         { font-size: 10px; fill: #4A4234; font-style: italic; }
      .anatomy-bold    { font-size: 10px; fill: #1F1A14; font-style: italic; font-weight: 600; }
      .direction-label { font-size: 10px; fill: #C8102E; font-weight: 600; }
      .strip-num       { font-size: 9px; fill: #1F1A14; font-weight: 700;
                         font-family: Inter, sans-serif; }
      .caption-body    { font-size: 11px; fill: #1F1A14; }
      .caption-title   { font-size: 14px; fill: #1F1A14; font-weight: 600;
                         letter-spacing: 0.04em; }
      .plate-caption   { font-size: 12px; fill: #1F1A14; font-variant: small-caps;
                         letter-spacing: 0.16em; }
      .meta            { font-size: 9.5px; fill: #6B5F4A; font-variant: small-caps;
                         letter-spacing: 0.10em; }
      .meta-italic     { font-size: 10px; fill: #6B5F4A; font-style: italic; }
      .scale-tick      { stroke: #1F1A14; stroke-width: 0.6; }
      .scale-bar       { stroke: #1F1A14; stroke-width: 1.2; }
      .header-title    { font-size: 20px; fill: #1F1A14; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.01em; }
      .header-sub      { font-size: 12px; fill: #4A4234; font-style: italic; }
    </style>

    <!-- Foot anatomy as a reusable symbol — every panel uses this same
         underlying foot at the same scale. The minimum-difference example
         set discipline depends on the foot being identical across panels;
         only the tape pattern changes. -->
    <symbol id="foot-anatomy" viewBox="0 0 360 200">
      <!-- Leg shaft / shin (proximal stub for anchor placement) -->
      <path class="skin" d="M 20,10 Q 18,4 28,2 L 100,2 Q 112,6 112,18 L 112,82 Q 108,92 96,94 L 32,94 Q 20,90 20,80 Z"/>
      <path class="skin-shadow" d="M 28,72 Q 60,90 100,90 L 108,80 Q 108,90 96,94 L 32,94 Q 22,90 28,72 Z"/>
      <path class="skin-stroke" d="M 20,10 Q 18,4 28,2 L 100,2 Q 112,6 112,18 L 112,82 Q 108,92 96,94 L 32,94 Q 20,90 20,80 Z"/>

      <!-- Heel / posterior foot -->
      <path class="skin" d="M 20,80 Q 8,90 8,118 Q 8,144 36,150 L 84,150 Q 98,148 110,134 L 112,82 Q 108,92 96,94 L 32,94 Q 20,90 20,80 Z"/>
      <path class="skin-shadow" d="M 12,130 Q 40,148 84,148 L 100,138 Q 98,148 84,150 L 36,150 Q 8,144 12,130 Z"/>
      <path class="skin-stroke" d="M 20,80 Q 8,90 8,118 Q 8,144 36,150 L 84,150 Q 98,148 110,134"/>

      <!-- Midfoot + forefoot (foreshortened lateral perspective) -->
      <path class="skin" d="M 84,150 Q 108,148 132,142 L 240,116 Q 296,108 326,116 Q 344,124 342,138 Q 332,156 296,160 L 200,168 Q 130,170 84,164 Z"/>
      <path class="skin-shadow" d="M 88,160 Q 130,168 200,166 L 296,158 Q 332,156 342,138 L 344,148 Q 332,162 296,164 L 200,168 Q 130,170 84,164 Q 86,162 88,160 Z"/>
      <path class="skin-stroke" d="M 84,150 Q 108,148 132,142 L 240,116 Q 296,108 326,116 Q 344,124 342,138 Q 332,156 296,160 L 200,168 Q 130,170 84,164"/>

      <!-- Toes (suggested at distal end) -->
      <path class="skin" d="M 326,116 Q 340,108 350,114 Q 354,124 344,128 Z M 312,108 Q 326,102 332,110 L 326,116 Z M 296,104 Q 308,98 316,106 L 312,108 Z"/>

      <!-- Lateral malleolus (visible bony prominence; right foot lateral side ≈ x 110, y 90) -->
      <ellipse class="bone-stroke" cx="108" cy="98" rx="14" ry="10"/>
      <!-- Medial malleolus (drawn fainter; on the opposite side, partially visible at top of heel) -->
      <ellipse class="bone-stroke" cx="68" cy="86" rx="11" ry="8" opacity="0.4"/>
      <!-- Navicular tuberosity (medial midfoot, on the working anterior aspect) -->
      <ellipse class="bone-stroke" cx="148" cy="146" rx="9" ry="6" opacity="0.55"/>
      <!-- Fifth metatarsal base (lateral midfoot prominence) -->
      <ellipse class="bone-stroke" cx="186" cy="156" rx="10" ry="7" opacity="0.55"/>

      <!-- Landmark dots (visible marker on skin surface where bony prominence is palpated) -->
      <circle class="landmark-dot" cx="108" cy="98" r="1.6"/>
      <circle class="landmark-dot" cx="68" cy="86" r="1.4"/>
      <circle class="landmark-dot" cx="148" cy="146" r="1.4"/>
      <circle class="landmark-dot" cx="186" cy="156" r="1.4"/>
    </symbol>

    <marker id="dir-arrow" viewBox="0 0 12 12" refX="10" refY="6"
            markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" orient="auto">
      <path d="M 0,0 L 12,6 L 0,12 L 3,6 Z" fill="#C8102E"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>

  <rect class="ground" width="1440" height="880"/>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       HEADER
       =================================================================== -->
  <text x="60" y="50" class="header-title">
    Closed basket-weave ankle taping — sequential application.
  </text>
  <text x="60" y="74" class="header-sub">
    Six panels; each panel adds one tape group to the prior. Right foot, foreshortened lateral view. The
    foot's anatomy is identical across panels; the tape pattern accumulates. Read left-to-right, top-to-bottom.
  </text>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       LANDMARK LEGEND (top right)
       =================================================================== -->
  <g transform="translate(1080, 30)">
    <rect class="panel-bg" x="0" y="0" width="320" height="60" rx="3"/>
    <rect class="panel-rule" x="0" y="0" width="320" height="60" rx="3"/>
    <text x="14" y="20" class="panel-num">ANATOMICAL LANDMARKS</text>
    <g transform="translate(14, 32)">
      <circle class="landmark-dot" cx="0" cy="0" r="2"/>
      <text x="8" y="3" class="anatomy">lateral malleolus</text>
      <circle class="landmark-dot" cx="120" cy="0" r="2"/>
      <text x="128" y="3" class="anatomy">medial malleolus</text>
      <circle class="landmark-dot" cx="0" cy="16" r="2"/>
      <text x="8" y="19" class="anatomy">navicular tuberosity</text>
      <circle class="landmark-dot" cx="120" cy="16" r="2"/>
      <text x="128" y="19" class="anatomy">5th metatarsal base</text>
    </g>
  </g>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       PANEL 1 — ANCHORS
       Three anchor strips: two proximal (around distal leg), one distal
       (around midfoot, proximal to the 5th MT base).
       =================================================================== -->
  <g id="panel-1" transform="translate(40, 110)">
    <rect class="panel-bg" x="0" y="0" width="440" height="340" rx="3"/>
    <rect class="panel-rule" x="0" y="0" width="440" height="340" rx="3"/>

    <text x="16" y="24" class="panel-num">PANEL 1 · STEP 1 OF 6</text>
    <text x="16" y="44" class="panel-step">Anchors</text>
    <text x="120" y="44" class="panel-title">3 strips · 2 proximal, 1 distal</text>

    <g transform="translate(40, 80)">
      <use href="#foot-anatomy" width="360" height="200"/>

      <!-- Two proximal anchors around the distal leg -->
      <g>
        <rect class="tape-active" x="18" y="14" width="100" height="14" rx="2"/>
        <line class="tape-stitch" x1="22" y1="16" x2="22" y2="26"/>
        <line class="tape-stitch" x1="36" y1="16" x2="36" y2="26"/>
        <line class="tape-stitch" x1="50" y1="16" x2="50" y2="26"/>
        <line class="tape-stitch" x1="64" y1="16" x2="64" y2="26"/>
        <line class="tape-stitch" x1="78" y1="16" x2="78" y2="26"/>
        <line class="tape-stitch" x1="92" y1="16" x2="92" y2="26"/>
        <line class="tape-stitch" x1="106" y1="16" x2="106" y2="26"/>
        <text x="68" y="11" class="strip-num" text-anchor="middle">1</text>

        <rect class="tape-active" x="20" y="36" width="100" height="14" rx="2"/>
        <line class="tape-stitch" x1="24" y1="38" x2="24" y2="48"/>
        <line class="tape-stitch" x1="38" y1="38" x2="38" y2="48"/>
        <line class="tape-stitch" x1="52" y1="38" x2="52" y2="48"/>
        <line class="tape-stitch" x1="66" y1="38" x2="66" y2="48"/>
        <line class="tape-stitch" x1="80" y1="38" x2="80" y2="48"/>
        <line class="tape-stitch" x1="94" y1="38" x2="94" y2="48"/>
        <line class="tape-stitch" x1="108" y1="38" x2="108" y2="48"/>
        <text x="70" y="32" class="strip-num" text-anchor="middle">2</text>
      </g>

      <!-- Distal anchor around midfoot -->
      <rect class="tape-active" x="156" y="128" width="78" height="14" rx="2"
            transform="rotate(-12, 195, 135)"/>
      <text x="195" y="118" class="strip-num" text-anchor="middle">3</text>

      <!-- Direction arrow on strip 1 (counterclockwise around the leg from medial) -->
      <path class="direction" d="M 18,21 Q 12,15 22,12" marker-end="url(#dir-arrow)"/>
      <text x="3" y="9" class="direction-label">apply</text>

      <!-- Landmark labels -->
      <text x="130" y="100" class="anatomy" text-anchor="end">lateral malleolus</text>
      <path class="leader" d="M 130,98 L 112,98"/>
      <text x="234" y="166" class="anatomy">5th MT base</text>
      <path class="leader" d="M 230,162 L 192,158"/>
      <text x="166" y="142" class="anatomy" text-anchor="end">navicular</text>
      <path class="leader" d="M 162,140 L 152,144"/>
    </g>

    <text x="16" y="306" class="caption-body">
      Two anchors around the distal leg above the malleoli; one distal anchor
    </text>
    <text x="16" y="320" class="caption-body">
      around the midfoot proximal to the fifth metatarsal base. All anchors
    </text>
    <text x="16" y="332" class="caption-body">
      circumferential; not so tight that they restrict venous return.
    </text>
  </g>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       PANEL 2 — STIRRUPS
       Three vertical stirrups, medial-to-lateral, from proximal anchor
       down under heel and up to opposite proximal anchor.
       =================================================================== -->
  <g id="panel-2" transform="translate(500, 110)">
    <rect class="panel-bg" x="0" y="0" width="440" height="340" rx="3"/>
    <rect class="panel-rule" x="0" y="0" width="440" height="340" rx="3"/>

    <text x="16" y="24" class="panel-num">PANEL 2 · STEP 2 OF 6</text>
    <text x="16" y="44" class="panel-step">Stirrups</text>
    <text x="120" y="44" class="panel-title">3 vertical strips · medial → lateral</text>

    <g transform="translate(40, 80)">
      <use href="#foot-anatomy" width="360" height="200"/>

      <!-- Anchors (now drawn as established tape — not active) -->
      <rect class="tape" x="18" y="14" width="100" height="14" rx="2"/>
      <rect class="tape" x="20" y="36" width="100" height="14" rx="2"/>
      <rect class="tape" x="156" y="128" width="78" height="14" rx="2" transform="rotate(-12, 195, 135)"/>

      <!-- Three stirrups: each runs from medial proximal anchor, down across
           the medial malleolus, under the heel, up across the lateral
           malleolus, and onto the lateral proximal anchor. -->
      <!-- Stirrup 1: most posterior (over the malleoli centers) -->
      <path class="tape-active" d="M 56,18 L 60,24 Q 36,80 28,130 Q 38,148 80,150 Q 102,140 116,98 Q 118,52 96,18 Z"
            opacity="0.95"/>
      <text x="36" y="74" class="strip-num">1</text>

      <!-- Stirrup 2: slightly anterior of #1 -->
      <path class="tape-active" d="M 66,18 L 70,24 Q 50,84 46,134 Q 58,150 92,148 Q 116,138 130,100 Q 130,54 110,18 Z"
            opacity="0.92"/>
      <text x="56" y="92" class="strip-num">2</text>

      <!-- Stirrup 3: most anterior -->
      <path class="tape-active" d="M 78,18 L 82,24 Q 70,90 70,138 Q 84,150 108,144 Q 132,130 144,102 Q 144,56 124,18 Z"
            opacity="0.88"/>
      <text x="84" y="124" class="strip-num">3</text>

      <!-- Direction arrow showing apply order -->
      <path class="direction" d="M 62,24 Q 40,80 32,128" marker-end="url(#dir-arrow)" opacity="0.85"/>
      <text x="6" y="120" class="direction-label">medial → lateral</text>

      <!-- Heel reference -->
      <text x="-6" y="148" class="anatomy" text-anchor="end">heel</text>
      <path class="leader" d="M -2,146 L 14,140"/>
    </g>

    <text x="16" y="306" class="caption-body">
      Each stirrup begins at the medial proximal anchor, descends along the
    </text>
    <text x="16" y="320" class="caption-body">
      medial side, passes under the heel, and ascends to the lateral proximal
    </text>
    <text x="16" y="332" class="caption-body">
      anchor. Apply medial-to-lateral; each subsequent stirrup overlaps the prior by half its width.
    </text>
  </g>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       PANEL 3 — HORSESHOES
       Three horizontal strips around the malleoli, distal-to-proximal.
       =================================================================== -->
  <g id="panel-3" transform="translate(960, 110)">
    <rect class="panel-bg" x="0" y="0" width="440" height="340" rx="3"/>
    <rect class="panel-rule" x="0" y="0" width="440" height="340" rx="3"/>

    <text x="16" y="24" class="panel-num">PANEL 3 · STEP 3 OF 6</text>
    <text x="16" y="44" class="panel-step">Horseshoes</text>
    <text x="120" y="44" class="panel-title">3 horizontal strips · distal → proximal</text>

    <g transform="translate(40, 80)">
      <use href="#foot-anatomy" width="360" height="200"/>

      <!-- Anchors -->
      <rect class="tape" x="18" y="14" width="100" height="14" rx="2"/>
      <rect class="tape" x="20" y="36" width="100" height="14" rx="2"/>
      <rect class="tape" x="156" y="128" width="78" height="14" rx="2" transform="rotate(-12, 195, 135)"/>

      <!-- Stirrups (now established) -->
      <path class="tape" d="M 56,18 L 60,24 Q 36,80 28,130 Q 38,148 80,150 Q 102,140 116,98 Q 118,52 96,18 Z" opacity="0.85"/>
      <path class="tape" d="M 66,18 L 70,24 Q 50,84 46,134 Q 58,150 92,148 Q 116,138 130,100 Q 130,54 110,18 Z" opacity="0.82"/>
      <path class="tape" d="M 78,18 L 82,24 Q 70,90 70,138 Q 84,150 108,144 Q 132,130 144,102 Q 144,56 124,18 Z" opacity="0.78"/>

      <!-- Three horseshoes: U-shapes around the heel/malleolus complex.
           Distal-to-proximal: each above the prior. -->
      <!-- Horseshoe 1 — most distal -->
      <path class="tape-active" d="M 124,144 Q 96,156 56,150 Q 30,142 16,128 Q 16,142 32,156 Q 88,170 130,158 Z"/>
      <text x="76" y="166" class="strip-num">1</text>

      <!-- Horseshoe 2 — middle -->
      <path class="tape-active" d="M 130,124 Q 96,138 50,130 Q 24,118 12,104 Q 12,118 28,134 Q 84,150 134,138 Z"/>
      <text x="80" y="142" class="strip-num">2</text>

      <!-- Horseshoe 3 — most proximal -->
      <path class="tape-active" d="M 134,104 Q 96,118 46,108 Q 22,98 10,82 Q 12,98 26,112 Q 82,130 138,118 Z"/>
      <text x="86" y="122" class="strip-num">3</text>

      <!-- Direction arrow -->
      <path class="direction" d="M 132,160 Q 80,170 28,158" marker-end="url(#dir-arrow)" opacity="0.85"/>
      <text x="138" y="170" class="direction-label">apply</text>

      <text x="2" y="78" class="anatomy" text-anchor="end">proximal</text>
      <text x="2" y="172" class="anatomy" text-anchor="end">distal</text>
    </g>

    <text x="16" y="306" class="caption-body">
      Three horseshoes wrap from posterior anchor, around the heel, to anterior
    </text>
    <text x="16" y="320" class="caption-body">
      anchor. Each new horseshoe is placed one half-strip-width proximal to
    </text>
    <text x="16" y="332" class="caption-body">
      the prior, building a basket-weave pattern over the malleoli.
    </text>
  </g>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       PANEL 4 — FIGURE-OF-EIGHT
       =================================================================== -->
  <g id="panel-4" transform="translate(40, 470)">
    <rect class="panel-bg" x="0" y="0" width="440" height="340" rx="3"/>
    <rect class="panel-rule" x="0" y="0" width="440" height="340" rx="3"/>

    <text x="16" y="24" class="panel-num">PANEL 4 · STEP 4 OF 6</text>
    <text x="16" y="44" class="panel-step">Figure-of-eight</text>
    <text x="120" y="44" class="panel-title">1 wrap · over dorsum and around heel</text>

    <g transform="translate(40, 80)">
      <use href="#foot-anatomy" width="360" height="200"/>

      <!-- Anchors -->
      <rect class="tape" x="18" y="14" width="100" height="14" rx="2"/>
      <rect class="tape" x="20" y="36" width="100" height="14" rx="2"/>
      <rect class="tape" x="156" y="128" width="78" height="14" rx="2" transform="rotate(-12, 195, 135)"/>

      <!-- Stirrups -->
      <path class="tape" d="M 56,18 L 60,24 Q 36,80 28,130 Q 38,148 80,150 Q 102,140 116,98 Q 118,52 96,18 Z" opacity="0.78"/>
      <path class="tape" d="M 66,18 L 70,24 Q 50,84 46,134 Q 58,150 92,148 Q 116,138 130,100 Q 130,54 110,18 Z" opacity="0.75"/>
      <path class="tape" d="M 78,18 L 82,24 Q 70,90 70,138 Q 84,150 108,144 Q 132,130 144,102 Q 144,56 124,18 Z" opacity="0.72"/>

      <!-- Horseshoes -->
      <path class="tape" d="M 124,144 Q 96,156 56,150 Q 30,142 16,128 Q 16,142 32,156 Q 88,170 130,158 Z" opacity="0.78"/>
      <path class="tape" d="M 130,124 Q 96,138 50,130 Q 24,118 12,104 Q 12,118 28,134 Q 84,150 134,138 Z" opacity="0.75"/>
      <path class="tape" d="M 134,104 Q 96,118 46,108 Q 22,98 10,82 Q 12,98 26,112 Q 82,130 138,118 Z" opacity="0.72"/>

      <!-- Figure-of-eight: starts at lateral midfoot, crosses dorsum to medial
           proximal, around posterior heel, back across dorsum, finishes at
           lateral midfoot. -->
      <path class="tape-active" d="M 190,154 Q 132,128 96,110 Q 64,86 50,46 L 70,52 Q 84,90 110,116 Q 148,144 200,166 Z"
            opacity="0.93"/>
      <text x="120" y="100" class="strip-num">1a</text>
      <path class="tape-active" d="M 50,46 Q 14,88 22,140 Q 60,160 116,150 L 96,140 Q 56,144 36,124 Q 32,90 60,58 Z"
            opacity="0.88"/>
      <text x="38" y="110" class="strip-num">1b</text>

      <!-- Direction arrow showing the loop -->
      <path class="direction" d="M 192,156 Q 130,124 96,108 Q 66,84 56,52" marker-end="url(#dir-arrow)" opacity="0.85"/>
      <text x="156" y="118" class="direction-label">across dorsum</text>
      <text x="22" y="46" class="direction-label">around heel</text>
    </g>

    <text x="16" y="306" class="caption-body">
      One continuous strip from lateral midfoot, across the dorsum, around the
    </text>
    <text x="16" y="320" class="caption-body">
      posterior heel, back across the dorsum, finishing at lateral midfoot.
    </text>
    <text x="16" y="332" class="caption-body">
      The crossing point sits over the dorsum; tape lies flat without pleats.
    </text>
  </g>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       PANEL 5 — HEEL LOCKS
       =================================================================== -->
  <g id="panel-5" transform="translate(500, 470)">
    <rect class="panel-bg" x="0" y="0" width="440" height="340" rx="3"/>
    <rect class="panel-rule" x="0" y="0" width="440" height="340" rx="3"/>

    <text x="16" y="24" class="panel-num">PANEL 5 · STEP 5 OF 6</text>
    <text x="16" y="44" class="panel-step">Heel locks</text>
    <text x="120" y="44" class="panel-title">2 wraps · medial then lateral</text>

    <g transform="translate(40, 80)">
      <use href="#foot-anatomy" width="360" height="200"/>

      <!-- Anchors / stirrups / horseshoes / figure-8 (established layers) -->
      <rect class="tape" x="18" y="14" width="100" height="14" rx="2"/>
      <rect class="tape" x="20" y="36" width="100" height="14" rx="2"/>
      <rect class="tape" x="156" y="128" width="78" height="14" rx="2" transform="rotate(-12, 195, 135)"/>
      <path class="tape" d="M 56,18 L 60,24 Q 36,80 28,130 Q 38,148 80,150 Q 102,140 116,98 Q 118,52 96,18 Z" opacity="0.68"/>
      <path class="tape" d="M 66,18 L 70,24 Q 50,84 46,134 Q 58,150 92,148 Q 116,138 130,100 Q 130,54 110,18 Z" opacity="0.65"/>
      <path class="tape" d="M 78,18 L 82,24 Q 70,90 70,138 Q 84,150 108,144 Q 132,130 144,102 Q 144,56 124,18 Z" opacity="0.62"/>
      <path class="tape" d="M 124,144 Q 96,156 56,150 Q 30,142 16,128 Q 16,142 32,156 Q 88,170 130,158 Z" opacity="0.66"/>
      <path class="tape" d="M 130,124 Q 96,138 50,130 Q 24,118 12,104 Q 12,118 28,134 Q 84,150 134,138 Z" opacity="0.62"/>
      <path class="tape" d="M 134,104 Q 96,118 46,108 Q 22,98 10,82 Q 12,98 26,112 Q 82,130 138,118 Z" opacity="0.58"/>
      <path class="tape" d="M 190,154 Q 132,128 96,110 Q 64,86 50,46 L 70,52 Q 84,90 110,116 Q 148,144 200,166 Z" opacity="0.62"/>
      <path class="tape" d="M 50,46 Q 14,88 22,140 Q 60,160 116,150 L 96,140 Q 56,144 36,124 Q 32,90 60,58 Z" opacity="0.62"/>

      <!-- Heel lock medial: from anterior dorsum, angled across medial
           malleolus, around posterior heel, ending at anterior dorsum on the
           lateral side. -->
      <path class="tape-active" d="M 132,82 Q 102,72 70,90 Q 14,108 22,148 Q 64,166 120,154 L 116,144 Q 70,150 36,138 Q 32,118 78,96 Q 110,82 138,92 Z"/>
      <text x="62" y="160" class="strip-num">1 medial</text>

      <!-- Heel lock lateral: mirror of medial, applied second. -->
      <path class="tape-active" d="M 144,72 Q 132,58 110,52 Q 78,32 40,72 Q 8,108 34,156 Q 78,170 130,160 L 124,150 Q 88,156 52,140 Q 36,108 60,80 Q 92,62 124,76 Z"
            opacity="0.85"/>
      <text x="40" y="174" class="strip-num">2 lateral</text>

      <path class="direction" d="M 134,84 Q 102,74 70,92" marker-end="url(#dir-arrow)" opacity="0.85"/>
      <text x="142" y="78" class="direction-label">medial first</text>
    </g>

    <text x="16" y="306" class="caption-body">
      Two angled wraps that cross beneath the calcaneus. Medial heel lock first,
    </text>
    <text x="16" y="320" class="caption-body">
      then lateral. Each crosses the opposite malleolus and locks the
    </text>
    <text x="16" y="332" class="caption-body">
      subtalar joint against the inversion vector that sprains the lateral ankle.
    </text>
  </g>

  <!-- ===================================================================
       PANEL 6 — CLOSURE
       =================================================================== -->
  <g id="panel-6" transform="translate(960, 470)">
    <rect class="panel-bg" x="0" y="0" width="440" height="340" rx="3"/>
    <rect class="panel-rule" x="0" y="0" width="440" height="340" rx="3"/>

    <text x="16" y="24" class="panel-num">PANEL 6 · STEP 6 OF 6</text>
    <text x="16" y="44" class="panel-step">Closure</text>
    <text x="120" y="44" class="panel-title">overlapping strips · all exposed edges covered</text>

    <g transform="translate(40, 80)">
      <use href="#foot-anatomy" width="360" height="200"/>

      <!-- All prior layers rendered uniformly as established tape -->
      <rect class="tape" x="18" y="14" width="100" height="14" rx="2"/>
      <rect class="tape" x="20" y="36" width="100" height="14" rx="2"/>
      <rect class="tape" x="156" y="128" width="78" height="14" rx="2" transform="rotate(-12, 195, 135)"/>
      <path class="tape" d="M 56,18 L 60,24 Q 36,80 28,130 Q 38,148 80,150 Q 102,140 116,98 Q 118,52 96,18 Z" opacity="0.5"/>
      <path class="tape" d="M 66,18 L 70,24 Q 50,84 46,134 Q 58,150 92,148 Q 116,138 130,100 Q 130,54 110,18 Z" opacity="0.5"/>
      <path class="tape" d="M 78,18 L 82,24 Q 70,90 70,138 Q 84,150 108,144 Q 132,130 144,102 Q 144,56 124,18 Z" opacity="0.5"/>
      <path class="tape" d="M 124,144 Q 96,156 56,150 Q 30,142 16,128 Q 16,142 32,156 Q 88,170 130,158 Z" opacity="0.5"/>
```

## `templates/mermaid-clinical-algorithm.mmd`

```mermaid
%% =============================================================================
%% Template: mermaid-clinical-algorithm.mmd
%% Status: Realized starter (no placeholders; ships as-is on a real subject)
%% Subject: Surviving Sepsis Campaign Hour-1 Bundle
%%          (Levy et al., Crit Care Med 2018; Evans et al., Intensive Care Med 2021)
%% Register: Clinical algorithm
%% Signature move: Algorithm-title-as-clinical-question + Hour-1 clock badge
%%                 governs every action node; recommendation-class chip
%%                 (ACC/AHA palette: Class I green, IIa light-green, IIb yellow,
%%                 III red) carried on every substantive node.
%% Pairs with: references/medium-playbooks/clinical-algorithm.md (the playbook).
%%             For the React decision-walker companion, see
%%             templates/react-clinical-algorithm.tsx (HEART pathway subject).
%% =============================================================================
%%
%% CUSTOMIZE — slots to swap when repurposing this template:
%%
%%   1. Subject. Replace the Hour-1 Bundle with the algorithm you are
%%      authoring; rewrite the entry node, the action nodes, and the
%%      terminus nodes. Keep the shape discipline (oval=start/terminus,
%%      diamond=decision, rect=action, parallelogram=data, pentagonal
%%      home-plate=off-page connector).
%%   2. Recommendation classes. The classDef blocks below encode ACC/AHA
%%      Class I/IIa/IIb/III. If your guideline uses GRADE (strong/conditional
%%      with quality-of-evidence dots), rename the classes accordingly and
%%      adjust the color discipline. Keep one system across the whole figure.
%%   3. Time budget. The header note declares the Hour-1 budget. If your
%%      algorithm has a different budget (door-to-needle 60 min, door-to-
%%      balloon 90 min, golden-hour stroke), update the header. If the
%%      algorithm is atemporal, delete the clock-badge node entirely.
%%   4. Off-page connector. The pentagonal "home-plate" syntax is
%%      cont1[/Connector A:\] — Mermaid does not have a native pentagon, so
%%      we use the trapezoidal/asymmetric shape closest to the convention.
%%      Rename the connector when you decompose into sub-algorithms.
%%   5. LoE badges. The action-node text carries [I] [A] / [IIa] [B-NR] etc.
%%      in square brackets. Update per the underlying guideline.
%%   6. Footer citation. The %% comments at the bottom hold the recommendation
%%      source. Update on every revision; never ship a clinical algorithm
%%      with no provenance.
%% =============================================================================

flowchart TB
    %% --------- header & time-zero ---------
    HEADER[/" SEPSIS HOUR-1 BUNDLE — complete all elements within 1 hour of recognition "\]
    style HEADER fill:#1F2937,stroke:#0B1220,color:#F9FAFB,font-weight:600

    %% --------- entry (oval = start) ---------
    START(["t = 0 · Suspected infection<br/>with new organ dysfunction"]):::entry

    %% --------- decision (diamond) ---------
    QSOFA{"qSOFA ≥ 2 OR<br/>SIRS criteria met?"}:::decision

    %% --------- branch terminus: not sepsis (oval = terminus) ---------
    NOTSEPSIS(["Disposition: continue<br/>workup for infection;<br/>reassess if deteriorates<br/><b>[Class I · LoE C-EO]</b>"]):::terminusBenign

    %% --------- core bundle actions (rectangles = imperative actions) ---------
    LACTATE["⏱ 1 hr · Measure serum lactate<br/><b>[Class I · LoE B-NR]</b>"]:::classI
    CULTURES["⏱ 1 hr · Obtain blood cultures<br/>BEFORE antibiotics<br/><b>[Class I · LoE B-NR]</b>"]:::classI
    ABX["⏱ 1 hr · Administer broad-spectrum<br/>IV antibiotics<br/><b>[Class I · LoE B-R]</b>"]:::classI

    %% --------- data input (parallelogram via trapezoid) ---------
    LACDATA[/"Lactate result<br/>(mmol/L)"/]:::data
    BPDATA[/"MAP measurement<br/>(mmHg)"/]:::data

    %% --------- fluid decision (diamond) ---------
    FLUIDQ{"Hypotensive (MAP &lt; 65)<br/>OR lactate ≥ 4 mmol/L?"}:::decision

    %% --------- fluid action (Class I) ---------
    FLUIDS["⏱ 3 hr · Administer 30 mL/kg<br/>IV crystalloid<br/><b>[Class I · LoE B-NR]</b>"]:::classI

    %% --------- reassess (rounded rectangle = sub-process call) ---------
    REASSESS("Reassess hemodynamic status<br/>(dynamic measures preferred over<br/>static CVP/PCWP)<br/><b>[Class IIa · LoE C-LD]</b>"):::classIIa

    %% --------- vasopressor decision (diamond) ---------
    PRESSORQ{"Hypotension persists<br/>during/after fluid<br/>resuscitation?"}:::decision

    %% --------- vasopressor action (Class I) ---------
    PRESSORS["⏱ Apply vasopressors to target<br/>MAP ≥ 65 mmHg<br/>(norepinephrine first-line)<br/><b>[Class I · LoE B-R]</b>"]:::classI

    %% --------- contraindicated action (Class III — example for color demo) ---------
    NOSTARCH["Do NOT use<br/>hydroxyethyl starch (HES)<br/>for fluid resuscitation<br/><b>[Class III · LoE A · HARM]</b>"]:::classIII

    %% --------- off-page connector (pentagonal home-plate; trapezoid approximation) ---------
    CONNA[/"→ Connector A:<br/>Vasopressor Escalation Algorithm<br/>(page 2 of 3)"\]:::connector

    %% --------- terminus: ICU disposition ---------
    ICU(["Disposition: admit to ICU<br/>for ongoing hemodynamic support;<br/>source control within 6–12 hr<br/><b>[Class I · LoE B-NR]</b>"]):::terminusICU

    %% --------- terminus: ward disposition ---------
    WARD(["Disposition: admit to monitored<br/>bed; reassess lactate at 3 hr;<br/>continue antibiotics + source control<br/><b>[Class I · LoE B-R]</b>"]):::terminusWard

    %% =================== EDGES (every conditional edge labeled) ===================
    HEADER -.-> START
    START --> QSOFA
    QSOFA -->|"no — atypical / unclear"| NOTSEPSIS
    QSOFA -->|"yes — sepsis recognized"| LACTATE
    LACTATE --> CULTURES
    CULTURES --> ABX
    ABX --> LACDATA
    ABX --> BPDATA
    LACDATA --> FLUIDQ
    BPDATA --> FLUIDQ
    FLUIDQ -->|"no — stable"| WARD
    FLUIDQ -->|"yes — meets fluid trigger"| FLUIDS
    FLUIDS --> REASSESS
    REASSESS --> PRESSORQ
    PRESSORQ -->|"no — fluid-responsive"| WARD
    PRESSORQ -->|"yes — persistent hypotension"| PRESSORS
    PRESSORS --> CONNA
    CONNA --> ICU
    FLUIDS -.->|"AVOID"| NOSTARCH

    %% =================== STYLES (ACC/AHA recommendation-class palette) ===================
    %% Class I  — green  (Benefit >>> Risk; SHOULD be performed)
    %% Class IIa — light-green / yellow-green (Benefit >> Risk; REASONABLE)
    %% Class IIb — yellow (Benefit ≥ Risk; MAY be CONSIDERED)
    %% Class III — red   (No Benefit OR Harm; should NOT / IS HARMFUL)
    %% Each class chip also carries a non-color secondary channel (the [Class X] text label).
    classDef classI    fill:#D1FAE5,stroke:#047857,stroke-width:2px,color:#064E3B,font-weight:500
    classDef classIIa  fill:#ECFCCB,stroke:#65A30D,stroke-width:2px,color:#365314,font-weight:500
    classDef classIIb  fill:#FEF3C7,stroke:#B45309,stroke-width:2px,color:#78350F,font-weight:500
    classDef classIII  fill:#FEE2E2,stroke:#B91C1C,stroke-width:2.5px,color:#7F1D1D,font-weight:600

    %% Structural shape classes (decisions, data, connectors, termini)
    classDef entry          fill:#E0E7FF,stroke:#3730A3,stroke-width:2px,color:#1E1B4B,font-weight:600
    classDef decision       fill:#FEF9C3,stroke:#A16207,stroke-width:1.75px,color:#422006
    classDef data           fill:#F1F5F9,stroke:#475569,stroke-width:1px,color:#0F172A,font-style:italic
    classDef connector      fill:#FDF4FF,stroke:#86198F,stroke-width:2px,color:#581C87,font-weight:600,stroke-dasharray:6 3
    classDef terminusBenign fill:#F0FDF4,stroke:#15803D,stroke-width:2px,color:#14532D,font-weight:600
    classDef terminusWard   fill:#DCFCE7,stroke:#166534,stroke-width:2.5px,color:#14532D,font-weight:700
    classDef terminusICU    fill:#FECACA,stroke:#991B1B,stroke-width:2.5px,color:#7F1D1D,font-weight:700

%% =============================================================================
%% Recommendation source:
%%   Evans L, Rhodes A, Alhazzani W, et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign:
%%   International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2021.
%%   Intensive Care Med. 2021;47(11):1181-1247. doi:10.1007/s00134-021-06506-y
%%
%%   Levy MM, Evans LE, Rhodes A. The Surviving Sepsis Campaign Bundle:
%%   2018 update. Crit Care Med. 2018;46(6):997-1000.
%%   doi:10.1097/CCM.0000000000003119
%%
%% Class / LoE convention: ACC/AHA 2015 methodology
%%   (Halperin JL et al., Circulation 2016;133:1426-1428).
%%
%% Last reviewed: 2026-05-24.
%% Reviewer: self-attested.
%% Disclosures: none.
%% =============================================================================
```

## `templates/dataviz-plot.html`

```html
<!doctype html>
<!--
  =============================================================================
  Template: dataviz-plot.html / Status: Realized starter
  Subject: Pricing-change impact on weekly active users (WAU)
  Register: Editorial; title-as-finding; baseline rule + shaded window
  Signature move: 1.5 chart-title-as-thesis + 2.1 direct end-label
  Render env: Single-file HTML, ESM import of Observable Plot @0.6.17
  =============================================================================

  CUSTOMIZE — slots to adapt when reusing this scaffold:

    1. Subject + finding. The <h1> states the chart's argument as a complete
       sentence. The .eyebrow names the series and context. The .lede gives
       unit, scope, and any interpretation cues (clipped axis, shaded band,
       baseline rule). Rewrite the four mastheads together.
    2. Data. The `data` array — every point is { date, value }. Make sure the
       date strings parse in your environment; ISO YYYY-MM-DD is safe.
    3. Reference annotations. The `launchDate`, the rectX shaded band, the
       baseline ruleY at 80, and the labels for each. Use sparingly — annotations
       are the most expensive ink in the chart.
    4. Alt prose. The screen-reader-only paragraph below #chart describes the
       chart in words. Write a full description; do not say "see chart".
    5. Figcaption. One sentence interpreting the shaded band + the baseline.
       Earns the visual cues by naming what they mean.
    6. Footer provenance. Real source, sample size, last updated; do not ship
       placeholder tokens of any kind.
    7. Palette accent hue. The --accent token. Single accent; keep neutral
       family separate.
    8. Y-axis clipping. This template uses a non-zero-based y-axis with a
       baseline rule to make the change visible without misleading. If you
       remove the baseline annotation, restore zero-based or you've lied.
-->
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>Pricing change on Feb 9 took WAU from 84k to 127k, then partially retraced</title>
<meta name="description" content="Weekly active users before and after a Feb 9 pricing change; shaded band marks the two-week post-launch window; baseline 80k is pre-launch Q4-2025 mean.">
<style>
  :root {
    color-scheme: light dark;

    --font-sans: "Inter Tight", "Inter", -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif;
    --font-serif: "Fraunces", "Source Serif Pro", Georgia, serif;

    --n-50:  oklch(98% 0.004 240);
    --n-100: oklch(95% 0.008 240);
    --n-200: oklch(90% 0.012 240);
    --n-300: oklch(80% 0.018 240);
    --n-500: oklch(50% 0.025 240);
    --n-700: oklch(28% 0.020 240);
    --n-900: oklch(13% 0.012 240);

    --accent: oklch(45% 0.18 250);
    --accent-soft: oklch(92% 0.04 250);
    --signal: oklch(55% 0.19 25);
    --growth: oklch(55% 0.15 150);

    --s-2: 0.5rem; --s-3: 0.75rem; --s-4: 1rem;
    --s-6: 1.5rem; --s-8: 2rem;
    --r-md: 8px; --r-sm: 4px;
  }

  @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
    :root {
      --n-50:  oklch(13% 0.012 240);
      --n-100: oklch(17% 0.014 240);
      --n-200: oklch(22% 0.016 240);
      --n-300: oklch(30% 0.020 240);
      --n-500: oklch(60% 0.024 240);
      --n-700: oklch(82% 0.016 240);

  *, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }
  body {

  .eyebrow {

<body>

<main>
  <p class="eyebrow">Product analytics · Q1 2026</p>
  <h1>Pricing change on Feb 9 took WAU from 84k to 127k, then partially retraced.</h1>
  <p class="lede">Weekly active users, thousands, snapshotted from internal analytics 2026-04-01. Y-axis is not zero-based; baseline-80 rule shown for reference.</p>

  <figure class="chart-frame">
    <div id="chart" role="img" aria-labelledby="chart-alt"></div>
    <p id="chart-alt" class="sr-only">
      Line chart of weekly active users across 14 weeks from January 1 to April 1, 2026, in thousands.
      The series starts at 64 on January 1, rises gradually to 71 by January 15 and 84 by February 1.
      A vertical dashed line marks the pricing change on February 9; a shaded band covers the two
      weeks following. WAU jumps to 92 on February 9 and peaks at 127 on March 1. The line then
      retraces to 121 on March 15 and 119 on April 1, settling roughly 49 percent above the pre-launch
      baseline of 80 thousand, which is drawn as a horizontal dashed reference line.
    </p>
    <figcaption>
      Figure 1. Shaded band marks the two weeks immediately following the Feb 9 pricing change.
      The dashed horizontal rule at 80k is the pre-launch Q4 2025 mean; current WAU sits roughly
      49% above it.
    </figcaption>
  </figure>

  <footer class="meta">
    Source: internal product analytics. n = 14 weeks. Last updated: 2026-04-20.
  </footer>
</main>

<script type="module">
  import * as Plot from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@observablehq/plot@0.6.17/+esm';

  /* ---------- Data ----------
   * Weekly active users (thousands) before and after a Feb 9 pricing change.
   * Snapshot 2026-04-01 from internal product analytics.
   */
  const data = [
    { date: new Date('2026-01-01'), value: 64 },
    { date: new Date('2026-01-08'), value: 67 },
    { date: new Date('2026-01-15'), value: 71 },
    { date: new Date('2026-01-22'), value: 76 },
    { date: new Date('2026-01-29'), value: 81 },
    { date: new Date('2026-02-05'), value: 84 },
    { date: new Date('2026-02-09'), value: 92 },
    { date: new Date('2026-02-15'), value: 118 },
    { date: new Date('2026-02-22'), value: 124 },
    { date: new Date('2026-03-01'), value: 127 },
    { date: new Date('2026-03-08'), value: 124 },
    { date: new Date('2026-03-15'), value: 121 },
    { date: new Date('2026-03-22'), value: 120 },
    { date: new Date('2026-04-01'), value: 119 },
  ];

  const launchDate = new Date('2026-02-09');
  const bandEnd = new Date('2026-02-23');
  const baseline = 80;

  /* ---------- Compute accent colors from CSS variables ---------- */
  const styles = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
  const accent = styles.getPropertyValue('--accent').trim();
  const accentSoft = styles.getPropertyValue('--accent-soft').trim();
  const n300 = styles.getPropertyValue('--n-300').trim();
  const n500 = styles.getPropertyValue('--n-500').trim();
  const n700 = styles.getPropertyValue('--n-700').trim();

  /* ---------- Build the chart ---------- */
  let rafId = null;
  function renderChart() {
    const node = document.getElementById('chart');
    const last = data[data.length - 1];
    const peak = data.reduce((a, b) => (b.value > a.value ? b : a));
    node.replaceChildren(Plot.plot({
      marginTop: 28,
      marginRight: 72,
      marginBottom: 32,
      marginLeft: 48,
      width: node.clientWidth || 800,
      height: 360,
      style: { background: 'transparent', color: n700, fontSize: 12 },
      y: {
        grid: true,
        label: 'WAU (thousands)',
        labelAnchor: 'top',
        labelArrow: 'none',
        tickFormat: (n) => `${n}k`,
        domain: [60, 140],
      },
      x: {
        label: null,
        tickFormat: '%b %-d',
      },
      marks: [
        // two-week post-launch shaded band
        Plot.rectX([{ x1: launchDate, x2: bandEnd }],
          { x1: 'x1', x2: 'x2', fill: accentSoft, fillOpacity: 0.6 }),

        // baseline reference (pre-launch Q4 2025 mean)
        Plot.ruleY([baseline], { stroke: n300, strokeDasharray: '2,2' }),
        Plot.text([{ x: last.date, y: baseline, text: 'Baseline 80k (Q4 2025 mean)' }],
          { x: 'x', y: 'y', text: 'text', dx: 6, textAnchor: 'start',
            fill: n500, fontSize: 10 }),

        // launch vertical rule
        Plot.ruleX([launchDate], { stroke: accent, strokeDasharray: '3,3' }),
        Plot.text([{ x: launchDate, y: 138, text: 'Pricing change · Feb 9' }],
          { x: 'x', y: 'y', text: 'text', dy: 4, dx: 6, textAnchor: 'start',
            fill: accent, fontWeight: 600, fontSize: 11 }),

        // main series
        Plot.line(data, { x: 'date', y: 'value', stroke: accent, strokeWidth: 2, curve: 'monotone-x' }),
        Plot.dot(data,  { x: 'date', y: 'value', fill: accent, r: 3 }),

        // peak callout
        Plot.text([peak], {
          x: 'date', y: 'value',
          text: () => `Peak ${peak.value}k`,
          dy: -14, textAnchor: 'middle',
          fill: n700, fontWeight: 600, fontSize: 11,
        }),

        // direct end-label (no legend needed for single series)
        Plot.text([last], {
          x: 'date', y: 'value',
          text: (d) => `${d.value}k`,
          dx: 10, textAnchor: 'start',
          fill: accent, fontWeight: 600, fontSize: 12,
        }),
      ],
    }));
  }

  function scheduleRender() {
    if (rafId) cancelAnimationFrame(rafId);
    rafId = requestAnimationFrame(renderChart);
  }

  renderChart();
  window.addEventListener('resize', scheduleRender);
</script>

</body>
</html>
```

```html
<!doctype html>
<!--
  =============================================================================
  Template: educational-explainer.html / Status: Realized starter
  Subject: How a Bloom filter trades space for false positives
  Register: Editorial-technical; Prime → Show → Explain → Invite → Check
  Signature move: 2.5 honest-null shown alongside positive case + 3.4 live count
  Render env: Single-file HTML, no build step, no external runtime dependency
  =============================================================================

  CUSTOMIZE — slots to adapt when reusing this scaffold:

    1. Subject + claim. The <h1>, the .lede, the .takeaway, the .check prompt,
       and every section heading argue one thing. Rewrite them as a set; never
       leave the title generic ("Bloom filters") when you have the specific

    4. Try-it control + simulation. The #bits slider, the runFalsePositives()

    8. Palette accent hue. The --accent token. Keep one neutral family +

<body>
<main id="main">

  <p class="meta">
    <span>8 min read</span>
    <span>One interactive demo</span>
    <span>Updated 2026-05-24</span>
  </p>

  <!-- PRIME -->
  <h1>How a Bloom filter trades space for false positives.</h1>
  <p class="lede">A small bit array plus a few hash functions tells you "definitely not in the set" for nearly nothing — at the cost of occasional "probably in the set" lies.</p>

  <!-- SHOW -->
  <section>
    <h2>What it looks like</h2>
    <p>One 32-bit array. Three hash functions. Insert the word <code>cat</code>: it lights three bits. Insert <code>dog</code>: three more, some possibly the same. After three insertions, a quarter of the array is on.</p>
    <figure class="stage" aria-label="A 32-bit array with bits set by three inserted words.">
      <svg id="stage-svg" viewBox="0 0 640 200" role="img" aria-labelledby="stage-title stage-desc">
        <title id="stage-title">A 32-bit Bloom filter after inserting three words.</title>
        <desc id="stage-desc">A row of 32 numbered cells. Cells that have been set by at least one hash are filled in one of three colors corresponding to the inserting word; each word lights three cells. Some cells are shared between words.</desc>
      </svg>
      <div class="legend" aria-hidden="true">
        <span><span class="swatch" style="background: oklch(55% 0.18 250)"></span>cat</span>
        <span><span class="swatch" style="background: oklch(60% 0.17 30)"></span>dog</span>
        <span><span class="swatch" style="background: oklch(55% 0.15 150)"></span>fox</span>
        <span><span class="swatch" style="background: var(--n-300)"></span>unset</span>
      </div>
      <figcaption>Figure 1. Three words inserted into a 32-bit Bloom filter with three hash functions. Asking <code>contains("bat")</code> probes three positions; if any is unset, the answer is a certain no. If all three are set — which can happen by accident — the answer is "probably yes."</figcaption>
    </figure>
  </section>

  <!-- EXPLAIN -->
  <section>
    <h2>What's happening</h2>
    <p>A Bloom filter is an array of <code>m</code> bits, all initially zero, paired with <code>k</code> independent hash functions. To <strong>insert</strong> an item, hash it with each of the <code>k</code> functions to get <code>k</code> positions in <code>[0, m)</code>; set each of those bits to one. To <strong>query</strong> whether an item is present, hash it with the same <code>k</code> functions and read the same <code>k</code> bits. If any is zero, the item was never inserted — guaranteed. If all are one, the item was probably inserted — but maybe not.</p>
    <p>The "maybe not" is the <strong>false positive</strong>. Other inserts can collectively light up exactly the bits your query needed, even though the queried item was never added. False positives become more likely as the array fills. The rate is approximately <code>(1 − e<sup>−kn/m</sup>)<sup>k</sup></code>, where <code>n</code> is the number of inserted items. There is no false negative: a bit you set stays set, so any inserted item always reports present. The asymmetry — yes is uncertain, no is certain — is the whole shape of the data structure.</p>
  </section>

  <!-- INVITE -->
  <div class="try-it">
    <h3>Try it</h3>
    <p>The filter below holds a fixed set of <strong>30 random items</strong> and tests <strong>1,000 random non-member queries</strong>. The slider changes only the bit-array size. <code>k</code> is held at 3 and the random seed is fixed, so two positions on the slider compare directly.</p>

    <div class="control">
      <label for="bits">
        Bit-array size
        <output for="bits" id="bits-out">32</output>
      </label>
      <input id="bits" type="range" min="8" max="128" step="1" value="32" aria-describedby="bits-hint">
      <p id="bits-hint" class="hint">Doubling the bits cuts the per-bit load. The false-positive rate falls fast at first, then much more slowly.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="readout" role="status" aria-live="polite">
      <div class="cell">
        <p class="label">Bits set</p>
        <p class="value" id="bits-set">—</p>
      </div>
      <div class="cell warn">
        <p class="label">False positives</p>
        <p class="value" id="fp-count">—</p>
      </div>
      <div class="cell">
        <p class="label">Rate</p>
        <p class="value" id="fp-rate">—</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <p class="predict"><strong>Predict before you drag.</strong> What happens at 16 bits? At 128? Why does the curve flatten as the array grows?</p>
  </div>

  <!-- TAKEAWAY -->
  <p class="takeaway">A Bloom filter is a contract: you trade exactness for size, and the rate of that trade is the only knob.</p>

  <!-- CHECK -->
  <section>
    <h2>Check yourself</h2>
    <p>If you doubled the bit array — same items, same hash count — would the false-positive rate halve? Why or why not?</p>
    <details>
      <summary>Show the answer</summary>
      <div class="disclosure">
        <p>No, not halve — better than halve when the array is heavily loaded, worse than halve when it is lightly loaded. The false-positive rate is approximately <code>(1 − e<sup>−kn/m</sup>)<sup>k</sup></code>. Doubling <code>m</code> drops <code>kn/m</code> by half, which shifts <code>e<sup>−kn/m</sup></code> in a non-linear way. The relationship is exponential, not proportional, which is exactly why the curve flattens.</p>
      </div>
    </details>
  </section>

  <!-- GOING DEEPER -->
  <section>
    <h2>Going deeper</h2>

    <details>
      <summary>The optimal <code>k</code> — and why three is often close</summary>
      <div class="disclosure">
        <p>For a fixed bit array of size <code>m</code> and a known item count <code>n</code>, the false-positive rate <code>(1 − e<sup>−kn/m</sup>)<sup>k</sup></code> is minimised at <code>k = (m/n) ln(2) ≈ 0.693 (m/n)</code>. Each additional hash function reduces the chance any single probe hits a set bit (good), but also lights more bits per insert (bad); the minimum balances the two.</p>
        <p>For a load of ten bits per item, optimal <code>k</code> is about 7. For three bits per item, optimal <code>k</code> is 2. Real systems pick something near the optimum — Google's <em>Bigtable</em> uses 4, the Chrome safe-browsing list once used 4, Bitcoin's SPV clients use a tunable <code>k</code>. Three is a common starting point because it captures most of the benefit without exotic hash counts.</p>
      </div>
    </details>

    <details>
      <summary>Why you can't delete</summary>
      <div class="disclosure">
        <p>To delete an item, you would need to flip its three bits back to zero. But each of those bits may also be supporting another inserted item. Flipping them would lose those items — silently — and re-introduce false negatives, which destroy the structure's only guarantee.</p>
        <p>The <strong>counting Bloom filter</strong> sidesteps this by storing a small counter (typically 4 bits) at each position instead of a single bit. Insert increments, delete decrements. The price is 4× the space and counter overflow at extreme loads. Cuckoo filters take a different route: they store fingerprints in a cuckoo hash table, supporting deletion and matching Bloom on false-positive rate at moderate loads, often at slightly better space efficiency.</p>
      </div>
    </details>

    <details>
      <summary>Related reading</summary>
      <div class="disclosure">
        <ul>
          <li>Bloom, B. H. (1970). <em>Space/Time Trade-offs in Hash Coding with Allowable Errors.</em> Communications of the ACM 13(7). The original paper; six pages, still the best introduction.</li>
          <li>Fan, B. et al. (2014). <em>Cuckoo Filter: Practically Better Than Bloom.</em> CoNEXT '14. The deletion-supporting alternative.</li>
          <li>Mitzenmacher, M. &amp; Upfal, E. (2017). <em>Probability and Computing</em>, ch. 5. The clean derivation of the false-positive bound.</li>
          <li>Broder, A. &amp; Mitzenmacher, M. (2003). <em>Network Applications of Bloom Filters: A Survey.</em> A tour of where the structure earns its keep.</li>
        </ul>
      </div>
    </details>
  </section>

  <footer>
    <p>False-positive simulation: 1,000 random 6-byte query strings against a fixed set of 30, with <code>k = 3</code> hash functions and a Mulberry32 PRNG seeded at 0xC0FFEE. Last updated 2026-05-24.</p>
  </footer>

</main>

<script type="module">
  // ===== Deterministic PRNG (Mulberry32) =====
  function mulberry32(seed) {
    let s = seed >>> 0;
    return function () {
      s = (s + 0x6D2B79F5) >>> 0;
      let t = s;
      t = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), t | 1);
      t ^= t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), t | 61);
      return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
    };
  }

  // ===== Hash =====
  // FNV-1a, seeded so we get k independent-ish hashes by varying seed.
  function fnv1a(str, seed) {
    let h = (2166136261 ^ seed) >>> 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
      h ^= str.charCodeAt(i);
      h = Math.imul(h, 16777619) >>> 0;
    }
    return h >>> 0;
  }
  function hashes(str, k, m) {
    const out = new Array(k);
    for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) out[i] = fnv1a(str, 0x9E3779B1 + i * 0x85EBCA6B) % m;
    return out;
  }

  // ===== Fixed corpus and queries (seeded) =====
  const ALPHA = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz';
  function randomString(rng, n) {
    let s = '';
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) s += ALPHA[(rng() * 26) | 0];
    return s;
  }
  const corpusRng = mulberry32(0xC0FFEE);
  const CORPUS = new Set();
  while (CORPUS.size < 30) CORPUS.add(randomString(corpusRng, 6));
  const CORPUS_LIST = [...CORPUS];

  const queryRng = mulberry32(0xBADCAFE);
  const QUERIES = [];
  while (QUERIES.length < 1000) {
    const q = randomString(queryRng, 6);
    if (!CORPUS.has(q)) QUERIES.push(q);
  }

  const K = 3;

  function simulate(m) {
    const bits = new Uint8Array(m);
    for (const w of CORPUS_LIST) {
      for (const h of hashes(w, K, m)) bits[h] = 1;
    }
    let set = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < m; i++) if (bits[i]) set++;

    let fp = 0;
    for (const q of QUERIES) {
      const hs = hashes(q, K, m);
      let all = true;
      for (let i = 0; i < K; i++) if (!bits[hs[i]]) { all = false; break; }
      if (all) fp++;
    }
    return { bits, set, fp, rate: fp / QUERIES.length };
  }

  // ===== Stage SVG: render 3 inserts (cat, dog, fox) into m=32 =====
  function renderStage() {
    const svg = document.getElementById('stage-svg');
    const m = 32, cols = 16, rows = 2;
    const W = 640, H = 200;
    const PAD = 24, GAP = 6;
    const cellW = (W - 2 * PAD - GAP * (cols - 1)) / cols;
    const cellH = 34;
    const yTop = 50;

    const words = [
      { w: 'cat', color: 'oklch(55% 0.18 250)' },
      { w: 'dog', color: 'oklch(60% 0.17 30)'  },
      { w: 'fox', color: 'oklch(55% 0.15 150)' },
    ];

    // Determine which color hits each cell (first hitter wins, layered marks below)
    const owners = new Array(m).fill(null);
    const marks = [];
    for (const { w, color } of words) {
      for (const h of hashes(w, K, m)) {
        marks.push({ idx: h, color });
        if (owners[h] === null) owners[h] = color;
      }
    }

    let out = '';
    // Column indices for readability
    for (let i = 0; i < m; i++) {
      const r = (i / cols) | 0;
      const c = i % cols;
      const x = PAD + c * (cellW + GAP);
      const y = yTop + r * (cellH + 24);
      const fill = owners[i] ?? 'var(--n-200)';
      out += `<rect x="${x}" y="${y}" width="${cellW}" height="${cellH}" rx="3" fill="${fill}" stroke="var(--n-300)" stroke-width="1"/>`;
      out += `<text x="${x + cellW / 2}" y="${y + cellH + 14}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="var(--n-500)" font-family="${'var(--font-mono)'}">${i}</text>`;
    }

    // Inserted-word tags
    const tagY = 22;
    words.forEach(({ w, color }, i) => {
      const x = PAD + i * 84;
      out += `<rect x="${x}" y="${tagY - 12}" width="64" height="20" rx="10" fill="${color}"/>`;
      out += `<text x="${x + 32}" y="${tagY + 2}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="white" font-family="${'var(--font-sans)'}">insert "${w}"</text>`;
    });

    svg.innerHTML = `
      <title id="stage-title">A 32-bit Bloom filter after inserting three words.</title>
      <desc id="stage-desc">A row of 32 numbered cells. Cells that have been set by at least one hash are filled in one of three colors corresponding to the inserting word; each word lights three cells. Some cells are shared between words.</desc>
      ${out}
    `;
  }

  // ===== Wire slider with debounce on input =====
  const bitsEl = document.getElementById('bits');
  const bitsOut = document.getElementById('bits-out');
  const bitsSetEl = document.getElementById('bits-set');
  const fpCountEl = document.getElementById('fp-count');
  const fpRateEl = document.getElementById('fp-rate');

  let pending = null;
  function update() {
    const m = +bitsEl.value;
    bitsOut.textContent = m;
    const { set, fp, rate } = simulate(m);
    bitsSetEl.textContent = `${set}/${m}`;
    fpCountEl.textContent = String(fp);
    fpRateEl.textContent = `${(rate * 100).toFixed(1)}%`;
  }
  bitsEl.addEventListener('input', () => {
    bitsOut.textContent = bitsEl.value;
    if (pending) clearTimeout(pending);
    pending = setTimeout(update, 80);
  });
  bitsEl.addEventListener('change', update);

  renderStage();
  update();
</script>

</body>
</html>
```
